News.title: Burnham says UK net migration now under 'sufficient' control
News.content:
The ONS said net migration had "fallen to levels not typically seen since the 1990s".

The biggest factors in Thursday's record low were falls in the arrivals of people coming from outside Europe in three major categories of migration: The number of people coming to the UK to work fell by 45,000, asylum claims fell by 19,000 and the total number of students fell by 33,000.

A fall had been expected because of the tightening of visas rules that began under the previous Conservative government which was then continued by Labour from July 2024.

Shadow home secretary Chris Philp argued the Conservatives should receive credit for the decrease in net migration.

He added: "We now need to go even further with an annual legally binding inward migration cap, set by Parliament, at far lower levels.

"British and European people are leaving in their droves because of Labour's high taxes whilst non-EU immigration remains far too high."

Liberal Democrat asylum and immigration spokesman Paul Kohler said Britain faces "serious demographic and economic challenges, and urgently needs a proper immigration plan to support our economy and public services".

Reform UK leader Nigel Farage welcomed the drop in numbers, but said he was concerned about "a lot of high skilled big tax paying people" leaving the UK and being replaced by people "who are paying far less in tax".

Meanwhile, his party's Treasury spokesman Robert Jenrick said the fall "came about solely because I went to see Rishi Sunak" in 2023 whilst an immigration minister in the Conservative former prime minister's government.

Jenrick, who defected to Reform earlier this year, told the BBC: "I threatened to resign unless he made a series of changes. He did".

"And as a result of those changes to the immigration system, we've got where we are today".

But he added that the changes "didn't go as far as I wanted to," adding this had been behind his resignation from the Tory government a few days later.

A Green Party spokesperson said: "Creating a harsh environment for migrants and asylum seekers is not a measure of success."

Additional reporting by Thomas Mason

News.title: Tommy Robinson charged with failing to give phone Pin code to police
News.content:
Far-right activist Tommy Robinson has been charged with failing to provide his phone's pin code to police at Heathrow Airport.

The alleged incident happened when Robinson, whose real name is Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, was detained after returning to the UK from Russia via Turkey on 13 June this year.

The 43-year-old is due to appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on 14 December, the Metropolitan Police said.

Posting on X after being charged, Robinson, describing himself as a journalist, said he "refused the Pin because it held private messages from grooming gang survivors".

He described the charge as "pure state persecution".

Robinson, from Bedfordshire, was detained under the Counter-Terrorism and Border Security Act 2019 in June and has been charged under the same act.

Prior to his arrival in the UK Robinson posted a video on X showing him meeting Elon Musk's father in Moscow.

Robinson is currently awaiting sentencing after being convicted of harassing two Daily Mail journalists.

A jury at Southwark Crown Court found him guilty of two counts of harassment causing fear of violence.

The case concerned Robinson's response to Daily Mail and Mail Online articles from August 2024, showing him on holiday in Cyprus while riots took place in England following the Southport murders.

Robinson was granted bail ahead of his sentencing, scheduled for 16 December.

Robinson had denied the charges, saying he had "panicked" and had been "scared" when the Daily Mail published a story accusing him of "stoking race riots from his sunbed".

News.title: Rodrigo Duterte goes on trial: What is the International Criminal Court?
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Former Philippine leader Rodrigo Duterte goes on trial on Monday for ​alleged crimes against humanity over his war on drugs, during which thousands of people were killed.

It is one of the highest-profile cases to come before the court in its more than two decades of existence, and the biggest since US president Donald Trump's administration imposed sanctions that could imperil the court's ability to function. Here ⁠are a few facts about the International Criminal Court.

open image in gallery ( Reuters )

When was the ICC set up and why?

The court was established in 2002 to prosecute individuals for war crimes, crimes against humanity, genocide and the crime of aggression when member states are unwilling or unable to do so themselves.

It can prosecute crimes committed on the territory of its 125 member states, or by their citizens elsewhere. Member states include all 27 EU countries, other rich democracies and many developing nations, but not the US, China, Russia or India.

The State of Palestine is a member despite not being a full member of the United Nations; Israel is not. In Duterte's case, the court says it has jurisdiction as the Philippines ⁠was a member until he withdrew partway through his term.

Who has been prosecuted by the court?

There have been 34 ​cases ⁠before the court, some with more than one defendant, ‌leading to 15 convictions, including 10 for the core offences of crimes against humanity and war crimes. All 10 were African militia leaders, from the Democratic Republic of Congo, Mali, Sudan, Central African Republic and Uganda.

ICC judges have issued 68 arrest warrants, with 34 suspects now at large. Duterte is only the second ‌former national leader to appear before the court for crimes allegedly committed while in power, after Laurent Gbagbo of Ivory Coast, who was acquitted in 2019.

Four serving national leaders face ICC arrest warrants: Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Russia's President Vladimir Putin, Afghanistan's Taliban leader Hibatullah Akhundzada and Myanmar military leader Min Aung Hlaing. Kenyan President William Ruto and his predecessor Uhuru Kenyatta both appeared at the court over allegations dating to before they took office; in both cases the charges were dropped.

Among former leaders who have faced arrest warrants are Sudan's Omar el-Bashir and Libya's late Muammar Gaddafi.

open image in gallery ( AFP/Getty )

Why does the US oppose the court and what is the impact?

The United States never joined the court and the Trump administration is strongly opposed to it, casting it as a political institution and a threat to US service members.

Trump imposed sanctions on some court officials during his first term, and this year imposed sanctions on the court itself, which Washington says are intended either to force major changes or shut the court down for good. Washington has been particularly angered by the court's arrest warrant for Netanyahu and its inclusion of ‌the actions of US troops in a wider investigation ⁠into Afghanistan. ICC judges closed that part of the case two weeks ago.

At the UN General Assembly in `September, Trump called the ICC a "rogue institution" and "an evil group of people", and urged its members to resign. The sanctions, which could exclude the court from the ‌global financial system, have yet to ​fully take effect. Court officials say they have prepared to keep ‌operating with measures such as replacing software on computers ​with open-source alternatives.

The court has rejected US criticism and called the sanctions an attack on the principle of international justice.

News.title: Ukraine says North ​Korea temporarily halted missile shipments to Russia following ‌diplomatic tensions
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Ukraine's military intelligence agency said on Thursday that North ​Korea has temporarily halted some military cooperation with Russia, including deliveries of KN-23 ballistic missiles, following ‌diplomatic tensions between the allies.

Ukraine's GUR military intelligence agency said North Korean foreign minister Choe Son Hui announced the temporary suspension of cooperation last month, in response to an assertion by one of Russia's deputy foreign ministers that the Kremlin would help to de-escalate tensions between ​Seoul and Pyongyang.

open image in gallery Russia's President Vladimir Putin (R) and North Korea's leader Kim Jong Un (C) leave after their meeting in Beijing on September 3, 2025 ( AFP/Getty )

North Korea has supplied Russia with weapons since 2023, according to a Reuters investigation, and with troops ​since 2024, including soldiers who fought Ukrainian forces after their incursion into Russia's Kursk region.

⁠Experts say the military support is a rare source of hard currency for North Korea, which is heavily targeted ​by international sanctions.

According to GUR, Ms Choe demanded that Russia clarify its policy towards South Korea and announced a temporary pause in ​military cooperation, including Russian military flights over North Korean territory and shipments of artillery shells and KN-23 ballistic missiles to Russia.

Reuters was unable to verify independently the content of the report.

GUR did not immediately respond to questions about where the statements attributed to Ms Choe and ​Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Andrey Rudenko were made.

open image in gallery ( AFP/Getty )

Russia's Defence Ministry and North Korea's embassies in Russia, London and New York ​did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

In statements last month, Rudenko – who oversees Asian relations — said Moscow had received signals from ‌Seoul that ⁠it wanted to normalize ties with Russia once the Ukraine war was over and the two sides were discussing a resumption of direct flights.

South Korea's Unification Ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Reuters was unable to confirm any public statements by Rudenko saying Russia would work to de-escalate tensions on the Korean peninsula, nor any public remarks ​by Ms Choe on the suspension ​of military cooperation.

The video player is currently playing an ad. You can skip the ad in 5 sec with a mouse or keyboard

In its ⁠report, GUR also said Pyongyang was holding off on a Russian request to expand North Korea's military presence in Russia from about 8,500 troops to 50,000.

open image in gallery ( AFP/Getty )

According to GUR's report, units ​of the 11th Corps of the North Korean army continue to serve in Russia's Kursk ​region. Also, ⁠since mid-summer, a combined missile unit of the North Korean army has been deployed in the Voronezh region, which the Russians are using to strike at Ukraine.

As recently as November 7, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said that Russia fired KN-23 missiles at ⁠a Ukrainian ​energy facility.

Diplomatic contacts have continued between Russia and North Korea in recent ​weeks. Last week, Russian President Vladimir Putin received Jo Yong Won, one of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un's closest aides, at the Kremlin, with ​both men reportedly praising bilateral cooperation.

News.title: What to know about North Korean move to shut down Swiss diplomatic office
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

In shutting down a month-old Swiss diplomatic office in Pyongyang and expelling its head, North Korea has signaled it will set its own terms as it pursues a more assertive foreign policy. But experts say the move could potentially risk the loss of many European nations as alternative diplomatic partners.

The Swiss drew the anger of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un after they imposed sanctions on a youth camp over its alleged role in the transfer of children from Russian-occupied areas of Ukraine.

Just a few days earlier, in a more upbeat diplomatic moment, Kim received credentials from 10 newly appointed ambassadors, including envoys from ally Russia and longtime diplomatic partner Sweden, in the first such event of his 15-year rule.

Kim used the meeting with ambassadors to defend his nuclear arms buildup and call for the world to respect North Korea’s sovereignty, a standard Pyongyang later accused Switzerland of failing to meet by sanctioning the camp.

Here's a look at the closure of the Swiss office in Pyongyang and what it says about North Korea’s foreign policy.

Feud stems from sanctions on North Korean youth camp

North Korea’s Foreign Ministry on Wednesday summoned Sylvain Astier, head of the Swiss diplomatic office that opened in Pyongyang last month, declared him persona non grata and handed him a notice demanding the office’s closure and his departure from the country within 48 hours.

In a statement provided to The Associated Press on Thursday, Switzerland’s Federal Department of Foreign Affairs said it regrets the North Korean decision and was arranging for Astier to return to the Swiss embassy in Beijing. It said diplomatic relations will be maintained through the Swiss embassy in Beijing and the North Korean embassy in Bern and that Switzerland will continue to pursue dialogue through these channels.

Kim Jong Un’s powerful sister, Kim Yo Jong, earlier condemned Switzerland for imposing sanctions on the Songdowon International Children’s Camp in the North’s eastern coastal city of Wonsan. She called the Swiss steps an “open hostile act” that violated the North’s sovereignty, but didn’t directly address Western accusations that some Ukrainian children abducted by Russian forces were sent there to be reeducated with pro-Russian propaganda.

North Korea is one of Russia’s allies and has sent thousands of troops to fight in Russian President Vladimir Putin’s invasion of Ukraine.

Switzerland earlier this month added the Songdowon camp to its sanctions over Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. The United Kingdom in May and the European Union in September imposed similar sanctions on the camp, freezing its assets and banning financial transactions with it. The measures were seen as largely symbolic, given North Korea’s limited financial ties with Europe.

North Korea said in August it downgraded the level of diplomatic relations with the U.K. to that of chargé d’affaires in response to its sanctioning of the Songdowon camp.

North Korea may want to send a warning to other Western nations

Switzerland, which established diplomatic relations with North Korea in 1974, has been one of the few Western countries to maintain talks with Pyongyang. Switzerland previously operated a humanitarian-focused cooperation office in Pyongyang, which closed when North Korea sealed its borders during the COVID-19 pandemic. It was among the few countries allowed to open a new diplomatic office after North Korea reopened.

Kim Jong Un and his sister spent several of their teenage years at Swiss schools in the 1990s, and that may have deepened the sense of betrayal when Switzerland sanctioned the Songdowon camp, said Koh Yu-hwan, former president of South Korea’s Institute of National Unification.

But more importantly, North Korea is sending a broader warning that it could cut off diplomatic access to any country that expands sanctions or pursues policies it considers hostile, effectively putting pressure on the North's remaining Western contacts like Sweden, Koh said.

While Russia and China have blocked recent efforts to tighten U.N. sanctions over North Korea’s nuclear and missile programs, the United States and its European and Asian allies have imposed their own sanctions over illicit activities Pyongyang uses to fund its weapons programs, including information-technology worker fraud and cryptocurrency theft.

Kim Jong Un's diplomatic clout on the global stage has been bolstered in recent years as he's aligned with Russia and has taken steps to strengthen cooperation with China, North Korea's economic lifeline.

Leif-Eric Easley, a professor at Seoul’s Ewha University, said North Korea is benefiting enough from its ties with Moscow that it’s willing to make an example of Switzerland.

“By ordering the Swiss office closed just weeks after it opened, the Kim regime wants to show other states it intends to reengage only from a position of strength and on its own terms,” he said.

Closure of Swiss office removes rare Western contact point with Pyongyang

However, the strategy carries some risk, warned Moon Seong Mook, an analyst at the Seoul-based Korea Research Institute for National Strategy.

“Kim Jong Un may win Russia’s favor, but I think this could further deepen North Korea’s isolation from the international community,” he said.

Park Won Gon, a professor at Ewha University, said the North’s move could have long-term consequences, risking the loss of Europe as an alternative partner while further increasing its dependence on China. About 98% of North Korea’s external trade was with China in 2025.

“For European countries, this move will only reinforce the perception that North Korea cannot be trusted,” Park said.

Kim's advancing nuclear arsenal and deepened cooperation with Russia have bolstered his international standing, and he has steadfastly insisted that he will not engage in talks with the United States unless Washington drops its demand for denuclearization.

As Pyongyang increasingly believes it has the leverage to deal directly with Washington, rather than through intermediaries, European countries such as Switzerland or Asian U.S. allies such as South Korea — which Kim in recent years declared as his most hostile enemy — have likely significantly less value to the North.

“They think they no longer need to make compromises with individual countries ... as they portray their status as a nuclear-armed state on an equal footing with the United States," Koh said.

News.title: Asian shares mostly rise ahead of Wall Street's reopening after the Thanksgiving holiday
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Asian shares were mostly higher in early Friday trading, following a market holiday on Wall Street for Thanksgiving.

Japan's benchmark Nikkei 225 added 0.7% to 57,919.30 in morning trading. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 rose 0.4% to 8,800.50. South Korea's Kospi surged 2.2% to 4,812.65. Hong Kong's Hang Seng edged up 0.4% to 22,310.11, while the Shanghai Composite lost 0.1% to 3,473.40.

Buying of stocks tied to artificial intelligence has been pushing benchmarks higher, despite some profit-taking that has kept those gains in check.

In Japan, Tokyo Electron and Advantest Corp. stocks dropped in morning trading but quickly recovered the declines, underlining the continuing appeal of issues in computer chips and AI.

Investors are also closely watching for the possible damage to the region from U.S. tariff hikes planned on China, Japan, the European Union and other trading partners.

U.S. markets will reopen later Friday for a holiday-shortened session.

In energy trading, oil prices have been volatile lately because of uncertainty over tensions in the Middle East. Benchmark U.S. crude rose 2.09% to $85.43 a barrel. Brent crude, the international standard, slipped 0.29% to $96.29 a barrel.

In currency trading, the U.S. dollar inched up to 159.25 Japanese yen from 159.23 yen. The euro cost $1.0967, down from $1.0975.

News.title: This £100 coffee machine was my favourite for 10 years – and now it’s just £45
News.content:
One of the simplest-to-use coffee machines on the market, the Lavazza pod machine works by inserting the pod and pressing the only button. The strength of your coffee will depend on how long you let the water run – it will stop at a ‘long’ measure, two of which is perfect for my morning brew.

But don’t be deceived by its simplicity: I love how consistently my coffee comes out every time. My favourite part is the smooth crema formed on top. As someone who drinks my coffee black, I use the passionale pods, which are intense enough for water dilution while keeping the rich, deep flavour. I would honestly forego a fancy coffee in a cafe because it wouldn’t match my Lavazza. There is a version with a milk frother that I can also vouch for (was £169, now £84: Amazon.co.uk).

I was gifted my machine by my mum because she loved hers so much too and I now recommend it to everyone else because it’s so cheap, but performs every single time.

Upkeep is simple too: just dump the used pods, keep the tank topped up with filtered water and add the odd descaling treatment. Although truth be told, I think I did this once in all the years I had it.

It’s perfect for small spaces because of its diminutive and slender size. It won’t cramp your countertop (and should have pride of place anyway). The EVO is the eco-conscious version of the a modo mio, making use of recycled materials and a shorter shut-off timer to ensure less wasted energy.

Take advantage of the over 50 per cent saving at Amazon right now.

News.title: I’ve spent 10 years covering Black Friday – here are my top tips to shop smart
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

With countless retailers and brands vying for your attention (and cash) now that Black Friday has arrived, it can be easy to have your head turned by the promise of a hefty discount. However, there are a few things to keep in mind before you dash to the checkout, as not all offers are as good as they seem.

In the decade I’ve spent covering Black Friday, I’ve seen enough sales to know that a big discount doesn’t always mean it’s worth parting with your money. A product might be advertised as “half price” even if it’s often sold for less than the full RRP. Meanwhile, offer countdowns can make a fairly ordinary saving feel like a limited-time opportunity you can’t afford to miss. Knowing what to look out for can help you spend your money wisely and avoid the disappointment of a purchase that doesn’t live up to expectations.

With Christmas on the horizon, Adobe’s digital analytics division predicts Brits will spend a record £28.52bn online across November and December. But before you start filling your basket, scroll on for my list of Black Friday dos and don’ts, to help you work out what’s worth buying and what isn’t.



1. Black Friday sales start earlier than you think

It wasn’t that long ago that Black Friday was a single day of chaotic in-store shopping. The good old days when we’d all queue up outside the local Tesco superstore to bag a cheap telly for one day and one day only. Black Friday later morphed into a four-day shopping extravaganza, culminating in Cyber Monday, before retailers shrugged their shoulders and decided to make Black Friday a month-long event.

For many brands and retailers, Black Friday now lasts all of November. Argos, Currys, John Lewis and others even kicked off their sales at the end of October this year. While that does mean you have longer to shop, it also makes the whole thing a whole lot more confusing.



2. Make a wish list and set a budget

With Black Friday plastered right across shopfronts, our TVs and our phones, it’s easy to get overwhelmed, feel like you’re missing out and subsequently end up buying something you never even needed (or really wanted) in the first place. Before you start shopping, the biggest thing you can do is make a wish list.

Ideally, you’ll have kept a running wish list throughout the year, adding things as and when you think of them, instead of waiting until October or November. But don’t worry if you haven’t been doing that.

Sit down now, grab a cup of tea and write down everything you need and want. Perhaps your vacuum cleaner is on its last legs and urgently needs to be replaced, but you’ve also had your eye on some new AirPods. The vacuum goes in the ‘need’ pile and the AirPods in the ‘want’ pile.

Assign a budget to each pile so you don’t overspend, then jot down how much each product currently costs, as well as the retailer and date. That way, when the actual Black Friday day itself eventually rolls around, you’ll have something to compare prices to. This is even good in the lead-up to the sale, giving you something to compare to as the sale gets closer.

And if you can get the kids and grandkids to figure out what they want for Christmas in advance, even better.

3. Don’t be fooled by big discounts – check the price history

It’s Black Friday and the air fryer you’ve just stumbled upon has a massive 50 per cent discount, taking it down to £80. Obviously, you’re going to pop it into your basket – it’s half price.

Except, it’s been selling for £80 for most of the year. One of the oldest tricks in the book is to advertise a massive discount against a product’s recommended retail price (RRP), even though it hasn’t actually sold for that amount in months. Just because something is reduced for Black Friday doesn’t mean it wasn’t cheaper in July, September or even a few weeks ago.

That’s why I always take those big red percentage discounts with a pinch of salt. The best way to check you’re actually getting a bargain is by using price comparison sites – Keepa and CamelCamelCamel are great for checking historical prices for products sold on Amazon. PriceSpy and PriceRunner are great for checking historical prices at other retailers, including Currys, John Lewis and Argos. You can look back over weeks, months and even years and set price alerts.

I recommend looking at a product’s price history over at least six months, ideally a year. If you spot that it’s always hovered around the price it’s been discounted to, then you’ll know it’s really not that big of a deal. Or you might find that it’s the lowest price it’s ever been and want to buy it immediately.

This will hopefully be cracked down on in the future, but not until next year. Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced plans in August to tackle misleading discounts. The government says it wants to ban fake ‘was’ prices, invented discounts and misleading RRPs. That should make it easier for regulators to take action against dodgy retailers and stop them from employing these tricks.

Either way, your friendly neighbourhood consumer experts at The Independent will be hunting down the best Black Friday deals and highlighting when a product is really at its lowest-ever price, so you don’t have to do any arduous research yourself.

4. Shop around before buying

Some shoppers are just wedded to certain retailers and brands. Maybe it’s a sense of loyalty, maybe it’s their reputation, or maybe it’s because of… well, your Amazon Prime account. But it’s always worth shopping around before buying. It’s Black Friday after all, and retailers are all discounting the exact same products, often at wildly different prices.

Don’t assume that because Amazon has taken a massive £100 off a dehumidifier, you don’t need to look elsewhere. Currys, John Lewis or Argos might have taken £120 off the very same dehumidifier. Do a quick Google search for the product and see what other retailers are charging. It’s only sensible.

If multiple retailers sell something for the exact same price, look to see if there’s any benefit in going with one retailer over the other. Maybe you get free next-day delivery, maybe you get a longer warranty, maybe one charges for installation while the other offers it for free. Factor that into the price.

5. Check if retailers price match

If you’re dead set on buying from a certain retailer, check to see if they can price match from a cheaper retailer. Maybe you trust John Lewis more than Amazon, or you have an Argos or a Currys round the corner and want to pick it up that very same day because you’re impatient (I get it).

Thankfully, lots of retailers this year are price matching, including Currys, John Lewis and AO. Currys, for example, is matching prices from other UK retailers, including discounts applied using promotional codes. You can even request a price match up to seven days after buying a product.

But just watch out – terms and conditions can differ from retailer to retailer. Some retailers won’t price-match Amazon, for example, especially if it’s sold by a third-party seller. AO requires the competing product to be exactly the same product (model number and all) and available to buy from a UK retailer.

6. Pay attention to Black Friday price guarantees

The worst thing about shopping Black Friday sales is the dread you feel when you buy something for it to only fall in price the following day. Or maybe you don’t know whether to buy now or wait for Black Friday itself. Thankfully, some retailers have implemented Black Friday price guarantees this year.

A Black Friday price guarantee ensures that if a product you've bought drops further in price during a specified period, you'll get the difference back. Argos, for example, has a Black Friday price guarantee on some of its products, with the retailer promising to give you a voucher for the difference if the price drops further before Christmas. Very has a similar scheme, with it saying it’ll refund the difference if a product you've bought drops further in price before 4 December 2026.

Again, there’s a catch. Argos’s scheme only applies to certain products with a “price guarantee” badge, and Very says you have to contact customer service to get the refund, suggesting you’ll need to make a claim. There are hoops to jump through.

7. Cashback sites can save you even more

One of the ways to get the best out of your money is with cashback sites. If you haven’t used one before, sites like Quidco and TopCashback essentially give you money back for shopping at the same places you would anyway. You just visit the retailer through one of the cashback sites, make your purchase and then get a percentage back, paid into your cashback account. Different cashback sites offer different cashback amounts, so compare amounts before choosing one over the other. Some retailers offer boosted cashback amounts for Black Friday.

It’s not foolproof – sometimes your purchases don’t track, meaning you don’t get the money. It can also take months for the cashback to make its way into your account, so don’t factor the potential cashback amount into your purchase or don’t think of it as an additional discount on top of the Black Friday price. Think of it as a nice little bonus.

8. 

Before you even start shopping, check to see if the retailer has a membership or loyalty scheme. Retailers often provide exclusive deals and discounts, early access to sales or free delivery just for their members.

Amazon Prime is the best example. You won’t need an Amazon Prime membership to shop its Black Friday sale, but members can access limited-time lightning deals and free delivery. It costs £8.99 a month or £95 a year. New and returning customers can also get a 30-day free trial. Just remember to cancel if you don’t want to continue after Black Friday.

AO’s Five Star membership costs £39.99 a year and comes with loads of exclusive member prices, which are often lower than the lowest Black Friday prices at competitor retailers, for example. You also get free delivery, free appliance recycling and a 100-day returns period.

You don’t actually have to pay to unlock extra discounts either. I definitely recommend signing up to Currys Perks. It’s completely free to join and you’ll be sent exclusive discount codes by email to use on your purchase. I also like the My John Lewis loyalty scheme. Sign up and John Lewis will give you exclusive rewards, early access to selected sales and extra discounts on specific product categories, tailored to you. It’s always worth checking to see if a retailer has a loyalty scheme before shopping.



9. Get first dibs on Black Friday deals with fashion-label apps

Here’s a little-known trick you might not know about. Some fashion labels actually launch their Black Friday sales on their app before launching the discounts on their website or in-store, letting you browse before everyone else.

Zara is one fashion label that does this. For a few years now, it’s launched its sale the day before Black Friday itself, with its deals going live on the app an hour before the website. It’s the same for all the brands owned by Inditex, including Bershka, Pull&Bear, Stradivarius, Oysho and Massimo Dutti, which all give app users the same one-hour head start.

Asos is another one. The fashion retailer gave 24 hours of early access to its Black Friday sale last year, with app users getting access to discounts of up to 70 per cent on Wednesday 26 November, before launching to the rest of the public the following morning.

10. Consider buying last year’s model

While it’s always nice to say you’ve got the latest gizmo in the product line, you don’t always gain much more by going for the latest model.

With tech, the previous generation is often just as good (and that’s coming from a tech editor). This is especially true for TVs, laptops and headphones. These get refreshed almost every year, but the upgrades are so small you probably won’t even notice the difference. You can often find bigger discounts on the previous model, primarily because retailers slash the price when the newest one comes out.

For example, an older pair of headphones might have almost identical sound quality and noise cancellation to the latest version, but cost £100 less. Just remember to compare the specs and read reviews before deciding.

11. Work out whether bundles actually save you money

One for those of you buying games consoles this Black Friday. Make sure you actually calculate everything in a bundle to see if you’re really saving money. A Nintendo Switch 2 bundle, for example, may come with two games, a camera and a three-month membership to Switch Online, but it might actually cost more than buying everything individually. The team and I will be calculating this for you at The Independent ourselves when highlighting any bundle deals.

And even if it is cheaper to buy a bundle than it is to buy the console on its own, take a step back and think about whether you actually want the games in that bundle or if you need those accessories. You might just end up paying more than you need to.

If you just want the console, and it’s cheaper, just buy the console instead of the bundle.



12. Avoid nonsense-name brands on Amazon

Amazon is littered with unidentifiable brand names that are just a series of random capital letters. The products they’re selling are often temptingly cheap. Avoid, avoid, avoid. These oddly-named brands put their products on sale every Black Friday for cheap-as-chip prices, but there’s rarely any mark of quality. You may think you’re getting a great deal on a smartwatch or a laptop, only to realise it breaks after a few months of use.

Most of these nonsensical brand names are created by third-party sellers, many based in China, who sell generic products on Amazon under invented names. There’s even a reason why the brands choose random letters for the brand name as well. Amazon’s brand registry gives sellers with registered trademarks control over their product listings. Registering a brand with random letters is less likely to clash with existing brand trademarks, helping these nonsense brands skirt the requirement.

It doesn’t automatically mean every brand with a weird name is naff, but it’s worth doing a bit of research to check if it has a website or if there’s an easy way to get in touch with the seller. Do a TrustPilot search for the brand name as well.

13. Be wary of electric toothbrush deals

This is one that comes up every year. In fact, all year round. Electric toothbrushes are notorious for having enormous discounts plastered across listings, with some toothbrushes supposedly reduced by 70 per cent or more. Don’t believe the discount. Many of these toothbrushes rarely sell for their full recommended retail price (RRP).

Maybe you’ve spotted an Oral-B or Philips Sonicare toothbrush slashed from £200 down to £60, making it look like you’re saving a whopping £140. Except it’s been that price all year long. Just remember to check price comparison sites and ignore the misleading discounts. I have no idea why electric toothbrushes are so notorious for this, but they’re the biggest culprit when it comes to misleading discounts.

14. Don’t be fooled by countdown timers

Another psychological tactic some retailers employ is countdown timers. Maybe you’ve seen a site telling you that 73 other people are looking at the exact same product you are, or that you have 20 minutes left before the deal expires. It’s a really nasty tactic that creates a sense of urgency to pressure you into buying because you think you’ll miss out. Ignore all of it. Oftentimes, the countdown timer just resets, which under UK consumer law is illegal. Take your time and shop around.

15. Check Christmas return periods.

I always use Black Friday as a chance to get my Christmas shopping out of the way early, but just remember to check the Christmas returns window. You don’t want to end up buying something during Black Friday, only for the standard returns window to expire before Christmas Day.

Thankfully, the biggest retailers usually extend their return window for Christmas, so if grandpa doesn’t like his jumper, you can take it back – most give you until January to return unwanted prezzies.

Argos gives you until 31 January to return products bought from 23 September and Christmas Day. For Amazon, anything bought from 1 November and Christmas Day can be returned until 31 January. John Lewis will let you return products bought from 1 October and Christmas Eve until 23 January.

The same exclusions that apply at any other time of year will still apply here, however, so opened toiletries, personalised gifts and some hygiene products may not be eligible for a change-of-mind return.

16. Use your credit card for purchases over £100

Under section 75 of the Consumer Credit Act, purchases that cost more than £100 and up to £30,000 qualify for additional protection when you pay with your credit card. If the retailer goes bust, your order never arrives or the product isn't as described, your credit card provider could be jointly responsible for putting things right. It’s a good way of protecting your full purchase. Just remember to pay off your balance in full to avoid interest charges.

18. Watch out for Black Friday scams

Black Friday is Christmas come early for scammers. With millions of shoppers hunting for bargains, fraudsters are out in full force. You’ll inevitably land on fake websites, you may get sent phishing emails and you may spot discounts on products that look too good to be true.

I never trust sponsored social media adverts from a brand I’ve never heard of, especially when they’re offering pricey products at unbelievably low prices.

Watch out for text messages pretending to be from your bank, a retailer or delivery companies. If you’re unsure, check the retailer’s website directly – don’t click any links you might be suspicious about.

19. Buy now, pay later schemes have more protections – but be careful

Buy now, pay later schemes such as Klarna and Clearpay now come with stronger consumer protections, making them work more like credit card payments. On 15 July 2026, interest-free buy now, pay later agreements were brought under the regulation of the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA). That means lenders must now carry out affordability checks, as well as provide clearer information about repayments. Qualifying purchases now also benefit from section 75 protection under the Consumer Credit Act.

Still, that doesn't mean you should throw caution to the wind. Buy now, pay later makes it dangerously easy to spend more than you can afford, and that’s especially so during Black Friday. While a £600 Dyson vacuum sounds affordable when you only have to pay £200 up-front, you’re still going to be spending £600 in total. And it’ll become unwieldy if you buy everything using buy now, pay later. Taking out multiple contracts could see your monthly outgoings balloon.

20. Follow IndyBest’s Black Friday coverage

Of course, if all this sounds like a whole lot of work, we’re here to help. Here at The Independent, my colleagues and I have spent weeks tracking prices. We’ll be comparing discounts as we hunt down the best Black Friday deals. News.title: Colombia earthquake triggers surge in malaria cases
News.content:
Cases of malaria in rural Colombia have surged after a devastating earthquake left towns and villages in ruins, according to local charities.

Colombia has recorded over 74,360 cases of malaria this year, 40 per cent of which have been concentrated in Chocó – the epicentre of the earthquake which struck in August, killing at least 335 people and injuring 4,500 more.

The region has seen a 46 per cent surge in cases of the mosquito-borne disease compared to last year, up from 23,757 cases in 2025 to 34,759 cases so far in 2026.

Malaria can be very serious at any age, but it is the most dangerous for young children under five. If left untreated, it can become a medical emergency in as little as 24 hours and result in death.

While Africa accounts for around 94 per cent of global malaria cases, an estimated half a million infections occur in South America every year, mostly in the countries surrounding the Amazon basin – Colombia, Brazil, and Venezuela.

The earthquake hit at 7.4 on the Richter scale and was the strongest Colombia has seen in a decade, destroying roads and buildings. It hit during the rainy season, and water has collected in and around destroyed buildings, allowing mosquitoes, which breed in stagnant water, to survive and multiply, according to Save the Children.

Following the earthquake, thousands of people in Chocó have moved into overcrowded and unsanitary shelters after their homes were destroyed, increasing the spread of infectious diseases including malaria – which is carried between people via infected mosquitoes.

“The earthquake has worsened the conditions that favour the transmission of malaria,” Maria Mercedes Liévano, Save the Children’s Country Director in Colombia, told The Telegraph.

“Because we’re now seeing collapsed and damaged homes, families that are sleeping in overcrowded conditions out in the open, and are dealing with a health network that is overwhelmed,” Ms Liévano added.

News.title: Milk of human kindness: Brazil exports its donor breastfeeding programme worldwide
News.content:
When baby Luis Miguel was born in Guarapuava, Brazil, in February, he was unresponsive.

He had inhaled meconium, a newborn’s first stool, during delivery. It then entered his lungs and blocked his airways. Doctors at Hospital de Caridade São Vicente de Paulo resuscitated and intubated the baby boy, saving his life. He spent the next three weeks in the hospital’s neonatal unit.

His mother, 25-year-old sales assistant Luany Thainara Machado, could not produce enough breast milk and so hers was supplemented with that of a woman she had never met.

“While it might not make much sense for a mother to do this under normal circumstances it becomes very important when the need arises,” she said.

Nine months later, Luis Miguel is healthy and Machado is grateful that donor milk was able to support her son when he needed it most; so much so that today she donates 2.5 litres of her now plentiful supply every week. “Being able to help other mothers and other babies today, it feels really good,” she told The Telegraph, bouncing Luis Miguel on her knee as she spoke.

News.title: One person had a worse night than United keeper – the wretched referee
News.content:
Few Manchester United fans expected a positive result from Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge at Anfield, but the bar will not be set so low for Sporting in the Champions League this evening.

The manner of the 4-0 defeat against Liverpool, even accounting for Leny Yoro’s early red card, was dispiriting but not unexpected. The next few weeks will reveal how Pochettino intends to get a grip on the job.

When it comes to United’s Champions League prospects, the comeback win over Roma at the tail-end of Michael Carrick’s tenure made their position less perilous, but avoiding outright elimination is the first target.

United are 19th in the table, with the top 24 teams going through. Those between ninth and 24th go into a play-off round before the last 16. After Sporting away, United host RB Leipzig and Bayern Munich before a trip to Villarreal so there are stiff tests to come.

Sporting are well-placed after three wins from four, but their Champions League schedule is rather one-sided: in their final three matches they travel to Roma, before playing Barcelona and Manchester City. They reached the quarter-finals of the competition last season, losing narrowly to Arsenal over two legs.

They are third in their league, having been weakened by the summer sales of Geovany Quenda (to Chelsea), Morten Hjulmand (to Atletico Madrid) and Ousmane Diomande (to Nottingham Forest). The vast majority of goals are scored by Colombian striker Luis Suárez.

Bruno Fernandes, United’s captain, returns to his former club tonight and there is hope Luke Shaw could be back at left-back. Pochettino must decide whether or not to stick with Matthijs de Ligt, who was extremely rusty at Anfield but may need the minutes.

Yoro’s one-game suspension was overturned by the FA, and he would have been available for this one in any case.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: ‘It blocks out the sun’: The toxic dust storms choking Uzbekistan
News.content:
In the early hours of the morning last June, Gulbara Aminova woke up with a violent fit of coughing. The 39-year-old got up to shut her bedroom windows. But as she did, she saw something disturbing outside.

“My car was covered in powder,” says Aminova, a resident of the town of Moynaq in western Uzbekistan. “It was like it had been snowing. But it was the summer.”

The fine dust on her car was far from a picturesque snow scene: it was in fact a toxic mix of salt and sand laced with pesticides and other chemicals, blown in by strong winds during the night. The dirty air had been making it difficult for Aminova and her three children to breathe at night.

For the residents of Moynaq, a former fishing town on the edge of the Aral Sea, these storms have become a public health emergency, with fears that they are behind not only air pollution spikes but high rates of cancer, tuberculosis and other diseases.

“Two of my daughters have asthma,” says Aminova. “I lost my father and my aunt to cancer. There is a lot of sickness here. I think it’s because of the dust.”

Today, sand and dust storms strike as many as a 100 times a year in Uzbekistan, many of them originating in the desiccated wastelands that decades ago were home to the world’s fourth-largest lake.

News.title: Mick Harford: ‘My prostate cancer diagnosis was a shock. As a footballer, I’d felt bulletproof’
News.content:
However, an MRI scan and a PSMA PET scan at UCLH, where I had been referred, showed only a little bit of growth on my prostate, and I was told I would be fine. But, while I was symptomless at the time, within around eight months I was getting up three or four times in the night to go to the toilet, and then feeling the urge to go back again only two minutes later. I instinctively knew something was wrong.

Upon my return to UCLH in December, I was told my PSA was now “very high”, at around 48 ng/mL – far more elevated than the 4.5 ng/mL considered healthy for my age group. Advanced prostate cancer was then confirmed with a biopsy. The first person I told was my son, William, in a phone call from the car at the hospital. It was horrible – it was not just me who would suffer, but my family too. I also needed to tell Luton Town, who were amazing and gave me as much time off work as I needed from my role as assistant manager.

Facing the opponent

My brilliant oncology team immediately had a plan for me. They got me on a course of hormone therapy medications called Enzalutamide and Zoladex, in preparation for me to begin radiation treatment from mid-August. I had 49 sessions over the space of about eight weeks, and it was daunting each time I travelled into London on the train from my home in Harpenden to go underground to the hospital’s Radiotherapy Department.

But I got through it, even with a bit of collateral damage. While my ongoing symptoms are not a pleasant conversation, it’s an important one, because it has affected my life in so many ways. My sleep is disrupted because I still need to get up multiple times during the night to go to the toilet so I can avoid an accident in bed. I also have to wear a nappy every day in case of leakage, and need to be careful when I’m out to ensure I’m close to a toilet.

I’m still on a hormone therapy called Triptorelin to block my testosterone, which feeds the cancer, and takes the form of an injection every six months. As a result, I’m going through the “male menopause”, which is not very nice and can cause tiredness, sleep issues and brain fog. It has given me lots of sympathy for women of my generation.

However, as I approach six years since my diagnosis, I’ve tried to stay proactive as much as possible. The discipline and drive instilled in me as a footballer have come in handy. To be a successful player, you need to stick to a routine. In the same way that I worked hard to ensure my teammates and coaches respected me on the pitch, so I’ve adhered to what all the doctors have advised – including trying to be diligent in terms of lifestyle.

News.content:
Enzo Maresca had two home games in four days to get Manchester City into decent shape for Sunday’s clash against Arsenal, which now feels like a must-win. On Tuesday, however, they ended up being taunted by Rasmus Hojlund on another evening that raised more questions than answers.

It is now one win in seven for Maresca, who cannot keep a clean sheet and has a £327m midfield that have played well individually, but is yet to form a unit. Worryingly, their reliable source of goals, Erling Haaland, had his quietest game of the season. It required Rayan Cherki to rescue a point against Napoli.

Maresca needs to find a solution in the next five days before heading to the Emirates to face the champions in what could be a defining weekend for the season. Defeat would put them nine points off the pace, with Maresca still trying to find his best combination of players to pick.

Club captain Rúben Dias was on the bench here and Josko Gvardiol was left out of the draw against Fulham at the weekend, which also ended as a draw rather than a morale-boosting win to get City out of their slump.

XABI ALONSO is in the middle of a culture war at Chelsea — and his future will hang on winning it.

After back-to-back humbling defeats to Sunderland and Leeds, having also lost to Tottenham at home this season, the Alonso era is off to a stuttering start.



Add to that Cole Palmer angrily dismissing a team-mate and coach at full-time at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, plus Wesley Fofana making a fool of himself in a YouTube interview, and all is not well in south-west London.

Alonso was hired to set the club on the correct course after a season of turmoil and some very serious looking in the mirror by the ownership.



The Spaniard was brought in to raise standards, stop wasteful red cards and put an end to the petulance which has defined Chelsea in recent years.

There has been plenty of talk of process and progress, and steps to be taken.



Alonso is aware that nothing will change if he can’t correct the undercurrent of immature behaviour.

Are we seeing any signs of a change? Not at all — and Alonso knows he has a big job on his hands to alter the attitude of his squad.

He said: “We are in the process. Taking steps, taking a step forward, but until it is totally in the DNA of the team it takes time.

“The tendency is improving, but we have highs and lows. We knew that could happen, but when you feel it, it is not good.

“Having lived that, we have talked about what we can do better and what we have to do better.

Alonso’s firm belief is that culture and team spirit come before everything. A strong culture leads to good football and good results.

The lack of a culture or identity, then, must lead to what we are seeing now, where Chelsea are too easy to push off course and soft when they need to stand up.



Alonso is concerned his side were unable to deliver the basics against Leeds and says that at Nottingham Forest on Friday night, there is no excuse not to at least deliver on that.

One reaction would be to start fighting back, rather than roll over.

Sports.title: How Mikel Arteta’s ‘tactical tornado’ can blow Man City away with Arsenal set to adopt new approach in attack
Sports.content:
Next

ARSENAL will be looking to give their hopes of retaining the Premier League crown a huge boost when they host Manchester City on Sunday.

The Gunners are six points clear at the summit despite being forced to settle for a draw at Newcastle last week.



And City have been struggling to rediscover their best form, with Erling Haaland admitting his team-mates are not on the same wavelength.

SunSport’s tactical expert Dean Scoggins broke down how Arsenal could get the better of their title rivals in the latest episode of Tactics Exposed.



ARTETA’S MUSICAL CHAIRS

I think Mikel Arteta is making a conscious tactical effort to give Arsenal more chances to score goals.

Some fans might say they look vulnerable, I say fun. Last season, they were the functional champions. But this season, I think they’re going to be more fun.



It’s musical chairs from Arteta, with there being a high number of rotations in the system.

The full-backs are really making that chaotic move. Arsenal are ending up with their full-backs in central midfield positions when they are on the attack.

It gives the opposition problems because the transitions make it very difficult to mark.

The right winger, who is expected to be Noni Madueke, also moves into the centre forward position and Viktor Gyokeres was running into the channels against Borussia Dortmund.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

They continue rotating and that creates more areas to run in behind the backline.

There were times in the draw with Dortmund where Piero Hincapie and Ben White, who started at full-back, were the furthest men forward.

The full-backs are the disruptors in this system. They are not getting on the end of the chances.

City’s defenders could get drawn out of position and that will lead to plenty of space in behind.

But Arsenal’s attacking shape means they could get caught out on the counter-attack.



If they go seven-versus-six on one side of the pitch, there could be space for City.

It’s a bit of a tactical tornado from Arteta, where it’s much more organised chaos than pure structure.

RAY OF HOPE?

David Raya will be a big miss because he is a fantastic goalkeeper. Kepa Arrizabalaga is a decent stand-in.



But Raya is the start of the tactical trigger. He plays them out and decides when to go short or long, but Kepa hasn’t done that as often.

City had a different approach to pressing when Kepa was between the sticks in the Carabao Cup final last season – and that is what we will see in this game.

Under Pep Guardiola, City moved into a 4-2-4 block shape. They dropped back and let Kepa have the ball.

Kepa made no passes into midfield during the Carabao Cup final because of how City set themselves up.

We will see Arsenal’s defenders split and the full-backs push up high and wide in an attempt to give their keeper options.



The central midfielders will also come out of the middle of the park to allow a pass to be made between the lines and into the attacking players.

Kepa needs to be brave on the ball because City will try to make it difficult for him.

RUNNERS SET TO MAKE DIFFERENCE

Arsenal will try to paralyse City in the press. City’s players have got sucked into a position before, which could leave Arsenal with a spare man.



Arsenal should target their runners, like Madueke and Gyokeres. It worked for Napoli during their Champions League draw at the Etihad.

Full-backs have been caught out at times this season, leading to their midfielders and centre-backs being split.

I think Madueke and Gyokeres are going to have a bit of a field day if City get their press wrong.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Arsenal will get their joy on the right-hand side of their attack, I reckon, because City have looked slightly off it in the press.

If Arsenal have an overload in the central area, Nico O’Reilly would have to push in from left-back and that creates more space for Madueke.

Sports.title: Premier League legend Fabrizio Ravanelli wins High Court battle over £340k tax bill linked to playing days
Sports.content:
Next

PREMIER League legend Fabrizio Ravanelli has won a High Court fight with the taxman over a bill linked to his playing days.

Italian striker Ravanelli, famed for his prematurely white hair, was one of the biggest stars in the early days of the Prem with Middlesbrough.



When he later moved to Derby County some of his earnings were paid into an “employee benefit trust”.

Tax was due when that was paid up — but the former player successfully argued it should not have included the £340,000 in National Insurance contributions as that was down to his old employers.



Mr Justice Eardley said: “I shall quash the decision refusing to reopen the settlement agreement.”

He added: “HMRC will need to remake that decision, this time without any reliance upon the erroneous view that, as a matter of substantive tax law, the trustee was liable to pay NICs.”

The judge said HMRC’s refusal was “vitiated by a material error of law” — though added it would be “jumping the gun” to order them to reopen the settlement or hand over the cash immediately.

During the hearing, Ravanelli’s barrister Tim Johnston told the court: “The NICs were not owed by or on behalf of Mr Ravanelli. They remained liabilities of the employer, who had ceased to exist.

“According to HMRC’s own guidance, no sums should have been withheld in respect of NICs when the distribution from the EBT was made to Mr Ravanelli.

“Mr Ravanelli’s case is that, as a matter of tax law, NICs were never due. As a result, no amount for NICs should have been deducted from the distribution out of the EBT.”



HMRC barrister Adam Tolley KC had argued: “When the trustee made the distribution, for the purposes of the relevant NICs legislation it did so as the deemed employer of the claimant and he received the distribution as the deemed employee of the trustee.

“As such, the trustee was liable to pay the NICs.”

Police were quickly on the scene to stop the trouble escalating.

And after reinforcements raced over, there were cheers as a large number of individuals were turfed out.

Sports.title: Hellberg tells Middlesbrough stars to embrace St Mary’s hate as bitter rivals face off for first time since Spygate
Sports.content:

KIM HELLBERG may have buried the hatchet with Tonda Eckert but he wants his Middlesbrough stars to embrace the hate at St Mary’s.

Boro face bitter rivals Southampton for the first time on Friday since last season’s Spygate controversy rocked the football world.



The Saints beat Hellberg’s side in the Championship play-off semi-final before being booted out having been found guilty of spying on them and two other clubs.

Boro were reinstated and lost to Hull City in the Wembley showpiece but Southampton are still feeling the effects from the scandal having also been hit with a four-point deduction this term.



Swede Hellberg, 38, told SunSport this summer he had forgiven opposite number Eckert, who received a six-week suspended ban and a £28,000 fine for three breaches of FA Rule E3.1 for directing or authorising observations of training sessions.

He later revealed Southampton’s German head coach, 33, called him personally to apologise and stressed throughout Thursday’s press conference the need to “move on”. The two managers even hope to enjoy a beer together after the full time whistl.



However, tensions remain high between supporters. Rather than direct their rage towards their own club for blowing a £215m promotion shot, some Saints fans have instead directed their anger towards Boro, whose own faithful are still fuming over the spy saga.

Security has been ramped up on the South Coast ahead of the game, and Hellberg knows his table-toppers will be stepping into a cauldron. But he wants his players to enjoy every second and learn from it.

On what his message will be to his stars ahead of stepping into the Southampton cauldron, he exclusively told Sun Sport: “It’s just embrace and love it, and looking forward to the challenge of playing a very good side in a very hostile environment. That is a thing to learn from, a thing that you can put in your backpack.

“I played derbies in Sweden in front of 50,000 where you cannot even hear what you’re thinking. I know a lot of players have similar experience from different types of leagues and things. So it’s all about being there, preparing to play a football game where we hopefully can, at the end of the day, be the better side.

“It is a great game of football between two very good teams. Southampton is up there with the best teams in the league.

“Tonda has done a brilliant job. They have some players that are absolutely fantastic that I gladly would have in my squad.”

Boro made it back-to-back wins since the international break as Will Lankshear’s 16th goal of the season secured a 2-1 victory over Swansea on Tuesday on the hotshot’s first start since a three-week lay-off with a hamstring issue.

He added: “It has been absolutely crazy with everything. And being the first time I’ve coached a team outside of Sweden, there was also the challenge that comes with that.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi confirmed to play in ex-Man Utd star’s football farewell match alongside Rio Ferdinand and Sergio Aguero
Sports.content:
Next

LIONEL MESSI has sensationally signed up to feature in Premier League icon Carlos Tevez’s emotional farewell match.

The World Cup winner, 39, is still gunning for MLS Cup glory with Inter Miami.



But Messi, who was lucky to escape a red card after launching the ball into Columbus Crew striker Gonzalo Tapia’s face last week, is set to be reunited with former Argentina team-mate Tevez.

The iconic striker is holding a special testimonial at Boca Juniors’ historic La Bombonera home on December 20.



It comes five years after Tevez – who scored 84 Premier League goals during spells with West Ham, Manchester United and Manchester City – hung up his boots.

And Messi has agreed to be involved just weeks after he could get his hands on the MLS Cup.



Tevez, 42, and the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner made 47 appearances alongside each other for Argentina.

Having been team-mates during the 2006 and 2010 World Cups, they have gone on to remain close pals.

And Messi, who made his final international outing in October, is preparing to head back to his homeland to be by Tevez’s side.

The Barcelona legend is not the only big name to have confirmed their involvement.

The pair got their hands on two top-flight titles while they were together at Old Trafford.

Sergio Aguero is also on course to link-up with his ex-City and Argentina strike partner.

Italian goalkeeping legend Gianluigi Buffon is in line to be between the sticks for the farewell fixture.



Leandro Paredes, who collapsed during a post-match interview last week, has given Tevez the green light.

Boca Juniors goalscoring sensation Martin Palermo is preparing to feature as well.

Sports.title: Europa League game suspended after pro-Palestine flag unfurled as police clash with fans
Sports.content:
Europa League game suspended after pro-Palestine flag unfurled as police clash with fans

The Europa League match was suspended as fans clashed with police in the stands and officers deployed tear gas and used batons

View 2 Images Play was stopped as Besiktas faced Hapoel Be'er Sheva in the Europa League (Image: Getty)

The Europa League match between Besiktas and Israel's Hapoel Be'er Sheva was brought to a halt after supporters clashed with police in the stands. The fixture is being staged in Batumi, Georgia.

‌



‌



Trouble flared amongst fans in the 25th minute of the match, prompting players and officials to swiftly leave the pitch as play was suspended. Georgian police officers appeared to deploy tear gas and batons against a section of the Besiktas supporters as tensions boiled over.

‌



Footage circulating online showed a Besiktas fan allegedly being carried out of the stands on a stretcher. The precise cause of the violence remains unclear, though the disturbances broke out after Besiktas fans unfurled - or attempted to unfurl - a pro-Palestinian banner in the crowd. Play has since resumed.

‌



The fixture had already been moved to a neutral venue after Turkish and UEFA officials relocated it from Istanbul amid security concerns surrounding ties between Turkish and Israeli clubs.

Diplomatic relations between Ankara and Israel remain deeply strained over the ongoing conflict in Gaza, with both the Turkish government and its public firmly backing the Palestinian cause.

View 2 Images The match was suspended (Image: Getty)

‌

Besiktas took to social media in the wake of the trouble to confirm that the match had resumed. The club also levelled accusations at Georgian police, claiming they had used "disproportionate force" against their supporters.

‌



Photographs accompanying the post showed tear gas or pepper spray being deployed against a section of the Besiktas supporters by police, corroborating reports emerging from inside the stadium.

Just before the interval, Besiktas were awarded a penalty, but captain Orkun Kokcu squandered the opportunity from the spot. The match remained goalless heading into the break.

‌



Prior to kick-off, Besiktas players, including Kokcu, refused to shake hands with Be'er Sheva players. Several other Turkish Super Lig clubs have since rallied behind Besiktas, voicing their opposition to the relocation of the match and the police's conduct.

Besiktas released a statement on the incident. It reads: "We strongly condemn the security forces for using disproportionate force against our fans before and during our first team's UEFA Europa League match against Hapoel Be'er Sheva in Batumi, Georgia, and extend our condolences to the fans affected by the incidents.

‌

"Our Board Members and club officials have been closely monitoring the situation since our fans began making their way to the stadium. Upon learning that security forces were obstructing our fans' entry into the stadium, we immediately contacted the UEFA delegate, who arranged for the stadium's evacuation gates to be opened, allowing our fans to enter the stadium quickly and safely.

Sports.title: Ex-Arsenal star Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang involved in crash with car overturned
Sports.content:
Ex-Arsenal star Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang involved in crash with car overturned

Former Arsenal striker Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang has been involved in a car crash on his way to training in northwest Spain

View 2 Images Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang was involved in a car accident (Image: Getty)

Ex-Arsenal and Chelsea striker Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang has been involved in a car accident on his way to training for Spanish club Deportivo La Coruna. The Gabon star's Ferrari collided with another car on a motorway in northwest Spain on Thursday morning.

‌



‌



Aubameyang, who left the Gunners in 2022, was on his way to train when his vehicle, a turquoise Ferrari F12 N-Largo, struck a BMW X1 on kilometre 16 of the AP-9 in the Piadela area. The BMW was overturned and had to be towed.

‌



However, the 37-year-old former Premier League forward was able to continue to his club's Cidade Deportiva de Abegondo training complex in his own car. Emergency services arrived on the scene, followed by the Civil Guard, firefighters and paramedics in the early morning, around 9:30am local time.

‌



No serious injuries were reported and everyone was able to exit their vehicles safely. Aubameyang completed the training session as expected and speaking after the ordeal, he said: "It was just a little scare.

"These things happen in life. The most important thing is that the other person involved in the accident is fine, and so am I."

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Aubameyang joined the newly-promoted Deportivo in July. Despite being 37, he admits that the hunger is still there. He penned a two-year deal, expiring in 2028.

‌



"The passion is still there, definitely, otherwise I'd choose another challenge," he told Mirror Football in August.

"I had a few offers, but the passion is still there and I still want to challenge myself and think this one is a special challenge to try to bring back the club to its best.

‌



"Next year is going to be 20 years since I started my career as a professional and I have to say the truth, I'm feeling quite good. I can still give a lot for the game and still have the passion, I think this will never change.

"As long as my body says I can go, I will go. Obviously, if I feel one day I cannot give my best to play at the best level, I'll say maybe I stop, but for the moment I'm sure that I have some more years to give.

‌



"This is why I accepted the challenge here, because I know I can really help, I can still score some goals, I can give some assists, I can be effective in the game."

Article continues below

Aubameyang signed for Arsenal in 2018 for a then-club-record fee. During his time at the Emirates, he scored 92 goals in 163 appearances. After four years as a Gunner, he left for Barcelona.

Since then, the Gabon international has played for Chelsea, Marseille on two separate occasions and Saudi Pro League side Al-Qadsiah before returning to Spain. He faces former club Barcelona on Sunday.

Sports.title: English footballer, 18, shot dead outside restaurant as tributes pour in
Sports.content:
English footballer, 18, shot dead outside restaurant as tributes pour in

Krissh Mahatma, 18, was fatally struck by a bullet outside Green Ghost Tacos in Jackson, Mississippi

View Image Krissh Mahatma was killed in the US (Image: Jam Press/Co-Lin Community College)

A talented young English footballer who relocated to the United States has tragically lost his life after being caught up in a shooting outside a restaurant.

Krissh Mahatma, 18, was fatally struck by a bullet after a shot rang out outside Green Ghost Tacos in Jackson, Mississippi, in the early hours of Sunday morning.

The teenager was in his first year at Copiah Lincoln Community College in Wesson, situated roughly 45 miles south of the city where the tragic incident occurred.

It is understood that Mahatma was with several of his team-mates when a man produced a firearm in a nearby car park and opened fire into the group, leaving the 18-year-old with a fatal gunshot wound.

Local police have since arrested a 22-year-old man on a murder charge. The Mississippi Department of Public Safety offered no further details regarding the circumstances surrounding the fatal shooting.

"While this arrest is an important step toward justice, we recognise that nothing can ease the pain of losing a loved one," said police chief Mark Miller, who also offered his condolences to Mahatma's family.

Mahatma had made 14 appearances in his first three months with the Co-Lin Wolves, netting once in a 3-2 victory over National Park College in September.

Prior to making the move across the Atlantic, he had turned out for Watford 'A' in the post-16 Community and Education Football Alliance league. Sports.title: Ex-Man City finance guru 'reveals date' of appeal verdict against 115 charges
Sports.content:
Ex-Man City finance guru 'reveals date' of appeal verdict against 115 charges

Manchester City are still waiting to discover their fate after being found guilty on of breaking Premier League financial rules - and an appeal verdict could arrive before Christmas

View 2 Images Manchester City may learn the outcome of their appeal in just weeks (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester City may discover the outcome of their appeal against financial breaches before Christmas, according to one of the club's former financial advisors.

‌



‌



City were found guilty of 114 breaches of financial rules by an independent commission, who concluded that the former multi-time Premier League champions used "sham" contracts in order to try and conceal in excess of £830million worth of extra funding. The club have since appealed the decision and are liable to serious penalties if it fails, including fines and/or points deductions and even potential expulsion from the Premier League itself.

‌



It remains to be seen when City will officially discover the outcome of their appeal amid concerns that a long delay could damage the integrity of this year's Premier League.

‌



But Stefan Borson, a former financial advisor to the club, has revealed that he has been told City could discover the appeal verdict as soon as next month.

Black Friday special! Click here to sign up to Mirror+ for just £1 a month!

Speaking on Football Uncensored with Piers Morgan and Simon Jordan, he said: "We're told that it [the appeal] will be mid-December. Because of the way the days fall, that's likely to start on the 12th.

‌



"It's likely to go for between five and 10 days, it seems, and therefore finish before Christmas. And then we wait for a decision. Ordinarily, that decision would take quite some time.

"I suspect that certainly the Premier League want to get it expedited so they get a decision and can then have the sanction hearing and the sanction appeal, which is inevitable either way, in before the end of the season so they can effectively sanction City and punish them this season."

‌



View 2 Images City could face expulsion from the Premier League if their appeal fails (Image: Getty Images)

Borson went on to theorise that a schedule for the process may have already been agreed given the Premier League will be keen to avoid a legal battle after taking years to get to this point.

‌



He added: "In the rulebook that came out at the start of the season, the rules changed and you had an expedited timetable. In any event, a case like City's and an appeal like City's would never fall within the standardised timetable.

"I think most likely the parties have ultimately agreed some form of timetable which means that any argument from City in the future about the process goes away.

Article continues below

"The last thing the Premier League will want is to give City another reason to take legal action under Rule X or otherwise and to say, actually the whole appeal process, not only was the old process flawed but we didn't even have a fair appeal. Because if they do that, we're back to square one."

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner slams players for not learning English
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner slams players for not learning English

Nottingham Forest head coach Oliver Glasner has questioned the standards prior to his arrival, revealing some players have not learned English despite being at the club for years

View 2 Images Oliver Glasner has criticised some Nottingham Forest players for not learning English (Image: Jon Hobley/NurPhoto)

Oliver Glasner singled out Nottingham Forest players who have been at the club for years and "can't speak English" in an attack on the poor standards that preceded his arrival.

‌



‌



The former Crystal Palace manager, 52, became Forest's fifth head coach in less than a year back in the summer when he was lured to The City Ground after bringing the curtain down on an impressive stint in south London, overseeing a Conference League triumph and an FA Cup for the Eagles.

‌



Glasner has endured a challenging start to his premiership with Forest, however, winning just two of his 11 Premier League games at the helm.

‌



The Austrian revealed this week that he will be backed in the winter transfer window by the Forest owner, Evangelos Marinakis, before taking aim at the environment he inherited.

Black Friday special! Click here to sign up to Mirror+ for just £1 a month!

“Stability in a company is having standards,” Glasner said. “Everybody who joins commits to the standards. I think, very honestly, the standards were not high enough.

‌



“We have players who are here for four years, [who] can’t speak English. If you go to Italy, after three months, every player gives his interview in the Italian language. For me, if I want to manage in England, I have to speak English.”

Forest face Chelsea on Friday night in their next Premier League outing. Ahead of the game, Glasner admitted Forest have fallen below expectations before demanding improvements from his players.

‌



“We have just two wins after 11 games. We wanted and expected more from us, to be honest, but that's the reality, he added. “For me, it's always accepting the reality and now having a look at what we need to improve and work on. That's the only way.

View 2 Images Glasner says he and Evangelos Marinakis have discussed January transfer window plans (Image: Andrew Kearns - CameraSport, CameraSport via Getty Images)

‌



“I'm no magician. I have no magician dust I can spread somewhere at the training ground. My experience is it takes hard work, especially in the Premier League.

“We need to improve our individual mistakes -- we make too many in defence and then you get punished in the Premier League.

‌



“We need to improve our efficiency in attack and we definitely need to improve our set-pieces, because it's still no goal from a set-piece.”

Glasner says he spent six hours travelling to meet Marinakis in London to discuss January transfer plans. The club are expected to target five new players when the window reopens.

Article continues below

“He [Marinakis] was asking ‘what do you need, what do you want here to improve in the squad, the staff and the environment’,” said Glasner. “He wants the best for Nottingham Forest, he wants the best for everyone here.”

Bruno Fernandes accidentally manufactured the divot that led to his freak goal for Manchester United just seconds later.

‌



The Portugal playmaker was back facing his former side Sporting Lisbon and scored twice in the space of three second-half minutes. His second was a strike from distance that initially looked like being a routine save for Kaique Pereira.
