Sports.title: Thomas Frank earns his first Crystal Palace victory as boss, Bournemouth win TENTH game in a row with comeback, and Brighton thrash Romanian minnows - but Sunderland are held at home
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace 2-1 Real Sociedad, by Will Pickworth

Thomas Frank said he was happy to be 'back in the circus' at his Crystal Palace unveiling, yet when he found himself staring down the barrel at a second defeat in a week, he may have been rueing that statement.

But when Chris Richards' long-throw made its way to Jean-Philippe Mateta, everything changed on a chaotic night at Selhurst Park.

The French forward was pulled down by Jon Martin, who was sent off, and after Mateta tucked away his penalty, a flat performance and atmosphere was transformed.

Having been dominated, Palace were now quick, confident and incisive, and it was the Basque outfit who were on the ropes as Daichi Kamada saw an effort cleared off the line.

Jorgen Strand Larsen then attempted an audacious bicycle kick which fell to the feet of Dwight McNeil yards out to send the home fans into delirium.

It could have been more, but Yeremy Pino's penalty in added time was saved and Strand Larsen missed an open goal. Dean Henderson then made a brilliant stop to secure the three points.

Thomas Frank got his first win as Crystal Palace boss as his side came from behind to beat Real Sociedad 2-1

Palace's season has been a disaster thus far, but it now has lift-off, and most importantly belief, heading into Sunday's crunch clash with Hull.

'It could be (a turning point) but we need to follow it up with a good performance against Hull,' said Frank. 'But you can take a lot of positives. What I really liked is the belief from the players and that we were a threat on set pieces.

'The penalty and red card changed the game. It’s not easy 10 vs 11, but we were brave and it paid off - and then we were all close to a heart attack in the last five minutes!'

Frank, who received a warm reception from the Eagles faithful ahead of his first home game, handed rare starts to Will Hughes, Ben Chilwell and Eddie Nketiah as he rang the changes after last week’s defeat by Coventry.

They practised defending set-pieces in the warm-up in an attempt to deal with what has become their kryptonite, yet Chelsea loanee Mamadou Sarr almost turned in at the far post from a free kick just minutes in.

After a poor opening half hour, Sociedad stepped things up and Henderson was forced into a string of good saves. Palace’s midfield was struggling and the Basque outfit should have gone ahead when Mikel Oyarzabal somehow fired straight at Henderson from a few yards out.

The England keeper had to be alert again soon after, yet the pressure paid off when Sarr turned home from Job Ochieng's cross.

But the game changed with Mateta's intervention, before McNeil ensured that, despite the injury-time mayhem, Frank is more than happy to be back in the madhouse of management.

'The feeling after a win on the pitch with players, staff and fans, but also in the changing room is so difficult to describe - it’s so unique,' said Frank. 'You like to experience a lot of that, but the hectic last 15 minutes, that was crazy.'

'The red card and penalty were the decisive action in the match,' added Sociedad boss Pellegrino Matarazzo. 'We controlled the match completely up until that. We tried to stabilise, but we could not hold them off long enough.'

Celta Vigo 1-2 Bournemouth , by Luke Power

Can anybody stop Bournemouth? For long stretches here it looked as if their relentless march would finally be stopped - but the 10-man Cherries found another gear to continue their rampage.

Marco Rose’s men have won 10 games in a row now, extending a club record. For two months, they have steamrolled their opponents with dauntless football and racked up an aggregate score of 25-3. They sit top of the Europa League with a perfect record.

Underneath the red and black armour, fans are starting to wonder if these players are actually of our species. Is Justin Kluivert a man or a cyborg? If you prick James Hill, does he bleed?

With each victory, the cry of the football world grows louder: somebody, please, stop this Bournemouth juggernaut, for the sake of everybody else’s trophy prospects.

Celta Vigo stepped up as the next challengers and thought they would be the heroes. They found Bournemouth’s net four times in all, but were denied by the offside flag for three of them. For long stretches, they were in command.

Bournemouth have now won 10 games in a row after coming from behind to beat Celta Vigo 2-1

After a disappointing first half, Alvaro Rodriguez got them level early in the second

Rayan scored the winner against the run of play as Bournemouth continued their perfect run in the Europa League

In the first half, Bournemouth looked average. They were gifting away the ball in their own half, Celta found ways to sneak through their pincer-movement press, and the Spaniards had the better chances.

The first red flag came 11 minutes in, when Michele Di Gregorio spilled a save into the path of Pablo Duran, who dinked over the goalkeeper but saw his effort ruled out for offside.

Such warning bells were unheeded. Not long later, former Liverpool man Iago Aspas forced a save with a spectacular overhead kick at the age of 39.

Bournemouth failed to clear their lines, and Aspas punished the visitors, ghosting past Alex Scott on his return from injury before blasting beyond Di Gregorio with his left foot.

Things went from bad to worse minutes later when Bafode Diakite was sent off for a stamp on Couhaib Driouech, his yellow card upgraded to a red after a review by referee Harm Osmers.

Celta almost doubled their lead when Duran beat Di Gregorio again, but he had strayed offside.

The cameras panned to Rose, who stood looking bewildered on the sidelines, hands on hips. It took them 37 minutes for Kluivert to register their first shot. Bournemouth had been played off the park. This was a case of clinging on.

But the side that emerged in the second half were unrecognisable. If Bournemouth were a man down, they played with all the swagger of having an extra body.

They were level within two minutes of the restart, Alvaro Rodriguez glancing in from Amine Adli’s header.

Suddenly Bournemouth were their efflorescent selves again. Antonio Silva, Adli, and Rodriguez combined for a beautiful passage of play but were spurned by the offside flag. Hill tested Ionut Radu from range.

They finally got their rewards on the counter-attack, when Marcus Tavernier teed up his fellow substitute Rayan to slot past Radu and stun their hosts. Another comeback job complete.

And so the Bournemouth army marches on unfettered. In the next nine days, they face Fulham, Brighton, and Hull in the Premier League. By the time they visit Arsenal in mid-December, they may be breathing down their necks.

Brighton 4-0 Craiova, by Ben Winstanley

Earlier this week, Brighton CEO Paul Barber revealed the lengths that his club go to before agreeing to sign a player.

'We try and talk to people that know them, people that have coached them, people that played with them, sponsors that have worked with them, media that have interviewed them, maybe even neighbours that have lived next door to them,' he told Men in Blazers media network. 'You know, what sort of people are we talking about? Are we talking about players that are entirely focused on their work?'

There can be little doubt that the rigorous selection process is working, and two of their budget buys were on the scoresheet in the first half as they made light work of the Romanian champions Universitatea Craiova - and continued to make a mockery of the supposed challenge of balancing domestic and European assaults.

In the third minute Ibrahim Osman - £16.6m from Nordsjaelland in 2024 – finished off a sharp team move from close range after a pinpoint Jack Hinshelwood cross. Then shortly after the half-hour mark full back Maxime de Cuyper, £17m from Club Brugge in 2025, seized on a slack defensive ball into midfield, took two touches in advancing forward and - still well outside the box – wrongfooted the goalkeeper as he stroked the ball into the far corner. He made the finish look much easier than it was.

Brighton thrashed Romanian champions Universitatea Craiova and look capable of competing on multiple fronts

If the result was still in any doubt then, it wasn’t by the 39th minute when Vladimir Screciu was sent off for a clumsy challenge on Matt O’Riley. Referee Matthias Jollenbeck showed a yellow card but a replay showed a hefty tread on the ankle and - after being sent to his monitor - upgraded it to red.

The second half, then, gave the Seagulls a chance to remind everyone of their ruthless side. Already the highest scorers in the Premier League - averaging 2.4 per game this season – they wasted little time adding to their tally.

First, 19-year-old Charalampos Kostoulas made it three with his sixth of the season thanks to a cool finish on the hour mark, two minutes before Osman – like Hinshelwood a constant menace - picked the ball up on the left and cut inside to roll home his second.

They ended 90 minutes of domination having had 27 shots – one of which saw Femi Azeez missing the chance to make it five on debut by inexplicably blazing over from five yards.

Brighton have now scored four or more in five of their eight home games this season, and ended last night’s rout top of the Conference League having yet to concede a goal. The competition does not look big enough for them.

Sunderland 1-1 Jagiellonia Bialystok, Miles Starforth

Sunderland still have work to do if the club is to reach the Europa League’s knockout stages after Jagiellonia Bialystok held them to a 1-1 draw in a game which saw some supporters of the Polish club evade a UEFA ban and get into the Stadium of Light.

Timur Tutierov’s second-half opener for Sunderland, hoping to secure a top-eight finish in the competition’s league phase and avoid the play-offs in their first European campaign in 53 years, was quickly cancelled out by the visitors.

‘It’s clear we are making many unforced errors this season leading to goals,’ said head coach Regis Le Bris. ‘The last two games, it didn’t happen, which is good, and now this is a reminder you can’t relax.’

Jagiellonia supporters had been banned from the game following crowd disturbances at the club’s fixture away to Levski Sofia on November 5.

But a number of visiting fans were removed from the stadium by police during the first half, and a “disappointed” Sunderland issued a statement after the game which claimed that Jagiellonia had “failed to engage and cooperate” with efforts to stop their supporters getting into home sections.

Le Bris had gone into the game without injured captain Granit Xhaka and striker Brian Brobbey, two of his most influential players. Sunderland’s head coach, mindful of forthcoming Premier League games against Tottenham Hotspur, Liverpool and Newcastle United, took no chances with the pair for the visit of Jagiellonia, ninth in the Polish league.

Sunderland had to settle for a 1-1 draw against Polish side Jagiellonia Bialystok

He made six changes from the team which had held Aston Villa to a goalless draw at the weekend, again fielding a youthful team in the competition.

A flat performance from a much-changed team had seen Sunderland beaten 2-0 by Croatian champions Dinamo Zagreb in their last European outing at the Stadium of Light. The visiting section had been bouncing that night, in contrast to the empty seats for the visit of Jagiellonia.

On Wearside, the feeling ahead of the match was that third-bottom Sunderland, while shot shy, were slowly turning a corner, having taken four points from fixtures against Chelsea and Villa without conceding a goal to climb above Manchester United in the table.

The big one in Europe - AC Milan at the San Siro - is next in the competition for Sunderland, with the fixture having captured the imagination of supporters.

There were scarves with the slogan ‘Have you ever seen a Mackem in Milan? You’re about to!’ on sale outside the ground, with the merchandise a nod to a song which fans of their rivals Newcastle United can no longer sing.

Sunderland had an early scare when a Nik Prelec shot took a deflection off Ndah Sidiki, but Robin Roefs was able to gather the ball.

Within minutes of the game starting, it became apparent that a group of Polish fans had managed to buy tickets in the North Stand, and police were quickly called to remove them from the stadium amid cheers from Sunderland supporters.

On the pitch, it was another slow start for Le Bris’ side, though Malick Fofana tested Slawomir Abramowicz with a fine left-footed shot from outside the box.

Timur Tutierov was on target fo the Black Cats, but this was a flat performance

Enzo Le Fee did well to seize on a back pass in the 30th minute and cross from the left for Nilson Angulo - who was unmarked in the box - after rounding the goalkeeper. However, his shot struck the feet of Yuki Kobayashi.

Omar Alderete was forced off as the half-time break approached, and Roefs beat away a free-kick from Kajetan Szmyt.

Sunderland went into the break knowing they should have led, but their finishing had again let them down in the absence of Brobbey, their talisman.

Le Bris’ team were ahead within seconds of the restart. Rigg broke through the middle, and the ball was worked to Le Fee, whose cross bounced off a visiting defender on its way to Tutierov at the far post, who headed home.

The lead did not last, with Kamil Jozwiak seizing on a Nilson Reinildo backpass before rounding Roefs to level.

Roefs denied Jozwiak at the hour-mark with a low save as home fans became increasingly frustrated with their team.

A frustrated Le Bris said: ‘It’s hard to take, because we would like to have better football, better expression.’

Sports.title: Europa Fight League! Marseille hooligans descend on Levski Sofia end after 'Nazi salute' - while Besiktas match is SUSPENDED due to pro-Palestine propaganda... and away fans infiltrate Sunderland
Sports.content:
European football has endured another night of chaos with fan trouble at Marseille, Besiktas, and Sunderland.

Fans of Marseille and Levski Sofia clashed violently at their Europa League match, with home hooligans descending on the away end with bats and metal pipes after being provoked by a Nazi salute.

Turkish side Besiktas' clash with Israeli team Hapoel Be'er Sheva was brought to a temporary halt after fans of the former unfurled a pro-Palestinian flag, leading to a clash with police.

And Sunderland's home end was infiltrated by supporters of Jagiellonia Bialystok, who had been banned for the fixture by UEFA - with some of the visitors starting brawls.

The three Europa League disturbances cast another dark shadow over football.

Marseille saw the worst events as an estimated 200-300 home hooligans entered the away end with bats, pipes, and flares.

Marseille's supporters descended on the Levski Sofia end with bats and flares

It is believed that the Marseille ultras were provoked by a Nazi salute by a Levski Sofia fan

One supporter at the Marseille-Levski Sofia match nursed a bleeding head injury

Besiktas fans unfurled a Palestine flag at their fixture against Israeli side Hapoel Be'er Sheva

They had reportedly been provoked by some of Levski's ultras, who have a long association with neo-Nazism, and Marseille's supporters responded with an antifascist chant.

Some people kicked and punched each other - another even used a fire extinguisher, according to L'Equipe.

Bulgarian news agency Bgnes reported that the French hooligans also hurled bottles, flares and firecrackers.

Women and members of Levski's entourage were among the crowd, and several injured supporters had to be escorted out of the stadium, according to reports.

'Olympique de Marseille condemns the incidents that occurred on the sidelines of the match against Levski Sofia,' the hosts said in a statement.

'The swift intervention of the club's security teams restored calm, without affecting the match itself.

'The club is currently working to establish the precise circumstances of these incidents, in conjunction with the relevant authorities.'

Meanwhile, trouble spiked in the 25th minute of Besiktas' 2-1 win over Hapoel Be'er Sheva.

One fan was seen being taken away on a stretcher at the Besiktas game, which was played in Batumi, Georgia

Besiktas full-back Kassoum Ouattara hung the Palestine flag over the advertising hoarding, covering the UEFA lettering

Police had to remove some Jagiellonia Bialystok fans who had infiltrated the home end at Sunderland

The match had been moved to Batumi, Georgia due to security worries surrounding ties between Turkish and Israeli clubs. There was even tension on the pitch, as Besiktas refused to shake hands with their opponents.

After a pro-Palestine banner was revealed by Besiktas' fans, the Georgian police appeared to react with tear gas or pepper spray and batons. One fan was seen being carried away on a stretcher.

The game had to be briefly suspended, with both sets of teams and the officials going to the dressing rooms.

After the match, Besiktas full-back Kassoum Ouattara hung the Palestine flag over the UEFA lettering on the pitchside advertising hoardings.

Besiktas condemned the local police, saying they had used 'disproportionate force'.

The club also wrote: 'Upon learning that security forces were obstructing our fans' entry into the stadium, we immediately contacted the UEFA delegate, who arranged for the stadium's evacuation gates to be opened, allowing our fans to enter the stadium quickly and safely.

'We announce that steps have been taken with our Consulate General in Batumi and UEFA regarding the disproportionate force used by security forces against our fans, and state that we will closely monitor the situation until each of our fans returns safely to our country.'

Turkey and Israel have long been simmering with tension amid the conflict and numerous Turkish clubs such as Galatasaray, Fenerbahce, and Mohamed Salah's Trabzonspor came out in support of Besiktas later - despite usually being bitter rivals.

A UEFA Disciplinary ruling meant Polish club Jagiellonia Białystok weren't meant to have any away supporters at The Stadium of Light for tonight's game at Sunderland, yet plenty of them have turned up in the home end… 🫣😭pic.twitter.com/lRBvHOp16T — Football Away Days (@AwayDaysFB) November 26, 2026

Jagiellonia Bialystok's supporters had been banned - but some bought tickets in the home end

Meanwhile, at the Stadium of Light, events were of a lower scale, but some away fans were seen brawling with the home faithful and police waded in to eject them.

Jagiellonia Bialystok's fans had been banned from attending the game by UEFA following disturbances between them and Levski Sofia fans earlier this month.

But around 20 of them managed to secure tickets, Sunderland believe, and squeeze into the stadium.

The club had already caught some out in advance, writing: 'The club is actively monitoring ticket purchases and has identified and cancelled tickets purchased by, or on behalf of, individuals identified as Jagiellonia supporters.

'All affected tickets will be refunded to the original purchasers.

'This restriction applies across all areas of the stadium, including home sections, and regardless of how tickets have been purchased or transferred.

'Any attempt to circumvent the restriction, including using tickets purchased through third parties or belonging to other supporters, will result in refusal of entry.

'Jagiellonia supporters without a valid entitlement to attend the fixture are strongly advised not to travel to Sunderland.

'No Jagiellonia supporters without valid permission to attend will be permitted entry into the Stadium of Light, and we strongly advise they stay away from the immediate surrounding vicinity.

'The club will continue to work closely with the relevant authorities to ensure UEFA's ruling is fully enforced and that the fixture takes place as a home supporter-only event.'

Sports.title: Paris Fury breaks down in tears over heartbreaking first miscarriage as Tyson reveals he buried the baby in his dad's garden
Sports.content:
Paris Fury breaks down in tears over heartbreaking first miscarriage as Tyson reveals he buried the baby in his dad's garden

Tyson Fury and his wife Paris have opened up about the devastating loss of their baby, with the former heavyweight world champion revealing how he brought their child home from hospital and buried him in the garden at his father's house.

The British boxing star has spoken about the miscarriage in a heartbreaking new Netflix documentary, with Paris breaking down in tears as she relives the moment they discovered they had lost their child.

The couple suffered their first miscarriage in 2014, more than a year before Fury's career-defining victory over Wladimir Klitschko in Dusseldorf. Now, the Gypsy King has revealed the unimaginable grief he was carrying into one of the biggest fights of his life.

In an emotional recollection, Tyson explains how he was able to take his baby son home from hospital, despite it not normally being permitted, before laying him to rest in the garden at his father John's house.

Speaking in the new Netflix documentary, TYSON FURY, Paris said: 'I was expecting my third child so I was at home. Then I got a call from the doctors to say the baby was gone and that I had to born it (give birth to it).

'I kept it quiet because Tyson already had his uncle in the hospital and I didn’t want to add any more pressure. Then it came to this point where there was no viable answer, no more reasons why I couldn’t talk about it.

Tyson Fury and his wife Paris have opened up about the devastating loss of their baby

The British boxing star has spoken about the miscarriage in a heartbreaking new Netflix documentary called TYSON FURY

'I had to go into the hospital and born this baby. I told Tyson. We went through it together. We made the decision to take it home.'

Tyson then recalled the heartbreaking decision to bring their son home and bury him in the garden at his father's house, where he could later visit his grave.

'I remember it all,' Tyson said. 'At that age, they don’t usually let you take them home. I said no, that’s my family, I’ll take it.

'I had this big fancy watch for years ago. It came in this big box, hard wood. Mahogany. The baby was literally this big. And I just took the baby to my dad’s and buried him in the garden. Me and my brothers.'

Paris added: 'I don’t really remember a lot in that week. I remember being at home and seeing the little garden where he was. And, that was that.'

The tragedy came as the Fury family were already enduring an incredibly difficult period, with Tyson's uncle Hughie seriously ill in hospital.

'Hughie was still in hospital,' Tyson said. 'Some days I was thinking he’ll come out of this for sure. He was moving his hands and moving his eyes. He was blinking and stuff.

'Thinking back to that, I can’t remember the day that it was but the family decided that was enough. He had been through enough. So they decided to switch the machine off.'

Tyson and Paris pictured with their family ahead of the launch of At Home with the Furys 2

Tyson explained how Hughie's illness added another layer of heartbreak to an already painful period, particularly with his uncle having been a source of support throughout his boxing career.

'With Hughie I could just nip round and see him. Ask him what I should do in this fight. All the hard work building up to the fight. He missed all the best parts. I’m the one that’s got to be strong.

'I’m the one that has to pretend everything is OK. So that’s the job I took on. Protect and provide and that’s the job men should do.'

Paris admitted that neither of them was able to properly process the loss at the time, with the couple struggling to speak about what had happened.

'We didn’t really talk about what had gone on. I couldn’t talk about it. I couldn’t talk about what happened with me and the baby.

'Even now I just don’t like talking about it. We were both heartbroken. The pain you feel. You can’t imagine it’s going to go away.'

Tyson, meanwhile, revealed how he buried his emotions as he focused on preparing for the biggest challenge of his professional career.

'There was so much s**t going on, so much pain. Just putting it in the back of my mind, back of my mind, back of my mind. Not talking about it.

Tyson said he blocked all of his emotions out as he prepared to fight Wladimir Klitschko

'It was in the deepest darkest locker I could put it in and just lock it away. All those horrible instances. I just put a lock on them because I was preparing for Klitschko.'

But the emotional toll of that period would eventually catch up with the British heavyweight, who went on to produce one of the greatest performances of his career against Klitschko in November 2015 before spiralling into depression.

Travelling to Germany as the underdog, Fury stunned the boxing world by beating the long-reigning Ukrainian on points, ending his 11-year unbeaten reign and claiming the WBA, IBF and WBO heavyweight titles.

Following his triumph in Germany, Fury struggled with depression, anxiety and substance abuse.

Fury's struggles ultimately saw him relinquish his heavyweight world titles, with the boxer later returning to the ring in 2018 after battling his demons and embarking on a remarkable comeback.

Sports.title: George Russell shows true colours with fresh response to F1 rival Max Verstappen
Sports.content:
George Russell shows true colours with fresh response to F1 rival Max Verstappen

Max Verstappen said that George Russell was 'so far below his level' after the pair's long-running feud reared its head at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, reignited by an incident during practice

View 3 Images George Russell wants to do his talking on the track (Image: Karim JAAFAR/AFP via Getty Images)

George Russell says that Max Verstappen's stinging criticism in Las Vegas was 'amusing' - but vowed to keep up the fight against the four-time world champion. Verstappen made headlines by branding Russell 'so far below his level' in a response to the Mercedes driver's inflammatory comments the day before.

‌



‌



Verstappen was also heard laughing on the radio after learning that Russell had crashed into the barriers on the penultimate lap of last weekend's chaotic Grand Prix, which he won from pole position. "Ha ha, well done! My god," the Red Bull star chuckled.

‌



Russell insists that he isn't fazed by Verstappen's comments, telling the media ahead of Sunday's Qatar Grand Prix: "I stand by what I said after practice, but he was the one who went out and won the race and I didn't, and I'm sure he had a bit of a laugh about that and it was reasonably amusing. He drove an incredible race and won it and he can afford to say what he wants."

‌



The 28-year-old added: "We're all competitors out there. There's no right or wrong way about the mentality everybody has.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"We are all different in many regards and you don't need to agree with one another. I'm not looking to be best mates with anybody on the grid. I am just working and looking and fighting to win. Simple as that."

Russell risked Verstappen's wrath during an interview last Friday. The Briton stated that 'somebody has got to stand up to that guy' after the pair made contact in the final practice session, with Verstappen subsequently being given a warning by the stewards for 'driving erratically'.

‌



Las Vegas marked continuation of the duo's long-running feud, with multiple flashpoints since their collision at the 2023 Azerbaijan Grand Prix, after which Verstappen called his rival a 'd***head'. The following year in Abu Dhabi, Russell fired back in extraordinary fashion by labelling his rival a 'bully', who 'lashes out with unnecessary anger and borderline violence'.

Will George Russell ever be on Max Verstappen's 'level'? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

‌



View 3 Images Max Verstappen showed no mercy with his reaction to George Russell's crash (Image: Mark Sutton/Getty Images)

Following his victory in Las Vegas, the Dutchman tore into Russell and quipped that 'karma is a b***h'. "He speaks a lot next to the track, and it doesn't really bother me because he's so far below my level that it doesn't really make any sense for me anyway to try and challenge that, you know?" Verstappen told a post-race press conference.

‌



"And today, karma is a bitch. It was honestly fantastic when I looked in my mirror and I saw what was happening. I was, like, 'Fantastic, my day is only getting better'. And of course, when I then crossed the line in first, my day was complete."

Reflecting on the drama, Russell admitted that he's been too 'honest' when speaking to the media, making it clear that he wants to do his talking on the track. "It's all a bit unnecessary," he added on Thursday.

‌



"It's not something I am looking to continue. I am not looking to have a poor relationship with people. That's not really the kind of person I am.

View 3 Images Max Verstappen and George Russell went wheel-to-wheel in Las Vegas (Image: Rudy Carezzevoli/Getty Images)

‌



"There are lessons to be taken from these situations. Maybe I am just too open and honest with the media. I need to remember I'm talking to a camera that is broadcasting to millions of people. That's the biggest takeaway.

"It is not a war of words off track. I maybe have been guilty of being too open and honest when I speak with you guys. I feel like I have a good relationship with the media and I sometimes forget I am not talking to one person - I am talking to millions of people on the television.

Article continues below

"That good relationship has probably hindered me a bit and that is life lessons. I respect Max immensely for his driving talent and what he has achieved on track."

Sports.title: BBC sports commentator and former England international dies after 11-year health battle
Sports.content:
BBC sports commentator and former England international dies after 11-year health battle

Nigel Starmer-Smith made seven appearances for England between 1969 and 1971

View 2 Images Nigel Starmer-Smith has passed away

Former England scrum-half and BBC broadcaster Nigel Starmer-Smith has died aged 81, his family has confirmed.

‌



‌



Starmer-Smith represented Harlequins and the Barbarians, earning seven caps for England between 1969 and 1971.

‌



Following his retirement from playing, Starmer-Smith transitioned into broadcasting and fronted the BBC's weekly highlights show Rugby Special for 15 years. He received a dementia diagnosis in 2015.

‌



His son Charlie shared on social media: "Dad passed away peacefully this morning after a long battle with dementia. He was (as they say in rugby circles) one of life's great tourists.

Inside the All Blacks: Training habits and motivation as questions asked after England loss READ MORE :

"A rugby player, commentator, editor, writer, raconteur, charity fundraiser, volunteer, speaker, prankster, family man, life and soul of the party but, above all, the greatest father anyone could wish to have.

"He did everything for us and, despite having to bury two of his children at cruelly young ages, both he and my mum refused to let the cavernous holes that Charlotte and Julian left behind define them.

‌



"Just as I choose not to let the cruel condition that robbed him of his ability to communicate (and ultimately of his dignity), define my memories of him.

"He was a modest man, and he'd hate for people to make a fuss. He loved to laugh but not as much as he loved to see others laughing. So for those that knew him think of a happy memory and smile. For that's how I'll remember him."

‌



Alzheimer's Society CEO, Michelle Dyson CB, said: "We are sad to hear that Nigel Starmer-Smith has died, and we send our heartfelt condolences to his family at this difficult time.

View 2 Images Nigel Starmer-Smith during his playing days with Harlequins in 1971

‌



"Dementia was one part of Nigel's story, but, as his son Charlie Starmer-Smith has so movingly said, it should never define the man he was. Both on and off the rugby pitch, it is clear from Charlie's beautiful tribute just how much laughter, love and joy he brought to those around him.

"Inspired by his dad's experience of dementia, Charlie wrote and released the songs Spotlight and Tonight, donating the proceeds to Alzheimer's Society. We are so grateful to him for using his music to raise awareness of the devastating impact dementia can have on the whole family.

Article continues below

"Dementia touches so many of our lives, and we must do everything we can to beat this devastating condition. If you or someone you know needs help, please visit the Alzheimer's Society website – alzheimers.org.uk – or ring our Dementia Support Line – 0333 150 3456."

Sports.title: FA dish out four-match stadium ban after Man Utd vs Aston Villa stoppage time fury
Sports.content:
FA dish out four-match stadium ban after Man Utd vs Aston Villa stoppage time fury

Aston Villa and Manchester United drew 4-4 earlier this month and there was a flashpoint near the tunnel at Old Trafford that involved Villa analyst Victor Manas

View 2 Images Victor Manas admitted the charge, the FA say (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

The FA have announced that Aston Villa analyst Victor Manas has received a four-game ban and been fined £6,000 for his behaviour against Manchester United. The incident happened during stoppage time of the 4-4 draw at Old Trafford on Sunday, November 8.

Villa had just conceded a controversial equaliser in the 96th minute, leaving their coaching staff furious. Unai Emery's side believed that Patrick Dorgu had fouled Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki before scoring the goal.

Manas, a longtime colleague of Emery's, vented his fury towards the match officials. After being removed from the stands by a United steward, the Spaniard was subsequently charged with acting in an improper manner by the FA.

A statement issued on Thursday read: "Victor Manas has been sanctioned for misconduct during Aston Villa's Premier League match against Manchester United on Sunday 8 November.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"It was alleged that at half time, the Villa analyst acted in an improper manner towards the match official(s) around the tunnel area. It was further alleged that he acted in an improper manner towards the match official(s) around the 96th minute of the fixture.

"Victor Manas subsequently admitted the charges. An independent Regulatory Commission imposed a four-match stadium ban, £6,000 fine, and a warning following a hearing, and the written reasons for its decision will be published in due course."

It's not the first time that Manas has been sanctioned by the FA. In 2023, he was slapped with a three-match ban following an altercation with Arsenal coach Miguel Molina. Manas was also suspended for two games last year for his part in a mass brawl during Villa's 3-0 defeat away to Newcastle.

View 2 Images There was significant debate over Manchester United's equaliser (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Manas' anger at United's equalising goal was echoed by Emery. "They score in minute 96, the referee added six minutes. I thought the game was done," the Villa manager fumed post-match. "Angry? Of course. How is to accept to lose in the last minute with two balls. It's difficult.

"The corner is adaptation to the Premier League with Suzuki, the pushing. To accept the two late goals is difficult. How we conceded this last goal, it is adaptation for Suzuki. They are pushing and disturbing him. Other countries, they do not permit it. Here, yes."

Sports.title: It's time to judge Florian Wirtz on his numbers - he's now the Premier League's top creator
Sports.content:
Back in September, Andoni Iraola argued that Florian Wirtz should not be judged solely by his goals and assists at Liverpool.

In an effort to articulate why it was more important that the No.7 was simply the controlling playmaker in a team that had other players firing, Iraola argued: "I am not too focused on numbers."

Over two months later, Germany international Wirtz might be forcing a rethink from his manager given that his contributions are becoming increasingly easier to measure by output in front of goal.

Since the end of the October international Wirtz has eight goals and four assists for club and country and added the latest to his growing catalogue here in this 3-0 win with a wrapped finish that effectively took the game away from Club Brugge, as laid out by The Echo.

‌



With the Belgians knocking on the door at 1-0 to the Reds, the counter-attack involving two-goal Alexander Isak and impressive substitute Rio Ngumoha saw Wirtz fire home from the edge of the box and break the spirit of the likable hosts.

"I think the most important thing is we have the three points," Wirtz said at full time. "It was not the best we've played this season but for phases we played good football.

Black Friday special! Click here to sign up to Mirror+ for just £1 a month!

"It's not easy here, they put pressure on us and we won 3-0 which maybe doesn't show what the game was.

‌



"We are happy and we showed our quality. It was important to get the second goal. It took a while but it was definitely an important goal and then Alex killed it completely then."

National boss Jurgen Klopp has taken ample credit for getting Wirtz back in the groove after a difficult period last term but Iraola deserves the lion's share from the coaching perspective.

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola has played a key role in Florian Wirtz's revival (Image: Richard Martin-Roberts/CameraSport)

The Reds boss has kept faith with the attacking midfielder and ensured that his system is geared towards getting the most from Wirtz as the No.10. There's a reason he has produced a Premier League high 29 chances so far.

‌



"I don't think anyone has ever doubted the quality," Reds legend Steven Gerrard said on TNT Sport's commentary. "It's just been about the confidence and the belief. He's someone who is really affecting games now."

Araujo presence crucial

If Liverpool have generally been a tough nut to crack in the Premier League it had been a different case entirely in the Champions League before Wednesday night.

Much-changed sides had led to a defensive frailty that had seen them ship 10 goals in the four games prior to this clean sheet here at the Jan Breydel Stadium.

‌



But with Jeremie Frimpong restored at right-back in an effort to get some minutes into the legs of the Dutch defender after a month on the shelf, Ronald Araujo shifted over and forged a rock-solid partnership with Jeremy Jacquet in the centre.

Brugge pressed and probed at times, particularly at 1-0 in the second half, but the powerful combination of Araujo and Jacquet ensured Alisson was never overly worked and the chances the hosts created were always manageable.

Araujo currently plays as a right-back in the Premier League but the popular on-loan Barcelona defender is a centre-half by trade and nights like this show his value to the cause at Anfield. It was another tick in the box for those who want the signing to be made permanent at £47m next summer.

Just as importantly, Araujo's presence allowed Virgil van Dijk to have the majority of the night off, which was a timely rest given Everton are next up at Hill-Dickinson Stadium this Sunday. Araujo's warrior-like qualities will be tailor-made for that particular Dockside battle this weekend.

‌



Isak confidence soaring

View 3 Images Alexander Isak is another Liverpool attacker who looks back to his best (Image: Getty Images)

If there was any doubt that Alexander Isak is a player with his tail up once more, the sheer audacity of his finish for Liverpool's third here said it all.

‌



Having raced onto an Alisson Becker punt that travelled some 46 yards - the goalkeeper's fourth assist for the club - Isak had the strength to shrug off his marker before going clean through against goalkeeper Yann Sommer.

Sommer is an experienced Switzerland international who contested the 2025 Champions League with Inter but Isak paid little respect to the Brugge goalkeeper's reputation as he deftly clipped the ball over him when clean through.

It was a finish that indicated the confidence currently coursing through Isak, who has 10 goals in 16 appearances this term.

Isak was signed to essentially replace Mohamed Salah's goals once the legendary Egyptian's time at Anfield was over, so it was fitting that the £125m striker matched his former colleague as the only two Liverpool players of the Premier League era to score in six or more successive away games. Everton might wince at that particular statistic before Sunday's Merseyside derby.

‌



"It's always difficult to say where you are up to but I feel good," Isak said after the game. "I am in a good place and the team is in a good place, that is where we want to be and hopefully it continues from here."

Now up to double figures for the campaign, across all competitions, the next milestone should be 20. He is certainly capable.

Sports.title: Ex-Man Utd star breaks down in tears as wife feared he'd DIED amid sleeping pill addiction
Sports.content:
Ex-Man Utd star breaks down in tears as wife feared he'd DIED amid sleeping pill addiction

Darron Gibson became addicted to sleeping pills during his career and, on one occasion, his wife thought she'd found the former Manchester United midfielder dead

View 2 Images Darron Gibson played at Man Utd under Sir Alex Ferguson but endured mental health struggles and addiction later in his career

The wife for former Manchester United midfielder Darron Gibson thought she'd seen him die following a battle with a sleeping pill addiction.

‌



‌



The Irishman, who also played for Everton, Sunderland and Salford City as well as the Red Devils, had a number of personal battles with mental health. They eventually led him to sleeping pills as he sought a way to turn off from the struggles.

‌



An injury in 2013 whilst on international duty first saw Gibson begin taking the pills - a road that eventually saw him get addicted. At its peak he was taking 14 in a night.

‌



Eight years after first taking them his wife, Danielle, found him following a seizure and thought he had died as the couple opened up in an emotional interview on the RTE’s Howler podcast.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Gibson's wife said: "When the ambulance staff came in, he had blue lips, I thought he had gone. I was being treated for shock. I just thought: 'At least he’s not struggling anymore.' Next minute (sharp intake of breath), he's back."

Reflecting on the near miss Gibson remarked: "Ultimately, if that hadn’t have happened, I wouldn’t be here now" with his wife agreeing he'd likely have died.

‌



During his downward spiral Gibson was convicted of drink driving at 2015 during his spell with Everton. The Premier League side chose not to punish him, and whilst the Irishman appreciates their stance, he wonders whether a tough punishment may have changed his direction.

View 2 Images Darron Gibson and his wife, Danielle, have opened up about his personal battles

‌



He said: "Looking back, who takes five sleeping tablets at 10 in the morning and doesn’t go to sleep? It’s ridiculous. But it’s where I was. It’s what I was doing. I think Everton thought they were looking after me by not punishing me, which I really appreciated at the time. And I don’t blame them for any of this, but I think if they’d punished me, maybe I would have changed. But I didn’t and kept going.'

Three years later at Sunderland he mixed together pills and vodka before crashing into parked cars. He dodged prison time but saw his contract at the Stadium of Light ripped up.

‌



Danielle worked as a specialist in addiction services while Gibson was at Sunderland and insists her husband's issues are not uncommon, suggesting the sport should shoulder more responsibiliy.

"I understand that football is a business. I just think they should have had a duty of care," she said.
