Sports.title: Verstappen to work with new race engineer Tom Hart again at Qatar GP
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen will be without his regular right-hand man Gianpiero Lambiase this weekend at the Lusail International Circuit. Red Bull had already opted for a rotation system for the latter part of this Formula 1 season, primarily to allow Tom Hart to settle into the role ahead of his expected permanent appointment while Lambiase is still with the team.

The initial plan was for Lambiase to cover the final two grands prix of the season as Verstappen's race engineer, besides his duties as Red Bull’s head of racing, but he will be absent in Qatar due to personal circumstances. The team told Autosport that Lambiase is expected to return in Abu Dhabi, provided his personal circumstances allow.

Lambiase is expected to be placed on gardening leave in 2027 ahead of his move to McLaren. While Red Bull has yet to formally announce it, this makes it very likely that Hart will become Verstappen's permanent race engineer as early as the start of the 2027 season.

Hart, who has worked for Red Bull since 2013, was on his way to Williams until Verstappen internally expressed his preference for Hart as Lambiase's replacement. Red Bull subsequently managed to reverse Hart's planned move to the Grove-based team, where he was due to become Alexander Albon's race engineer.

Hart’s first races working with the four-time world champion have presented several challenges. In Austin, there were technical problems with the radio connection, while in Brazil Verstappen repeatedly complained about a strange feeling in the RB22 after his opening stint. A particularly chaotic race unfolded in Las Vegas, although communication between Verstappen and Hart already appeared to be considerably better.

Verstappen has spoken positively about Hart, who he says has made a “good impression” despite those challenges.

How Verstappen has adapted to F1’s energy management demands

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Lars Baron / LAT Images via Getty Images

In Las Vegas, Verstappen was praised for "outsmarting" Mercedes, as Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies put it. Although the Dutchman is still not a fan of the current regulations, he demonstrated his understanding of energy management in his battle with George Russell, whom he repeatedly repassed.

Verstappen’s performance underlined the progress Red Bull has made with its DM01 power unit on energy-poor circuits, but also the extent to which Verstappen played with the tools at his disposal – something that also appeared to represent a step forward compared with the season opener in Melbourne.

“I think we all got better at it, drivers and teams, in understanding the energy management, but that's normal when it's a new regulation,” Verstappen said when asked by Autosport in Qatar which steps he has taken behind the scenes.

“When you look at the first race weekend, I think if we go back, you would do things differently. It would also be bad if you go back and you wouldn't know what to do differently, so it's just normal progression, I would say.”

While Verstappen felt the layout in Las Vegas suited the RB22 well, he expects Qatar to present a different challenge. The Lusail International Circuit is dominated by high-speed corners, an area in which Verstappen says Red Bull has not always been particularly competitive this year.

However, following Red Bull's successful upgrade in Baku, team-mate Isack Hadjar believes the team should now be competitive everywhere.

Sports.title: Hamilton convinced Ferrari will "figure it out" following Leclerc skirmish
Sports.content:
Ferrari driver Lewis Hamilton says he is confident that he and team-mate Charles Leclerc will "figure it out" following their latest on-track skirmish at last week's Las Vegas Grand Prix.

A fortnight on from a costly on-track incident fighting for the lead in Mexico, which drew the ire of team boss Fred Vasseur, history repeated itself when Leclerc was found responsible for contact with Hamilton on the streets of Las Vegas, robbing both drivers of a solid result.

The clash prompted more anger from Vasseur and fresh talks over how he will get his two number one drivers in line. "It's unacceptable," Vasseur fumed after the race. "It's a lack of respect for the team, for the sponsors, the same speech as after Mexico. I think we had a clear discussion in Sao Paulo. Today it wasn't professional."

Speaking in Doha on Thursday ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix, Leclerc said he was "very much thinking about trying to find a solution together with the team in order to make sure that we maximise the team points and that episodes like last week don't happen again" - stopping short of offering any suggestions.

Hamilton also struck a conciliatory tone and said he was still convinced that the pair could co-exist in harmony at the team as joint number one drivers.

"I do, I do. We're going to figure it out," Hamilton said. "We're team-mates at the end of the day, and I think we always learn from these experiences, whilst maybe it doesn't necessarily look like it. But there will be learnings that we take from this difficult period.

"I still believe in everything we're building and working towards in the background. We came here with the goal of taking Ferrari back to the top."

He added: "You learn really through the hardest times. And these are definitely very, very challenging times for Fred and Chares and I. But think these are the moments that you really learn and grow closer together through conversation and communicating and having those sit-downs."

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Manuel Eletto

Hamilton revealed he and Leclerc have gone through every corner and every incident between the pair this year, which also included a clash at Monza. But the seven-time world champion also acknowledged every incident is different and dynamic, so it's not as simple as imposing strict racing rules. Instead, he suggested that he and Leclerc have to use their instinct while keeping the team's interests in the back of their minds.

"You can never cover everything, because every scenario is different," Hamilton explained. "But you can definitely go through every single race, corner by corner, and discuss things, which Charles and I have.

"But there's always going to be something new that you maybe haven't foreseen. You also have to use your instinct, and at the core you always have to have the team.

"Speaking for myself, when I'm driving, when I'm attacking, whoever it is on track, I'm always thinking: 'OK, how is this going to impact everybody behind me, team-wise?' So, I really do try to be as responsible as I can, and make the best decision when I am attacking, I think."

Sports.title: Leclerc furious with integrity being questioned after Hamilton clashes
Sports.content:
Charles Leclerc was left furious by those ‘questioning his integrity and love for Ferrari’ after yet another clash with Formula 1 team-mate Lewis Hamilton - having urged to find a “solution”.

The Ferrari pair have been at loggerheads several times during the second half of the 2026 F1 campaign, clashing at Monza, Zandvoort and Mexico before their latest spat in Las Vegas.

Last weekend Leclerc attempted to overtake Hamilton for sixth down the inside of Turn 7, but copped a 10-second penalty for causing a spin - leaving team boss Fred Vasseur furious.

The Frenchman said on team radio during the cooldown lap: “Charles, I want to see you at the end of the race, before anything else.”

Now a week later in Qatar, Leclerc has accepted responsibility for the “unacceptable” clash but refuted any theory that he is attempting to establish dominance as Ferrari’s number one driver.

“I absolutely have zero clause that says that in my contract,” said Leclerc, who signed a “multi-year” renewal in June. “It's never something that I was interested in and never something that I personally wanted.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Photo by: Colin McMaster / LAT Images via Getty Images

“So no, I don't. I think the only thing that I don't like seeing is people questioning my integrity to the team, my love for the team. I've been in Ferrari since 2019.

“I think there's nothing clearer than the love I have for the team and I'll do absolutely everything in order to bring Ferrari back to the top.

“Then, of course, mistakes happen along the way and always will. We just have to minimise them and particularly between team-mates.

“But yeah, I think it's more the question mark of that that I have seen going around that hurts me more than anything else.

“The rest is a lot of noise and it's not the most enjoyable time, but it's part of the game and I have to accept that.”

Leclerc then insisted that the relationship between him and the seven-time world champion is still “very good”, claiming much of the talk has been heightened due to the nature of driving for Ferrari.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Bryn Lennon / Formula 1 via Getty Images

So the team is striving to find a solution with several internal discussions, which started in the aftermath of the Mexico incident amid Hamilton criticising Leclerc’s “do or die” attitude to racing.

“At least one more year together, we've got to do the best for the team,” said Leclerc, with Hamilton’s current contract expiring at the end of 2027.

“So, I think I've been very much thinking about trying to find a solution together with the team in order to make sure that we maximise the team points and that episodes like last week don't happen again.

“That is my main priority. We're just really very much focused on trying to find a solution that works and particularly because I really believe we are in a good momentum.

“If next year we are to be in a position of fighting for the championship, it's even more important to find the right solution for both of us to bring Ferrari back to the top.”

Leclerc eventually finished 10th in Vegas with Hamilton three spots higher, leaving Ferrari still second in the championship ahead of the final two rounds: Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

Sports.title: Russell stands by Verstappen comments at Las Vegas GP - despite "amusing" reaction
Sports.content:
Two years after their last major spat around this time of the year, George Russell and Max Verstappen clashed again last week in Las Vegas after an impeding incident in free practice. It infuriated the Briton, with Verstappen ruining the Mercedes driver's lap by passing him into the last corner - an unwritten rule that the Dutchman doesn't tend to mind breaking.

Russell responded by sending his car up the inside, pushing Verstappen off.

The end result was a needless, though moderately entertaining spat at this quiet time of the season, reprise of Verstappen's and Russell's off-track rivalry.

"He does this week in week out with many drivers and everybody accepts it, and I'm not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they're bigger and better than everyone else. Somebody's got to stand up to that guy," Russell said.

So, when Russell sent his Mercedes into the wall while trying to pass team-mate Kimi Antonelli, right behind leader Verstappen, the four-time world champion couldn't hide his glee post-race. "He speaks a lot next to the track," he said. "And honestly, for me, it doesn't really matter because he's so far below my level that it doesn't really make any sense for me anyway, to try and challenge that. So, it doesn't bother me. And today, karma is a bitch."

A few days on, tempers have cooled and while Russell may not win too many mind games against the steely Dutchman, he stands by what he said.

"I found some of the comments post-race quite amusing, but at the end of the day, he drove an incredible race and won it, so he can afford to say what he wants, really," Russell mused when grilled on the topic.

"At the end of the day, I guess I stand by what I said after practice, but he was the one who went out and won the race. I didn't.

"How I responded on track would have been the same if it was any driver, because if you're going into the last corner, preparing for your lap, if somebody does overtake you into that corner, your next lap is screwed.

"So you either have a decision just to try and retake the position and start your lap like normal or just accept you're going to lose that next lap because you're too close to the car in front."

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Lars Baron / LAT Images via Getty Images

'My risk dial is too great'

Russell could have responded on-track instead, by winning the race as he and Verstappen battled lap after lap as part of an oval-like overtaking bonanza. But having fallen behind Antonelli, Russell took too big a risk trying to overtake the world champion on the dirty inside of Turn 4 and veered into the wall.

The Briton admitted he is so eager for a big result at the end of the season that he's probably taking too many risks to try and get one more morale-boosting win after what has been a brutal campaign.

"Obviously, my mistake in Vegas came when I was trying to overtake my team-mate," he said. "I think the truth is my risk dial is probably a bit too great at the moment because I'm just kind of wanting to go for these big results and get some highlights on the board towards the end of the season.

"If that was race one of the season, there's no way I would have gone for that move with two laps remaining. But with two races to go in the season, I kind of wanted to go for it.

"It wasn't out of any frustration. It was just willing to risk more to get a victory. Was it a mistake in hindsight? Yes. But as I mentioned, I could have been conservative and I'm confident I would have finished third or second. And I probably would have been frustrated with myself that I didn't go for the move."

Reflecting on his latest spat with Verstappen, Russell suggested he had been too open with the media in saying what he thinks, which he says is his "biggest takeaway" from the whole episode.

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Jim Watson / AFP via Getty Images

"Maybe I have been guilty of being just too open and honest," he added. "I feel with all of the media and the journalists I have a good relationship with and you sometimes forget that you're not talking to one person.

"I'm talking to millions of people on the television, so I think that good relationship has actually probably hindered me a little bit. And that's, I guess, life lessons in this world we live in.

"The competition is on track and that's where I want to have the battles. I respect Max immensely for his driving talents and everything he's achieved on track. And that's that, really.

"I'm not looking to have poor relationships with people. That's just not really the type of person I am."

Sports.title: F1 2027 grid: Who will be racing and where?
Sports.content:
The 2027 Formula 1 grid is now complete following the announcement from Haas that it has retained star youngster Oliver Bearman.

But the American squad is also the only team that is altering its driver pairing for next season, as many potentially enthralling storylines failed to materialise.

So, here’s a look at the situation.

George Russell, Mercedes, Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Toto Wolff, Mercedes Photo by: Hector Vivas / Formula 1 via Getty Images

The 2026 season has witnessed a significant shift in the dynamic down at Mercedes between Kimi Antonelli and George Russell, as the latter headed into the year as the heavy title favourite - only to fall flat early on.

It came after Russell finished 169 points ahead of Antonelli last season in what was a very up-and-down rookie campaign for the Italian, while the Briton arguably delivered his best yet. So, with Mercedes expected to master the regulation switch, which it did, Russell was the natural favourite yet Antonelli learned his lessons impressively fast to vastly improve upon 2025.

This eventually led to the 20-year-old becoming F1’s youngest ever world champion by securing his maiden title at the Mexico Grand Prix, with four rounds still to play at the time. Although this came as a surprise to many, Mercedes would have argued that his performances had been as forecast when it plucked him from karting and into its junior programme.

Read Also: Formula 1 How Antonelli rose so rapidly to become F1 world champion

As for Russell, his season has been a “complete disaster” - per Max Verstappen - and with two grands prix left in 2026, he sits fourth in the standings and could easily drop to fifth as he is level on points with 2025 world champion Lando Norris.

Nevertheless, he will remain with Mercedes for 2027 with his and Antonelli’s fate known for quite some time.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Colin McMaster / LAT Images via Getty Images

Ferrari and Charles Leclerc agreed upon a new deal earlier in 2026 - announced in June - meaning the 29-year-old is continuing his length association with the Italian outfit. Leclerc joined its junior programme in 2016, made his F1 debut with customer squad Alfa Romeo Sauber in 2018 before moving to the works’ outfit in 2019.

The Monegasque has won nine grands prix in that time, which can be seen as a disappointment considering the promise displayed early on. But with Ferrari’s improved performance in 2026, jumping from fourth to second in the championship, Leclerc’s hope is that the team can press on and finally deliver a championship-winning car having signed a multi-year contract.

But he will have Lewis Hamilton to worry about in the neighbouring garage, as the seven-time world champion is understood to be under contract until the end of 2027 after joining in 2025. Last year was a disappointment for the Briton, finishing 86 points behind Leclerc, but he’s strengthened in 2026 with a 17-point advantage over his team-mate.

Tensions have also been high recently, with the two colliding on various occasions, most notably Monza, Mexico and Las Vegas, so that is a dynamic Ferrari must manage heading into 2027.

Oscar Piastri, McLaren, Lando Norris, McLaren Photo by: Clive Rose / Formula 1 via Getty Images

It was known that at one stage Verstappen held some level of talks with McLaren when his Red Bull future was up in the air. Though this simply may have been a tactic to secure a more lucrative deal with the Austrian outfit, which is something he eventually earned, so McLaren is remaining with Norris and Oscar Piastri.

The Briton seems content with being a one-team man for the time being, staying with McLaren since his debut in 2019, and why not? Norris has secured that world title he so strived for and has been impressive in 2026 with three victories, even if the car hasn’t been quite there on several occasions.

As for Piastri, what happens with him is an on-and-off talking point given the Australian would have likely been the man to move had Verstappen joined. This year has been a disappointment for him, continuing on from his late title collapse in 2025, as he is seventh in the standings and 97 points behind Norris. His most recent victory was Zandvoort in August last year.

But he is on a “multi-year contract”, signed in 2025, and looks set to stay for now.

Red Bull: Max Verstappen, Isack Hadjar

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Manuel Eletto

The 2026 season has been quite similar to 2025 for Red Bull, having started quite slowly before a late rejuvenation with Verstappen enjoying four wins and nine podiums since this year’s summer break.

That has vaulted him into second in the drivers’ standings and should he carry such momentum into 2027, then a fifth world title could easily be on the way for the Dutchman. That would put him one short of Hamilton’s record for the most championships with one team - he achieved six at Mercedes - as Verstappen signed a bumper deal until at least 2030 this year.

It will see him start a second season alongside Isack Hadjar, who has had a solid first campaign at Red Bull and gave the team no reason to replace him. Perhaps the team now has its ideal number two driver to assist Verstappen in his title charge next year.

Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls, Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls Photo by: Rudy Carezzevoli / Getty Images

The situation down at Red Bull’s sister outfit was one of the biggest sources of uncertainty, given it was only in November that Racing Bulls confirmed its pairing for 2027. It will be an unchanged duo, however, as Arvid Lindblad will return for his second season in F1 alongside Liam Lawson, whose seat was in doubt despite his best year yet.

Lawson is on course for a career-best ninth in the standings with 89 points, securing a top 10 finish at all but six grands prix, which in itself is enough for the Faenza outfit to secure its highest-ever constructors’ championship finish of fifth.

But Red Bull junior Nikola Tsolov has impressed as an F2 rookie this year, sitting second to Rafael Camara, and historically Racing Bulls doesn’t keep drivers for long if a promotion to the main squad isn’t on the cards.

With 2027 going to be Lawson’s third proper season at Racing Bulls, historically the team may have dropped him in favour of its next protege. Tsolov, however, will have to settle for a reserve driver role in 2027 while Lindblad continues to perform, taking 38 points from his rookie year so far and 11th in the standings.

Pierre Gasly, Alpine Photo by: Lars Baron / LAT Images via Getty Images

Pierre Gasly signed a contract extension with Alpine last year, demonstrating his commitment to the cause despite the team being adrift at the back of the constructors' order across 2025. The arrival of Flavio Briatore, Steve Nielsen, and Mercedes has put the team back into the midfield battle, and the Frenchman is hoping that the Enstone squad can deliver a car worthy of his immense - and oft-underrated - talent.

Gasly is 10th in the 2026 standings with 52 points, helping Alpine sit sixth in the constructors’ championship and although he’s the French outfit’s clear number one driver, Franco Colapinto has still made a considerable step.

The Argentine has taken 35 points in 2026, compared to zero last year, and that earned him a new deal in August for 2027.

Haas: Oliver Bearman, Rafael Camara

Oliver Bearman, Haas F1 Team, Rafael Camara, Haas F1 Team Photo by: Bryn Lennon / Formula 1 via Getty Images

Haas is another squad to have endured serious question marks surrounding its driver pairing for next year. The first concerned Esteban Ocon, who just couldn’t make things click ever since he joined the American outfit from Alpine for 2025.

At the time he was seen as a real coup, the first grand prix winner to drive for Haas, but instead he was consistently outperformed by his much more inexperienced team-mate - Bearman - across both last year and 2026.

In the end things turned quite ugly and after it being confirmed that the 198-time grand prix starter wouldn’t continue into 2027, he was dismissed by Haas with five rounds still to play in the season.

His replacement is F2 championship leader Camara, who has signed a “multi-year” deal and given up his title ambitions in the feeder series to finish the season in F1 before his first, full campaign in 2027.

That will come alongside Bearman, who has mightily impressed in his time at Haas so far. Although the Briton was all but certain to continue with Haas into 2027, his announcement came rather late as Bearman's camp was looking for long-term assurances ahead of his third season at Haas on loan from Ferrari.

Gabriel Bortoleto, Audi F1 Team, Nico Hulkenberg, Audi F1 Team Photo by: Guido De Bortoli / LAT Images via Getty Images

Audi F1 boss Mattia Binotto confirmed in September that it will retain Nico Hulkenberg and Gabriel Bortoleto for the 2027 season. At the time it didn’t really cause any particular conversations because the announcement came as little surprise, considering how well both drivers have done - thus giving Audi no reason to change its line-up.

The German marque, which made his F1 debut in 2026 after taking over from Sauber, has the perfect blend of youth and experience, plus a harmonious relationship between the pair.

Bortoleto is set for his third season in the championship, compared to Hulkenberg’s 16th, and both drivers have scored 14 points this year to give Audi eighth in the standings.

Alexander Albon, Williams, Carlos Sainz, Williams Photo by: Peter Fox / Getty Images

Williams' decision to lock in Alex Albon and Carlos Sainz for at least another year demonstrates the buy-in for its long-term ambitions from both drivers, even if this season has presented a step back in fortunes. Some might uncharitably suggest that there was nowhere else for either driver to go, which is probably also true, but the retention of both drivers is a significant boost for the team.

Had Sainz decided to do something else, Williams is said to have hedged its bets and had spoken to the management of Sergio Perez and Colapinto for 2027, while Luke Browning has also impressed in his FP1 outings with the team.

Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing, Lance Stroll, Aston Martin Racing Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

The situation at Aston Martin was another which promised potential drama for 2027 but failed to materialise as such. That is because for months the questions surrounding Fernando Alonso’s future were strife, considering he is 45 years old, driving for a backmarker and heavily dislikes the current regulations with his previous contract expiring at the end of 2026.

But all speculation stopped in September when the two-time champion announced his extension with Aston Martin into 2027. It is believed that him not publicly committing to F1 through the summer months was partly an effort to put pressure on the series to make changes.

As for team-mate Lance Stroll, his extension into 2027 arrived on the same day as Alonso, but was far from the same talking point considering father Lawrence owns the team. So, the 28-year-old Canadian, who next season will have had a decade in F1, effectively has a contract for as long as he likes.

Cadillac: Sergio Perez, Valtteri Bottas

Valtteri Bottas, Cadillac, Sergio Perez, Cadillac Photo by: Bryn Lennon / Formula 1 via Getty Images

F1 newcomer Cadillac was the final squad to hold intrigue surrounding its driver pairing for 2027. Said intrigue didn’t really concern Sergio Perez, who in October signed a multi-year extension, but more Valtteri Bottas.

The 10-time grand prix winner has been outperformed by Perez this year, with a losing 16-10 head-to-head record in qualifying (including sprints), causing his seat to be thrown in doubt. Team management refused to publicly commit to him for some time as it weighed up the possibility of promoting reserve driver Colton Herta, given its desire to have an American driver racing for an American team.

One sticking point for Herta was his lack of an FIA Superlicence - required to compete in F1 - despite winning nine races in IndyCar. But he eventually obtained one via six FP1 appearances this year, yet that still wasn’t enough to grab an F1 seat with his highly disappointing F2 season, sitting 19th in the standings, in mind.

So, in November Cadillac announced its decision to stick with Bottas for 2027.

F1 2027 grid

Sports.title: Alonso to not let his age determine F1 retirement
Sports.content:
Fernando Alonso says he will quit Formula 1 when he feels slow and he doesn’t need to be as fit as a football player to be competitive.

Alonso is the most experienced driver in F1’s history, having competed in 23 seasons from 2001 to 2026, and the two-time champion has maintained his involvement well beyond his peers’ retirement age despite his current 245-race winless streak.

“Motorsport is a very unique sport in that regard,” the 45-year-old said. “You don't rely so much on your fitness to perform at the highest level. You are not a tennis or football player where you need to run all the time. You rely a lot on your technical environment.

“Of course, you still need to be fit and motivated, but at the end of the day I don't see anyone superior on the track. I don't feel that I've lost speed, or lost my reflexes at a race start, or lost motivation to come to the next grand prix.

“Some people say that the younger generation need a spot in F1 and drivers like myself and Lewis [Hamilton] need to move on because we've been on the grid so long, but motorsport doesn't work like that. I will stop when I feel slow, not when my passport says I'm this age or that age.”

Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

Alonso did clarify that he definitely wouldn’t be around when V8 engines return in 2030, and this may not be unrelated to his new role as a parent.

“That's been the toughest thing,” he said of spending so much time away from home. “Many nights this year, I've found myself wondering if I'm missing important moments.

“I think about the race team, too. My number-one mechanic and his partner had a boy three years ago, and they will have another child soon.

“Before I became a father, I probably didn't fully understand how much it meant to those who have children and how difficult it was to be away from them so often, but now I completely understand.

“And I think about them because they work harder than me. They spend more hours than I do at the circuit. They travel one or two days earlier than me, they travel one or two days after me back home, but they're always working hard, still motivated.

“Seeing that has helped me understand I'm a privileged part of the team and makes me want to work even harder together with them.”

Sports.title: Haas finally announces Bearman for F1 2027
Sports.content:
Oliver Bearman will officially stay at Haas for the 2027 Formula 1 season after he and the team finally put pen to paper on a new deal.

The American squad announced the renewal on Thursday, meaning the 21-year-old Briton will partner Brazilian rookie Rafael Camara at Haas next season.

It means the 2027 grid is now complete ahead of the final two rounds of the 2026 campaign, one in which Bearman has shone with 23 of Haas' 31 points.

Team boss Ayao Komatsu said: "Continuing with Ollie into 2027 was a natural decision for us.

"We’ve seen his growth, his commitment, and the quality he brings to the team, both on and off the track.

"He has a tremendous work ethic and a strong desire to develop both himself and the team, and there is no better person, in my opinion, to lead this team forward.

Ayao Komatsu, Haas Photo by: Lars Baron / LAT Images via Getty Images

"TGR Haas F1 Team has one of the most exciting driver pairings on the grid, and I look forward to seeing Ollie flourish further with this incredible team."

Next season will be Bearman's third, full campaign in F1, although he did make three appearances in 2024 - his debut for Ferrari in Jeddah, before outings in Baku and Sao Paulo for Haas.

"It’s no secret that I’m delighted to be continuing with TGR Haas F1 Team into 2027," said Bearman.

"This team has played an integral role in my development, and I’ve felt a huge amount of belief and support from everyone here.

"We’ve got big ambitions to keep pushing forward, and I’m excited to lead that work, building on what we’ve achieved, and striving for even more together – we have unfinished business."

Although this news comes late into the season, the Ferrari protege was always going to stay with Haas, which has loaned him from the Scuderia since his rookie year.

Oliver Bearman, Haas Photo by: Joe Portlock / Getty Images

But as he is entering year three with the American squad, Bearman's camp also wanted assurances about his long-term future - with driving for Ferrari being his ultimate goal.

Bearman's camp is also believed to have been looking for a significant pay increase, considering he's become Haas' lead driver after outperforming the now ousted Esteban Ocon.

At last week's Las Vegas Grand Prix, Bearman admitted he was "quite disappointed" that "I'm sitting here at round 20 without a contract signed for next year. It's been a strange situation, but we're getting there."

He now heads into Qatar this weekend with that new deal ahead of the Abu Dhabi finale, as Haas attempts to hold off Audi in the battle for seventh with three points separating them.

Sports.title: Williams breaches F1 2025 cost cap, Alpine guilty of procedural violation
Sports.content:
Williams and Alpine have fallen foul of Formula 1's 2025 cost cap, reaching an Accepted Breach Agreement with the FIA, with Williams incurring a sporting penalty for overspending and Alpine handed a fine.

The FIA announced on Wednesday that Williams overspent the 2025 cost cap by £627,000 or 0.48%. The overspend was found to be unintentional through the way the team interpreted the financial regulations, which meant it had committed what is called a "Minor Overspend Breach and a Procedural Breach".

The FIA's cost cap administration offered Williams an Accepted Breach Agreement (ABA), which the team accepted. The governing body noted the team "acted cooperatively and in good faith" and concluded that Williams did not attempt to seek a sporting advantage.

Nevertheless, the FIA handed Williams both a financial and sporting penalty. Alongside paying the FIA an undisclosed fine and reimbursing the cost cap administration expenses, Williams will be docked 1.5% reduction in wind tunnel and CFD testing over the next 12 months.

In a statement the team explained it had made an error while reorganising its team structure, believing some of its administrative costs fell outside the cost cap.

"The breach relates to administrative costs we incurred making changes to our company structure. We believed these costs fell outside of the cap," a Williams spokesperson said. "Following discussions with the FIA, we have agreed to resolve the matter in line with their interpretation that the costs should have been in cap.

Carlos Sainz, Williams Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

"The FIA has noted that Williams did not gain any sporting or financial advantage, and nor did we ever seek to. It has also noted that we acted cooperatively and in good faith throughout the review process.

"Integrity is central to what Williams stands for, and we can now close this case and remain focused on our future. We have always been and will continue to be strong supporters of the Cost Cap, which naturally requires accurate policing to be effective."

Autosport understands Williams will receive a 1.5% hit on the maximum number of wind tunnel runs and CFD hours allowed across the second half of this season and the first half of 2027. That's against a 105% baseline for the current period, based on the team being eighth in the championship at the previous measuring point, and a 1.5% ATR hit against a 110% baseline for the following period, assuming Williams stays ninth in the standings until Abu Dhabi.

It means the Grove team respectively sees its number of wind tunnel hours reduced from 336 to 331 for the remainder of the current period, and from 352 to 347 for the first half of next year.

Alpine handed fine for procedural breach

Alpine was fined for a "Procedural Breach", which meant it did not actually overspend the 2025 cap but included a number of inaccuracies in its financial reporting.

Alpine wrongly excluded a number of non-sporting costs, including marketing and HR costs.

Pierre Gasly, Alpine Photo by: Steven Tee / LAT Images via Getty Images

As a result, Alpine will also be handed a fine while reimbursing the cost cap administration expenses. As is the case with Williams, the size of Alpine's fine was not disclosed, although similar offences are usually thought to be fined somewhere between $300,000 and $500,000.

"BWT Alpine Formula One Team acknowledges and accepts the findings of the Cost Cap Administration (CCA) for the 2025 Reporting Period," the team stated. "The team accepts that it unknowingly committed a Procedural Breach, which is a result of inaccuracies in the Full Year Reporting Documentation for costs related to exclusions and adjustments.

"The errors and inaccuracies in the reporting were specifically related to non-sporting and operational costs which the CCA recognised didn’t give the team any performance advantage, such as Marketing Activities, non-F1 Activities, HR Activities, Employee’s Bonus Costs, Offsetting of Costs, and Costs of Inventories.

"The team would also like to express its thanks to both the CCA and FIA, for its diligence and understanding throughout the entire process. The Financial Regulations are still relatively new, constantly evolving and complex, with some exclusions and adjustments being open to each team’s interpretation. The team acknowledges the collective efforts it needs to make across the business and recognises where improvements can be made in future."

Sports.title: Leclerc denies claim he has a ‘number one’ clause in his Ferrari contract | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Charles Leclerc has denied he has a clause in his contract guaranteeing him number one status at Ferrari.

The claim was made in a report following the Las Vegas Grand Prix and has been widely shared on social media. Leclerc stated he did not have such a clause in his current contract.

“I normally never disclose what I have in my contract but I think this one is an important one to speak about,” he said. “I absolutely have zero clause that says that in my contract.

“It’s never something that I was interested in and never something that I personally wanted. So, no, I don’t.”

The claim was made by Rebecca Clancy, who spent 10 years as Formula 1 correspondent for The Times before joining Motorsport Network. She now contributes to the BBC’s F1 coverage.

“Certain drivers, like Charles Leclerc, they want that number one status, they have had it written into their contracts as well,” she said. “Whether or not the team would miss it or not is a different thing, but they get it written into their contract.

“Max Verstappen is another one, he is obviously the number one driver. He couldn’t care less either.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Leclerc joined Ferrari in 2019 and last extended his contract to drive for the team in June.

He was penalised for colliding with his team mate Lewis Hamilton at the last round in Jeddah. Despite the criticism he faced over the incident – his second penalty for an incident involving his team mate in two rounds – Leclerc said he is committed to putting Ferrari back on top.

“The only thing that I don’t like seeing is people questioning my integrity to the team, my love for the team,” he said. “I’ve been at Ferrari since 2019. I think there’s nothing clearer than the love I have for the team, and I will do absolutely everything in order to bring Ferrari back to the top.

“Of course, mistakes happen along the way and always will. We just try to minimise them, and particularly between team-mates.”

He said claims he isn’t committed to the team “hurt me more than anything else” but “the rest is a lot of noise.”

“It’s not the most enjoyable time, but it’s part of the game and I have to accept that,” he added.

Ford has revealed the GT41 Hypercar which will compete the World Endurance Championship next year.

Like the GT40, with which Ford won the Le Mans 24 Hours every year from 1966 to 1969, the GT41 takes its name from the chassis’ height in inches.

It uses a 5.4-litre V8 producing around 670bhp, which Ford says will push the car to a top speed of around 354kph (220mph).

Sports.title: “We need to find another solution” to Ferrari driver clashes, admits Leclerc | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Charles Leclerc accepts Ferrari needs to improve how its drivers interact on-track following his latest clash with his team mate in Las Vegas.

The stewards penalised Leclerc for knocking Lewis Hamilton into a spin during the race. It was the second time in three rounds the Ferrari drivers have badly disadvantaged each other.

However Leclerc was reluctant to reveal what has been discussed between the pair and Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur.

“I’m not going to disclose that,” said Leclerc. “I’m not allowed to anyway, so I cannot go into the detail of that.”

The trio held discussions after they tangled in the Mexican Grand Prix, opening the door for Max Verstappen to beat them to victory. However Leclerc said it was clear this had failed to solve the problem.

“We are speaking about a solution to that. Lewis and I already talked. I think our off-track relationship is really strong but at the same time it happened again in Las Vegas and before that moment there were other moments as well. And so for that, we need to find another solution. That’s all I can say.”

He admitted the Las Vegas incident was “unacceptable” for Ferrari.

“As a team, we cannot afford clashes between team mates. I think that is very clear for everyone.

“For the clash in particular of Las Vegas, as I said, I took responsibility. I think there’s just tension around that we just need to dissipate and make sure that we look at more positive days in the future. That’s all I’m looking for.

“But I do agree it’s unacceptable that both Ferraris clash together, of course.”

Sports.title: Hadjar says unfortunate timing caused his front wing to “explode” in Las Vegas | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Isack Hadjar says Red Bull are reinforcing the design of their car’s front wing after his failed during the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

The Red Bull driver believes his failure occured as he switched his wings to the closed position while approaching turn five. This coincided with him running over a bump.

“I think it’s just unfortunate timing,” Hadjar explained. “I think the moment I was closing SM {Straight Mode], the moment of the bump, I think just everything timed it perfectly so the front wing couldn’t take it.

“The team has been working on that for the weekend, reinforcing it. We should have enough for that not to happen, so it’s still going under investigation.

“But collapsing by itself is definitely extremely not what I want here, for sure. They are working hard on it.

“I really believe if I had closed that system two-tenths earlier it would not have happened. I just think everything aligned so it would explode at that time, which is just very unfortunate.”

The Red Bull driver was running in second place when the Safety Car was deployed in Las Vegas, prior to his front wing failure. He believes he is getting closer to winning a race.

“But I believe that now Max [Verstappen] has won four races in that second half, it just shows how good the car is behaving.

“On my side, if I just keep doing what I’m doing, I just believe it’s going to happen. I’m still pushing very hard, I have two more races.

Sports.title: Russell “amused” by Verstappen’s comments in Las Vegas: “I stand by what I said” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
George Russell was “amused” by Max Verstappen saying he is “so far below my level” following their clash at the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

The pair tangled in practice earlier in the weekend. The stewards gave Verstappen a formal warning for the collision and Russell remarked afterwards: “somebody’s got to stand up to that guy.”

Verstappen won the race while Russell fell to ninth place after skidding off the track while trying to pass his team mate Andrea Kimi Antonelli. Afterwards Verstappen said it was “honestly fantastic” to see Russell retire from the race. “Karma is a bitch,” he added.

Russell made light of Verstappen’s response. “It was quite amusing, I found, some of the comments post-race,” he said. “But at the end of the day he drove an incredible race and won it so he can afford to say what he wants really and from my side, moving on.”

The Mercedes driver said he hadn’t changed his view that Verstappen tries to intimidate his rivals on the track. “I stand by what I said after practice,” he said.

“But he was the one who went out and won the race. I didn’t, and I’m sure he had a bit of a laugh about that, and that was reasonably amusing. So from my side, just new race weekend, try and focus on the driving, and move on.”

Nonetheless Russell said he does not want a “war of words” and indicated he may choose his words more carefully in the future when speaking to broadcasters and journalists.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“I maybe have been guilty of being just too open and honest when I speak with you [media] guys. I feel with all of the media and the journalists I have a good relationship.

“You sometimes forget that you’re not talking to one person. We’re having a conversation now and you forget that, actually, I’m not really talking to you, I’m talking to millions of people on the television.

“So I think that good relationship has actually probably hindered me a little bit, and that’s, I guess, life lessons in this world we live. But the competition is on-track, and that’s where I want to have the battles, that’s why I want to have the fights. I respect Max immensely for his driving talent and everything he’s achieved on track, and that’s that.”

However he made it clear he isn’t interested in improving his relationship with Verstappen. “I don’t think it’s important to have a good relationship or no relationship in that regard to be honest,” he said. “We’re all fighting for race wins.”

Having lost the drivers’ championship to his team mate, Russell said he was prepared to take more risks to win the final rounds of the season. “Obviously my mistake in Vegas came when I was trying to overtake my team mate.

“I think the truth is my risk dial is probably bit too great at the moment because I’m just kind of wanting to go for these big results and get some highlights on the board towards the end of the season. If that was race one of the season there’s no way I would have gone for that move with two laps remaining, but with two races to go in the season, I kind of wanted to go through.

Sports.title: Haas finally confirms Bearman’s new contract for 2027 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Oliver Bearman will continue to drive for Haas in 2027, the team has confirmed.

Haas has not indicated Bearman’s new deal will last beyond next season.

The Ferrari junior driver will spend a third consecutive season at the team. Haas is a Ferrari power unit customer and Bearman’s team mate will be Rafael Camara, who is also part of the Italian manufacturer’s young driver programme.

Bearman said last week he was “disappointed” the team hadn’t clarified his situation for next year. He said some team members had been “questioning why [I] haven’t been announced yet.”

Team principal Ayao Komatsu said it had been “a natural decision” to retain Bearman. He has become the team’s most senior driver following its split from Esteban Ocon. Beraman’s former team mate was already due to leave the team at the end of the year, then was unexpectedly dropped mid-way through the Mexican Grand Prix weekend.

Komatsu said Bearman is clearly ready to lead Haas. “We’ve seen his growth, his commitment, and the quality he brings to the team, both on and off the track,” he said. “He has a tremendous work ethic and a strong desire to develop both himself and the team, and there is no better person, in my opinion, to lead this team forward.”

Bearman said he is pleased to continue driving for Haas. “This team has played an integral role in my development and I’ve felt a huge amount of belief and support from everyone here,” he said.

Haas’s announcement means the 2027 Formula 1 grid is complete. Haas will be the only team to start next season with a different driver line-up to the start of this year.

Sports.title: Spotlight: F1 has ‘more people who look like the fans’ due to diversity push – Hamilton | Brief

Lewis Hamilton says Formula 1 has made clear progress bringing in people from more diverse backgrounds over the past five years.

Sports.title: UK Boxing Pundits Worry Saudi Gravy Train Is Stopping
Sports.content:
All-expenses-paid trips to Riyadh are becoming scarce, and some in the British boxing media worry the Saudi gold rush is running dry.

Ade Oladipo and Gareth A. Davies are remembering when they had it good during the brief two-year span from 2023 to 2025, when UK commentators got used to the red-carpet treatment of traveling to Saudi Arabia for big events.

“It felt like we were out there every week. Like we were in the sky on the way to Riyadh every single week for these big cards that you never thought were going to stop,” Oladipo said on talkSPORT Boxing.

Those big events have largely disappeared, leaving Ade and Gareth wondering if Turki Alalshikh will close up shop for UK fighters after Tyson Fury (36-2-1, 25 KOs) fights Anthony Joshua (30-4, 27 KOs) on December 11. You kind of knew it would end sooner or later, with wealthy, underperforming fighters doing the minimum to win and events that failed to attract PPV buys.

Oladipo harped about it being six or seven months since he was flown out to Riyadh, saying he was not even sent over for Canelo Alvarez’s fight against Christian Mbilli on October 31. That was an expensive event for fans, who had to pay $79.99 in the U.S. and £24.99 in the UK.

Not Built for U.S. Fans

Gareth questioned whether the British media are now “at the close of a particular era” when the Fury vs. Joshua event concludes in Cardiff. For Riyadh Season, that would be them finishing with a bang, but only because they are giving UK fans the fight they wanted, not because it is a matchup that non-Brits want to see.

If this is it for Turki and Riyadh Season, it is not a great deal for Americans, watching two heavyweights 10 years past their prime fight it out for the vacant WBA Super belt.

Riyadh Season Did Not Leave Boxing

Turki has not stopped spending money on the sport entirely. Instead, he is putting money into Zuffa events, which are less costly than massive cards like Canelo Alvarez vs. Terence Crawford and Fury vs. Joshua.

The difference is that Zuffa cards involve less well-known fighters who put on surprisingly more entertaining fights than the well-paid superstars. What those fights have shown is that Zuffa does not have to pay huge money to get good action.

For the last three years, British promoters leaned on Saudi budgets to bail out domestic matchups that could not sell on UK pay-per-view alone. If Saudi money disappears for average British cards in 2027, UK promoters will have to pay fighters based on what they actually bring in for ticket and PPV sales. It is going to be a shock for British promoters to go back to the old ways of putting events together.

Sports.title: Dmitry Bivol Puts Canelo Alvarez Rematch Odds At Five Percent
Sports.content:
Dmitry Bivol doubts that Canelo Alvarez will fight him again, rating it as just a 5% chance. Both Canelo and his trainer, Eddy Reynoso, said last month they want to fight Bivol or Terence Crawford next, following Canelo’s win over Christian Mbilli on October 31. Interestingly, Bivol says his team has never received any offer from Canelo for a rematch.

Bivol (25-1, 12 KOs) is defending his IBF, WBA, and WBO light heavyweight titles next month against Callum Smith (31-2, 22 KOs) in Ekaterinburg, Russia, at the UMMC Arena.

“To be honest, I’m feeling like on 5% it could happen,” Bivol told The Stomping Ground. “Yeah. Just kind of past that.”

Canelo lost a 12-round unanimous decision to Bivol in May 2022 in Las Vegas. Despite the close scorecards, the fight was one-sided. Bivol dominated Canelo with combinations and in-and-out movement.

“Well, look, I would like an immediate rematch with Crawford. Hopefully, Crawford can return to boxing, which I think he already said he might come back, and I would like the rematch with him. And if that is not possible, someday also have a rematch with Bivol,” said Eddy Reynoso to Fight Hub TV Español.

Saudi Funding And U.S. Box Office Reality

The lack of movement on a rematch with Bivol may not be entirely Canelo’s fault. For the fight to happen, the Saudis would need to finance it. Canelo is signed with Turki Alalshikh and Riyadh Season and is being paid well, reportedly in the hundreds of millions, with his per-fight purses being large.

Unless Riyadh is willing to fund rematches with Bivol and Crawford, those fights have little chance of happening because of the purse requirements. Those two would want large purses as well, perhaps as much as Canelo.

The problem is, Bivol isn’t a big name in the U.S., so the PPV buys wouldn’t likely cover the guaranteed purses for him and Canelo. The interest from casual fans isn’t enough to make the rematch worth funding. Moreover, Bivol’s inactivity has hurt the measure of popularity that he’d gotten from his wins over Canelo and Artur Beterbiev.

It makes sense for Riyadh Season to not pursue rematches between Canelo and Bivol or Crawford. If Canelo loses again to one or both, his value to the Saudis declines. Also, what fans may be overlooking is how boring those fights were.

Bivol just boxed Canelo from the outside and rarely stood in front of him to go toe-to-toe, as fans like to see from their fighters. If the Saudis want to see pure action, they can get more return by targeting fighters with more entertaining styles for Canelo.

Bivol admitted that Canelo has a lot of options for other fights to keep him busy in this late stage of his career. Canelo doesn’t need him.

The Saudi spending changes have also been seen affecting Bivol’s trilogy fight with Artur Beterbiev, which still hasn’t taken place after they fought for the second time in 2025, due to Riyadh Season no longer choosing to finance it. With both fighters reportedly getting $10 million each for their first two fights that were funded by the Saudis, fighting for less than that without their involvement doesn’t work. It’s too risky a fight for Bivol and Beterbiev to take without receiving outside financing.

Why Bivol Rejects The Easy Rematch Talk

“Never. Never. Second fight is never easier against anybody. Maybe it even harder,” Bivol said when asked if a rematch with Canelo, now 36, would be easy, believing the adjustments the Mexican star would make would present a problem.

If the Canelo vs. Bivol rematch is going to happen, the Saudi financiers will need to come up with the money to fund it. Ideally, it would be great if Bivol agreed to take a smaller purse just so he could make the rematch happen, but that doesn’t sound realistic. If anything, he’d want a massive purse that doesn’t balance out with the low number of PPV buys the match would likely bring in.

Sports.title: Agit Kabayel Brushes Off Pressure Ahead Of Nelson Hysa Defense
Sports.content:
Agit Kabayel says he feels no pressure going into Saturday night’s title defense of his WBC heavyweight belt against fringe contender Nelson Hysa at the Merkur Spiel-Arena in Düsseldorf, Germany. This is the type of fight where Kabayel can win and receive absolutely no credit. It’s considered a pure 100% mismatch.

Kabayel (27-0, 19 KOs) will be making his first defense of his WBC belt against the 42-year-old Hysa. It’s not the ideal type of fight for Kabayel, but the top contenders were all busy, leaving him with limited options. He’s in the ‘who needs him’ club, where he’s too risky for big-money stars like Anthony Joshua, Tyson Fury, or Oleksandr Usyk to face. That leaves Kabayel stuck, fighting no-names like Hysa, and not getting much press because of that.

Since Hysa (25-0, 23 KOs) is also with Queensberry, it was a no-brainer match-up to be made. It’s an in-house fight, and a large crowd of nearly 50,000 is expected.

“I was the underdog over and over again, and then right now I’m the favorite, and there is no pressure,” Kabayel said at Thursday’s DAZN Boxing press conference via a stage translator. “I am Agit Kabayel. I want to be better in every fight and I want to show that to the people, and there’s no pressure for me.”

Spencer Brown Calls Out The Resume Gap

Hysa made a big deal during the buildup for this fight, boasting about having done well in sparring with Kabayel in the past, and criticizing him about his delay in signing.

“About that I call him rabbit, it was before that he and his team accept the fight,” said Hysa. “He’s not a rabbit. He’s a good guy. He’s a good boxer.”

Hysa had to say something to get fans into the fight, because this match-up had been largely ignored by people for obvious reasons. Hysa is not a household name, has never beaten anyone recognizable, and is not exactly young at 42. In situations like this, there’s desperation to come up with trash talk that gets the attention of fans.

“He can talk so much bullst, you know, this is no problem,” said Kabayel. “I give him, you know, he’s the better trash talker than me, but in the ring you must fight. After that, he say, ‘You are afraid from me.’ So bro, I never scared from one guy in the heavyweight division.”

Well, Hysa looked powerful in his last fight, knocking out previously unbeaten Thomas Narmo (14-1, 14 KOs), but he was facing a guy with a resume filled with second-tier opposition. Hysa beat him, but he was just as unknown as his previous 24 opponents.

“Let’s have a look at the levels of the different fighters that you’ve faced and he’s faced,” Brown told Hysa on the dais. “Let’s not get into it because they’re completely different levels. Anybody they’ve thrown in front of him, he has taken them out. These are world-class one, two, three boys.”

Returning Heavyweight Boxing To Düsseldorf

Saturday’s heavyweight championship event in Düsseldorf, Germany, will be the first one at the venue since Tyson Fury defeated 39-year-old Wladimir Klitschko in 2015. That fight wasn’t the most entertaining to watch, as there was very little action between the two large heavyweights. Kabayel vs. Hysa should provide more sparks while it lasts in their fight live on DAZN.

“The fight 11 years ago when Wladimir Klitschko lost to Tyson Fury, it was bad for Germany, but Tyson Fury kind of inspired me, and now I got the same manager, and this was kind of the starting point,” said Kabayel.

Kabayel will surely take the fight to Hysa immediately, targeting his body, looking to wear him down and score a stoppage to please the large German crowd.

Sports.title: Canelo Alvarez Eyes Willy Hutchinson To Escape 168 Minefield
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez would be showing genuine bravery if he actually returned to light heavyweight to face WBC champion Willy Hutchinson in the first quarter of 2027. Hutchinson is the target right now over the three super middleweights, Osleys Iglesias, Lester Martinez, or Hamzah Sheeraz.

“Canelo has given the green light,” said talkSPORT Boxing host Ade Oladipo.

Trainer Eddy Reynoso will have a say in whether Alvarez signs for this fight. Hutchinson (21-2, 14 KOs) defeated Joshua Buatsi on November 7 to win the vacant WBC light heavyweight title, switch-hitting, moving, jabbing, and landing clean shots.

He had Buatsi tied in knots throughout that fight with his versatility. Hutchinson showed that he can punch, move, and take a shot. At 28, the 6’1″ Hutchinson is confident, and he’s not going to fight timidly against Canelo the way unbeaten contender Christian Mbilli did in their fight on October 31.

“Willie Hutchinson could sneak a points victory against Canelo in my view,” said talkSPORT analyst Gareth A. Davies. “I’ve seen enough from Willie now in the last couple of years to know this guy walks into the ring just so confident and has the style as a mover to cause Canelo problems. Those are the fighters that have caused the big man problems.”

Canelo (64-3-2, 39 KOs) looked overmatched the last time he fought at 175 against the pure boxer Dmitry Bivol in May 2022, losing a 12-round unanimous decision. In a sign of resignation and defeat, Canelo never attempted to avenge the loss by signing for a rematch with Bivol. Instead, he moved on toward softer targets, fighting 40-year-old Gennady Golovkin and John Ryder.

The 36-year-old Canelo’s mobility is slower now than it was in 2022, and he would have to find a way to improve that for him to have a chance of dethroning the 28-year-old Hutchinson in early 2027. The way Canelo looked against Mbilli, slow and always waiting near the ropes, he’d get picked apart by Hutchinson.

Reynoso has no easy outs for Canelo at 168. Against Mbilli, it was the perfect situation: fighting a guy who changed his normal fighting style of volume punching and instead attempted to outpunch Canelo with single shots. Even with the fight slipping away, Mbilli never switched to plan B by returning to his normal fighting style.

If Canelo stays at super middleweight, he can’t count on IBF champion Osleys Iglesias (16-0, 15 KOs) or interim WBC titlist Lester Martinez (21-0-1, 17 KOs) mentally undermining themselves by changing their normal fighting styles in an attempt to beat him at his own game. They’d both stick with what’s worked for them, which is an attack-oriented style that provides no rest breaks for their opponents.

Choosing Hamzah Sheeraz would result in Canelo being ridiculed by fans, who view the British fighter as a classic example of a fake manufactured hype job. Reynoso has been around long enough to know what the fan perception is of Hamzah by now, and he would recognize ahead of time what the reaction would be if Canelo picked him as his next opponent. It would be a PR disaster.

For Canelo, the best strategy would be moving back up to 175 pounds to face Hutchinson to try and figure out this difficult puzzle. He would be gambling by facing him, but staying at 168 could be far worse. If Canelo loses at 168, he won’t have the weight excuse he gets by moving back up to light heavyweight.

Sports.title: Joseph Parker Ready To Break Daniel Dubois Will Again
Sports.content:
Could Daniel Dubois quit if Joseph Parker takes him into the later rounds and he feels the fight slipping away? Dubois has proven to be a royal basket case when the going gets tough in fights. He’s fine when things are going well, but he goes to pieces when dealing with adversity.

We may see that happen before our eyes on January 30 when he defends his WBO heavyweight title against the experienced veteran Parker at the Co-op Live in Manchester, England. Parker is accustomed to war in the trenches and thrives on conflict. You can’t say the same thing about Dubois.

Queensberry Promotions is trying to sell this thing as unfinished business from February 2025 in Riyadh, where Dubois pulled out during fight week sick, and Parker knocked out an out-of-shape Martin Bakole in two rounds. Plenty of boxing fans still think Dubois got cold feet back then rather than being ill.

All I can say is he didn’t look thrilled sitting across from Parker on DAZN. He had fear in his eyes, being stared down by Parker. From that brief meeting, it’s easy to believe he pulled out of the fight because of stage fright.

Dubois (24-3, 23 KOs) will be favored to win, yet his reckless style leaves him wide open for a fast veteran counterpuncher. He marches forward behind a hard jab, which worked well for him against Jarrell Miller and Anthony Joshua. It’s going to take more than a jab to defeat Parker because he’s well equipped to neutralize that weapon.

If Parker gets inside and forces Dubois onto his back foot, Dubois tends to mentally crumble fast. Once Dubois hits the deck, he appears to give up on himself, looking at his corner for help.

Dubois has been through a lot of brutal fights since 2022, and we’ve all seen his chin give out when somebody survives his early bum rush and hits him flush, just like Oleksandr Usyk and Kevin Lerena did. You could see the look of resignation on Dubois’ face in those fights. He got lucky against Lerena when his opponent gassed out.

Parker (36-4, 24 KOs) is coming back after a year out since Fabio Wardley stopped him in the eleventh round in October 2025. He served a suspension, but chose not to take a tune-up. It makes sense because he wasn’t going to pass up this golden opportunity to relieve a vulnerable champion of his WBO belt,

“I almost feel like there’s a bit of me that thinks Joseph deserves it,” said Ade Oladipo on his YouTube channel.

It makes sense why Frank Warren is making this fight. He also promotes WBC heavyweight champion Agit Kabayel and IBF belt holder Filip Hrgovic. Matching the aging, soon-to-be 35-year-old Parker against Dubois removes the risk that would be there if he put him in against Kabayel or Hrgovic. Parker is a safer opponent on paper, and even if there is an upset, the WBO title still stays with Queensberry. Although Dubois did beat Hrgovic in the past, it would be risky putting him in with him now after Hrgovic’s win over Moses Itauma. The last thing Warren needs is for Hrgovic to beat Dubois.

Parker’s hunger still makes him a real threat to beat Dubois. If Parker is still standing past the midpoint of the fight, he could break Dubois down and make him quit like he did against Usyk and Joe Joyce. As the saying goes, once a quitter, always a quitter.

Sports.title: British Fans Rip Weak Fury vs. Joshua Undercard Lineup
Sports.content:
Turki Alalshikh revealed the full card for the Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua event on December 11 at Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales, and the fan reaction has been negative, particularly among Brits.

With the Fury vs. Joshua fight being billed as the biggest domestic heavyweight bout in years in the main event, fans are hopping mad that the undercard looks like it’s been thrown together without any care about quality.

Fans are finally realizing they’re basically paying for the Fury vs. Joshua fight and getting nothing else worth watching.

Virtually all the undercard bouts, including the co-feature pitting Deontay Wilder vs. Martin Bakole, have been bashed as pure 100% garbage. Fans who subscribed to Netflix just to see the event aren’t happy about it. I’m not surprised.

We saw the same thing with Floyd Mayweather Jr. vs. Manny Pacquiao and Canelo Alvarez vs. Terence Crawford. All the effort and dough went into the main events for those two mega-events, and man, did the undercards look like junk of the highest kind.

Matchroom promoter Eddie Hearn got one of his fighters, former two-time super featherweight champion Joe Cordina, onto the card. The kicker is that Cordina, 35, has been placed on the preliminary portion of the card, fighting Mauricio Lara, out of sight, out of mind.

If Hearn thought this was Cordina’s big chance to win back the fans he lost when he was knocked out by Anthony Cacace in the eighth round in May 2024, he can forget it.

“What about Joe Cordina?” Hearn said when discussing the lineup. “What about a two-time world champion from Wales? Absolutely mental.”

Hearn had been banging the drum about wanting Cordina to fight on the main card against Manny Pacquiao, WBO lightweight champion Abdullah Mason, or Sam Noakes. Instead of fighting one of them in a highly visible fight, Cordina will be hidden away on the prelim card that will be shown on Netflix, TikTok, and The Ring social channels.

Hearn has got to be hopping mad, seeing his fighter fail to make the grade for the main card. I can totally understand the organizers’ decision to place the Cordina vs. Lara fight on the prelim card. Neither of these two fighters has beaten anyone halfway decent since losing. Cordina beat a fringe contender in Gabriel Flores Jr. and a lower-level fighter in Jaret Gonzalez Quiroz since losing to Cacace.

As for Lara, he’s won his last five fights against obscure opposition in confidence builders after fighting to a draw against Daniel Lugo in February 2024 and losing to Leigh Wood by a 12-round unanimous decision in May 2023.

The main card is just as abysmal, with Deontay Wilder facing replacement opponent Martin Bakole in the chief support bout after Jai Opetaia’s injury pullout, Zuffa heavyweight Da’Mazion Vanhouter battling Michael Essomba, and Moses Jolly fighting Igor Adiel Macedo.

Hearn blasted Zuffa promoter Dana White and Zuffa’s influence for the poor undercard, and British fans are replying in droves to Turki’s undercard lineup, echoing Hearn’s thoughts. The people who paid good cash for tickets to see the event live in Cardiff are harping about the scarcity of UK fighters, the 1:30 a.m. local start time for the headliner, and the lack of quality fights beyond the Joshua vs. Fury fight.

The rest of the preliminary lineup is filled with obscure prospects and names that even hardcore boxing fans won’t recognize, aside from Tyson’s younger brother Roman Fury. If you’re tuning in on December 11, you don’t need to set your alarm until right before the main event.

Sports.title: WBA Sets 75-25 Split for Teofimo Lopez Against Jack Catterall
Sports.content:
It’s not looking good for Teofimo Lopez to dodge his mandatory obligations at welterweight. Today, the WBA called a purse bid for December 4 in Cypress, Texas, for a fight between WBA welterweight Super Champion Teofimo and Jack Catterall with a slanted 75/25 purse split.

Financially, that should make Teofimo happy. Even with three-quarters of the money guaranteed, he’s shown no eagerness to sign to fight the mandatory he inherited after his win over WBA champion Rolando ‘Rolly’ Romero by majority decision on August 22. Lopez needs a special permit from the WBA to avoid Catterall (33-2, 14 KOs), but he may not get his wish. It’s understandable why Teofimo doesn’t want to fight Catterall. It’s a style that he’s struggled with, and it’s unlikely he would win.

Teofimo (23-2, 13 KOs) wants to face WBC welterweight champion Ryan Garcia in what would be a lucrative unification, where even if he loses, he’d still do well financially. He needs the WBA title for purse negotiations more so than it being a valuable chip to create more interest in a fight with Ryan.

Teofimo’s title isn’t why fans are interested in seeing the fight. For him, it’s just a negotiation tool to get a better deal, because he lacks Ryan’s popularity to get an even split. Even with a title, you can argue that Teofimo doesn’t rate a 50/50 purse split.

Catterall Risk Explains Lopez Delay

If this were an easy mark, Lopez would be overjoyed at receiving a 75/25 gift split from the WBA. Catterall’s style is similar to Shakur Stevenson’s, which left Teofimo baffled and helpless in a unanimous decision loss over 12 rounds earlier this year at Madison Square Garden on January 31. Teofimo looked embarrassingly bad in that fight. The judges scored it 119 to 109 on all three cards, and he was outlanded 165 to 72.

Defensively, Catterall isn’t as sharp as Shakur, but he’s close enough to be the same kind of nightmare for Teofimo. On offense, Catterall is superior to Shakur, and coupled with his defensive ability, he would be a difficult problem for Teofimo to try and figure out. Besides all that, the pressure that Teofimo would be under would be severe if he needs to defeat Catterall to get to the lucrative payday fight against Ryan Garcia.

If he gets beaten by Catterall, he can forget about fighting Ryan for the time being. Unlike his loss to Shakur, Teofimo wouldn’t be given a straight title shot immediately after. He’d have to rebuild and get in line, which is what he should have had to do after losing to Stevenson instead of being given a crack at Rolly’s WBA title.

Catterall captured his WBA regular welterweight title by beating former mandatory Shakhram Giyasov by a wide 12-round unanimous decision last May. Giyasov was the mandatory challenger that Rolly was avoiding. Now, we’re seeing the new WBA champion Teofimo trying to give Catterall similar treatment. The WBA can stop this cycle by rejecting Teofimo’s request for a special permit.

It’s easy to predict what Lopez’s next move will be if the WBA rejects his appeal. Vacating the WBA belt will be the easiest way of getting Catterall out of his path to a fight with Ryan. Teofimo will still get a nice payday against Ryan, but probably not as nice as it would be if he still had his WBA title.

Sports.title: Brian Mendoza Replaces Keith Thurman in Weak Vergil Ortiz Jr. Co-Feature
Sports.content:
PBC and Golden Boy Promotions made it official today with Brian Mendoza replacing Keith Thurman as Vergil Ortiz Jr.’s opponent for his 10-round co-feature middleweight bout on December 5 at the Desert Diamond Arena in Glendale, Arizona.

Ortiz Jr. and Mendoza will be fighting on the undercard of WBA and WBO cruiserweight champion David Benavidez’s unification bout against WBC champion Michal Cieslak on DAZN PPV and Prime Video.

The addition of Mendoza (23-5, 17 KOs) has received mixed views from fans. Many of them view the 32-year-old as a poor replacement, given his 1-3 record in his last four fights. That’s not exactly top shelf unless losing is the benchmark requirement used to get enlisted as a fill-in opponent for Vergil Ortiz Jr.

Back in Mediocrity Since Fundora

What Mendoza has got going for him is that he knocked out Sebastian Fundora in the seventh round in April 2023 in a huge upset at the time. Fundora was beating the living daylights out of Mendoza for the first six rounds until he got careless in the seventh and got clipped. Since then, Mendoza’s career has slipped back to what it was before that win. That was his textbook Cinderella night, where he got lucky in a fight that he was getting beaten up in.

What’s interesting is that fans online see this as an upgrade over 38-year-old Thurman, just because of his win over Fundora. If you look at Mendoza’s results since that upset, he’s a major downgrade, and that’s saying a lot because Thurman was not a great opponent. He’s not a middleweight, and definitely not young.

Tim Tszyu beat Mendoza by a wide 12-round unanimous decision in October 2023. That fight was an example of Mendoza being brought back down to earth. It wasn’t even slightly a close fight. It looked like Mendoza wandered into the ring from the crowd, and Tszyu took advantage by beating the stuffing out of him. Serhii Bohachuk did the same thing to Mendoza in a clash for the interim WBC junior middleweight title in March 2024.

The only win for Mendoza in the last three years came against journeyman Jesus Antonio Rojas (12-11-2, 10 KOs). It took that level of opponent for Mendoza to snap his two-fight losing streak. In Mendoza’s last fight, he returned to his losing ways, getting trounced by Yoenis Tellez by a one-sided 10-round unanimous decision in March 2026.

Basically, what we’re seeing here is not a dangerous threat being used as a replacement opponent for Ortiz Jr. (24-0, 22 KOs), who recently looked like pure gold in wins over Israil Madrimov, Bohachuk, and Erickson Lubin.

A Cheap Showcase for Ortiz Jr.

Yanking Mendoza out of his fight with Eric Priest enabled Sampson Boxing, TGB Promotions, and Golden Boy Promotions to save money on finding a quality opponent. It’s a showcase fight for Ortiz Jr. Ideally, they should have spent some money to enlist a quality middleweight contender like Yoenli Hernandez to put Ortiz Jr. in a sink-or-swim fight.

What Mendoza does have going for him is a strong chin, as he’s never been knocked out in his career. So if the idea is for Ortiz Jr. to get some rounds in to sharpen up after a year on the shelf, Mendoza is the guy for the job. However, the referee may step in and halt this fight anyway because of the likely one-sided nature of it.

Entertainment-wise, Mendoza eating hard shots from Ortiz Jr. is not fun to watch in a PPV co-feature slot. Fans want competitive fights, not slaughters.

Ortiz Jr. is 28 years old, making the move up to middleweight, and has still accomplished little in his career. It’s got to bug him that he sees fighters like Jaron ‘Boots’ Ennis taking the express route to superstardom, leaving him behind. The difference is, Ennis has been a risk-taker from day one, hasn’t feasted on weak opposition, and has stayed active. In contrast, Ortiz Jr. hasn’t fought the best, and he’s missed a lot of time in his career due to health and promotional issues.

Ghana News.title: CLOGSAG demands probe into alleged assault on Okaikwei North Assembly worker
Ghana News.content:
The Civil and Local Government Staff Association of Ghana (CLOGSAG) has called for a full-scale investigation into the alleged slapping of an administrative officer of the Okaikwei North Municipal Assembly, warning that violence against public servants cannot be tolerated in the workplace.

The demand follows the circulation of a video purportedly showing the Personal Assistant to the Municipal Chief Executive (MCE), Christian Tetteh Badger, striking an assembly staff member, Jeffrey De-Graft Johnson, during a confrontation reportedly over a speech prepared for the MCE.

The aide has since been suspended, while the case has been referred to the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) of the Ghana Police Service for further investigation.

In a statement issued on Thursday, November 26, CLOGSAG said it was deeply troubled by the incident, describing the alleged conduct as a violation of the dignity and professional rights of public service employees.

CLOGSAG said disagreements over official assignments or administrative matters could not justify physical attacks, intimidation or humiliation of workers.

“CLOGSAG unequivocally condemns any form of violence, intimidation, harassment or victimisation against public servants in the discharge of their official duties,” the statement said.

It wants the Office of the Head of the Local Government Service and other relevant oversight institutions to investigate the circumstances surrounding the incident and determine whether any administrative or disciplinary rules have been breached.

CLOGSAG has also urged the police to pursue their investigations and take appropriate legal action against anyone found to have committed an offence.

CLOGSAG said it stood with Mr Johnson and other employees of the Local Government Service, adding that it would use all lawful means available to defend the rights, welfare and safety of its members.

“The Association will pursue all legitimate and lawful avenues available to ensure that the rights and interests of its members are adequately protected,” it said.

The incident has drawn attention to workplace conduct and the treatment of public servants, particularly the responsibility of officials in public institutions to resolve professional disagreements without resorting to intimidation or violence.
