Ghana News.title: Cashew export restriction threatens thousands of livelihoods – Traders petition Mahama
Ghana News.content:
Cashew traders, exporters and farmer-led associations have petitioned President John Mahama to withdraw the proposed three-month restriction on raw cashew exports, warning that the policy could threaten thousands of livelihoods and undermine investments in the sector.

The petitioners fear the proposed restriction could drive down farmgate prices, weaken farmers’ bargaining power, disrupt international supply contracts and expose traders and exporters to significant financial losses.

In a petition dated November 17, 2026, and signed by Chairman Abdel Mumuni Musah and Secretary Adams Ayuba, the associations called for urgent stakeholder consultations before the government implements the proposed measures.

The petition represents about 3,500 traders and aggregators across Techiman, Nkoranza and Kintampo, along with farmer-led associations in Ghana’s cashew-producing communities.

It follows the announcement of the proposed three-month export restriction and export levy during the commissioning of the NADKANSCO processing factory in Techiman on November 16.

“While we support local processing, we believe these measures, if implemented without adequate consultation and safeguards, could negatively affect farmers' incomes, traders' investments, exporters' contractual obligations and the livelihoods of thousands of people within the cashew value chain,” the petition stated.

The associations questioned whether Ghana currently has sufficient domestic processing and purchasing capacity to absorb the country’s raw cashew production.

They warned that restricting exports could reduce competition among buyers, leaving farmers vulnerable to lower prices while threatening existing investments and bank financing arrangements.

The petitioners are demanding the immediate withdrawal of the proposed blanket restriction pending comprehensive stakeholder consultations and an assessment of its economic implications.

However, they expressed support for introducing a fair and reasonable export levy, provided stakeholders agree on its structure and implementation.

They believe a properly structured levy could stabilise prices, protect farmers’ incomes and promote a sustainable cashew industry.

The associations also urged the government to protect existing stocks, commercial contracts, bank facilities and legitimate investments.

They want adequate financing and incentives for local processors so they can compete fairly for raw cashew nuts rather than rely on blanket export restrictions.

“Your Excellency, our position is not against local processing or industrialisation. We believe Ghana can expand domestic processing while maintaining a competitive and sustainable raw cashew trading and export industry.”

The petitioners further demanded that recognised farmer, trader, and exporter associations be formally represented in future policy decisions affecting the industry.

They are seeking an urgent audience with President Mahama or his designated representatives to present their concerns and propose practical alternatives that protect all stakeholders.

Ghana News.title: Twifo Praso clash: One dead, police deploy 100 officers after anti-drug raid
Ghana News.content:
A police operation targeting suspected drug hideouts at Twifo Praso in the Central Region has ended in violence, leaving one civilian dead, several others injured, and three police officers hurt.

The fatality was one of two men reportedly shot when officers from the Police Intelligence Directorate (PID) of the Central North Regional Police Command encountered resistance during an operation near the Pra River on Thursday, November 26.

The exercise was intended to dismantle makeshift structures believed to be used for drug-related activities as part of an intensified campaign against narcotics trafficking and consumption in the area.

Tensions flared after some suspects were arrested, prompting a group of youth to confront the officers.

The confrontation reportedly escalated when two individuals allegedly attempted to set fire to a police pickup vehicle. Officers subsequently fired gunshots to disperse the crowd, hitting the two men.

They were taken to the Twifo Praso Government Hospital, where one was later pronounced dead.

The violence did not end with the shooting. A group of angry youth reportedly besieged the Twifo Praso Police Station, while some protesters vandalised the facility, damaging its glass windows.

The disturbances also left some police personnel injured, with reports indicating that officers had been pelted with stones during the confrontation.

In response, the police deployed 100 additional officers to the town to contain the situation and prevent further violence.

Ghana News.title: Kosmos Energy renovates dining hall at Senya SHS
Ghana News.content:
Kosmos Energy Ghana (KEG) has renovated the dining hall at Senya Senior High School in the Awutu Senya District of the Central Region, providing dining furniture and kitchen facilities to serve about 800 students.

The project followed the completion and handover of a school clinic to the institution in February 2025. Subsequent engagements with school authorities identified the poor condition of the dining hall and the need to improve facilities for students and kitchen staff.

The renovation included the provision of tables and chairs for about 800 students, a kitchen for food preparation and cooking, a storeroom for food supplies and equipment, and washroom facilities.

Speaking at the commissioning ceremony, Kosmos Energy's Senior Vice-President and Head of Ghana Business Unit, Joe K. Mensah, said educational infrastructure extended beyond classrooms and laboratories.

He said students' educational outcomes could improve when they had access to facilities that supported their health, dignity and general well-being.

“It is our expectation that this modern, well-equipped dining hall will provide a more conducive dining environment for students to complement the efforts of parents and government to provide a conducive learning and working environment for the students and staff,” he said.

Mr Mensah commended the school authorities for maintaining the school clinic since its handover and urged them to give the renovated dining hall similar attention to ensure its long-term use.

The Member of Parliament for Awutu Senya West, Gizella Tetteh-Agbotui, also commended Kosmos Energy Ghana for its support for the school and other communities.

The Headmaster of Senya Senior High School said the renovated facility would improve dining conditions and contribute to students' welfare and learning experience.

The project was undertaken under Kosmos Energy Ghana's Corporate Social Responsibility programme.

The commissioning ceremony was attended by the Central Regional Director of Education, Dr Julliete Dufie Otami; the District Chief Executive for Awutu Senya, Kalala Eghan Nyamekye; and traditional leaders from the Senya Beraku Traditional Area.

Ipi Kwa Bentum IV, Tufuhene and Acting President of the Senya Beraku Traditional Area, chaired the ceremony.

Ghana News.title: Twice billed for dirty state databases
Ghana News.content:
At 2:26 pm on 24 November 2026, a speed camera flashed along a northern highway. A commercial minivan wearing a 2026 Greater Accra plate, GT [REDACTED]-26, clocked 85 km/h in a 50 km/h zone. Hours later, Police MTTD dispatched a GH¢240.00 speeding ticket through TraffiTech-GH.

The SMS landed on an innocent citizen’s personal phone. He had never owned that commercial minivan, was not driving, and stood miles from that highway.

Puzzled, he tapped the link inside the GPS-MTTD text message. Without asking for a PIN or plate check, the portal opened a stranger’s traffic record on his screen.

There sat another man’s full name, commercial plate, ten-digit mobile number, and five-decimal highway coordinates. All four identifiers are masked in this essay. State platforms have broadcast enough private data for one week.

Whenever public databases misfire, defenders of state IT projects usually blame dusty legacy folders. That alibi dies on the rear bumper of this minivan.

The yellow commercial plate ends in -26. The Driver and Vehicle Licensing Authority (DVLA) issued it this year, deep inside Ghana’s mandatory Ghana Card era.

Counter Fees Without Five-Second Checks

Parliament mandates DVLA under Section 3(1)(k) of Act 569 to keep accurate vehicle registers. The Road Traffic Regulations, 2026 (L.I. 2519) reinforce that duty with paid physical inspections. Private motorists renew road use certificates annually, while commercial vans return every six months

At every renewal, vehicle owners queue at testing bays, pay statutory fees, and present Ghana Cards under L.I. 2111. Since 2 November 2026, L.I. 2523 has tightened that rule with live biometric matching. Still, DVLA accepted an unverified ten-digit phone number on a 2026 commercial registration.

Meanwhile, pre-2023 vehicle owners face an extra GH¢25 fee to digitally onboard existing records ahead of 2027 plate changes. Motorists must make separate trips carrying registration certificates that DVLA itself printed and holds by law, and vehicle import documents. Drivers pay once to register a car, then pay again to digitise DVLA’s own paperwork.

Charging fresh fees to clean older archives rings hollow while the 2026 intake pours unverified numbers into the same register. A five-pesewa One-Time Password (OTP) at the registration desk would have stopped that wrong number cold.

Two Strangers Trapped in One Bad Row

Police guidelines note that back-office officers review camera photographs before issuing tickets under Act 1153. Staring harder at a bumper photo cannot rescue a corrupted DVLA phone field.

Trace the fallout for both men tied to that single database entry.

DVLA captured the subscriber’s mobile number indirectly from a third party without his knowledge. That breaches direct-collection limits in Section 21 and accuracy duties in Section 26 of the Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843). Serving a statutory penalty on an uninvolved citizen’s line also violated Sections 18 and 20.

Across town, the actual van keeper had his identity, route, and alleged offence exposed to a stranger. Official Police advisories warn citizens never to tap links inside SMS messages. Yet the GPS-MTTD message opened his dossier unchallenged, leaking special personal data protected under Sections 28, 30, 37, and 96.

Crime-prevention exemptions in Sections 60 and 61 of Act 843 never pardon weak security controls or third-party leaks. Under Section 31, both DVLA and GPS-MTTD owe formal breach notices to the Data Protection Commission and that vehicle keeper.

Contesting a Mistake You Never Made

At the foot of the TraffiTech-GH citation sits a small yellow box. If the matched register details are not yours, it shrugs, “contest the fine and say so”.

Article 23 of the 1992 Constitution binds administrative bodies to act fairly and reasonably. The ticket gives 14 days to pay GH¢240.00, after which Regulation 242 of L.I. 2519 adds a 1 per cent daily surcharge. Disputing it requires an online filing, a regional MTTD station appointment, and a court date.

How did DVLA’s skipped five-second check become an innocent citizen’s multi-day errand? Meanwhile, the real commercial keeper remains legally unserved, walking blind towards DVLA service blocks after 9 December.

Recycled SIMs and Decaying Registries

Even a verified phone number at first registration decays over time. Mobile networks routinely deactivate dormant SIM cards after six months of inactivity and resell those numbers to new Ghana Card holders. When SIM owners switch lines or let secondary phones numbers lapse, strangers legally inherit their old digits.

Section 26 of Data Protection Act 843 requires state controllers to keep personal data up to date, not merely accurate on day one. Commercial vans already visit the DVLA every six months for paid inspections, matching the telecom industry’s six-month churn cycle.

Failing to re-check SIM ownership against the keeper’s Ghana Card turns every recycled number into a waiting data breach. Live matching between the NCA Central SIM Register and NIA records must therefore run before any ticket leaves TraffiTech-GH.

Fixing the Logbook Before Scaling the Cameras

Public confidence erodes fastest when state referees ignore the rules they enforce on private businesses. Last month, the Data Protection Commission flagged six firms in Kaneshie and Tudu and summoned them before CID. When state registries leak offence records or fire blind citations, that regulatory voice drops to a murmur.

Basic engineering hygiene must precede any expansion of TraffiTech-GH into automated insurance and roadworthiness fines. DVLA should block any phone number from entering the vehicle register without live SMS OTP confirmation and NIA-linked SIM verification.

On the policing side, GPS-MTTD and its NIB payment portal must gate every citation behind a plate or Ghana Card challenge. The Data Protection Commission should simultaneously audit both controllers under Section 31 and publish its remediation timeline.

Sharp highway cameras cannot rescue a careless licensing counter. When the logbook inside the registration hall is crooked, faster software simply delivers state errors to innocent phones on time.

By: Sitsofe Mensah, Solutionist and Technology Associate with IMANI Africa

Ghana News.title: Budget projections vulnerable to global and domestic shocks — Terkper
Ghana News.content:
Seth Terkper

Former Finance Minister Seth Terkper has cautioned against judging government budget projections without considering the economic shocks that can undermine revenue and expenditure assumptions after the estimates have been prepared.

He cited Ghana's experience with the sharp decline in crude oil prices in 2015 and the recent difficulties in the cocoa sector as examples of how developments beyond the government's control can disrupt fiscal plans.

Speaking on JoyNews' PM Express on Thursday, November 26, 2026, in a discussion of the 2027 Budget, Mr Terkper said governments had to prepare budgets based on available economic information but could not always anticipate how global commodity markets and domestic conditions would evolve.

He recalled that during preparations for the 2015 and 2016 budgets, crude oil prices were relatively high, with the 2015 budget using a benchmark revenue price of US$99.38 per barrel.

However, the market turned sharply against the projections, forcing the government to revise the benchmark to US$57 per barrel in its 2015 mid-year review. Crude oil prices fell further, with Brent trading at about US$45.70 per barrel in August that year.

Mr Terkper said the decline had serious implications for government revenue and the execution of projects and programmes financed from petroleum receipts.

He explained that the country's fiscal framework included mechanisms such as the Annual Budget Funding Amount (ABFA), the Stabilisation Fund and the Contingency Fund to support budget implementation and cushion the economy against revenue shortfalls.

The former minister said the experience illustrated the difficulty of accurately forecasting commodity revenues, particularly when global prices changed significantly after a budget had been prepared.

Turning to domestic developments, he said the government also had to contend with inherited financial obligations and unforeseen pressures that could not simply be transferred to previous administrations.

“If a debt was defaulted, do you bring back the past administration and say this is your responsibility, go and pay? No, you don't do that,” he said.

He also pointed to the difficulties in Ghana's cocoa sector, arguing that developments in the industry had demonstrated how quickly domestic economic conditions could change after a budget was presented.

Mr Terkper recalled that during the preparation of the previous year's budget, the outlook for cocoa had been different from the severe difficulties that later confronted the sector, including the pressure on payments to farmers.

The International Monetary Fund's 2026 assessment of Ghana's economy documented a sharp correction in global cocoa prices during the 2025/26 season. Prices fell from about US$8,800 per tonne at the beginning of the season in August 2025 to approximately US$2,800 by the end of February 2026.

The decline, combined with a farmgate price that had become misaligned with international market conditions, contributed to unsold cocoa stocks and severe liquidity pressures at the Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD).

The government subsequently approved measures to address the crisis, including the clearance of GH¢3.62 billion in arrears owed to cocoa farmers and the restructuring of about GH¢3.7 billion in COCOBOD's legacy debt.

Mr Terkper said such developments reinforced the need for flexibility in budget management, as governments had to respond to changing economic circumstances while protecting fiscal stability.

His comments come amid debate over the assumptions, expenditure commitments and fiscal targets underpinning the 2027 Budget.

He maintained that the ability to manage unexpected pressures, rather than simply produce estimates at the beginning of the budget cycle, remained one of the major challenges confronting finance ministers.

Ghana News.title: Leroy Botchey named HR Future Leader Under 35
Ghana News.content:
A Human Resource professional and HR Administration Manager at Société Générale Ghana PLC, Leroy Botchey was named the HR Future Leader Under 35 Award recipient at the 2026 HR Professionals Summit & Awards in Accra.

The HR Certification Centre organised the awards under the theme “Building Africa’s Human Resource Ecosystem for Transformation,” which brought together HR practitioners, business leaders and industry stakeholders to discuss the evolving role of human capital in Africa’s development.

Speaking on the recognition, Société Générale Ghana PLC's HR Administration Manager, Leroy Botchey, thanked the organisers for the honour. He described the award as a reflection of the many people and experiences that have shaped his professional journey.

“I am truly honoured and humbled to receive this recognition. I sincerely thank the HR Certification Centre, the Awarding Jury, and the organisers for considering me worthy of this award.

"I see this recognition not just as a personal achievement but as a reflection of the many people and experiences that have shaped my journey,” he said.

As an HR professional, he has developed experience across HR operations, employee relations, workforce management, performance management, organisational support and people administration.

In his current role at Société Générale Ghana PLC, he helps strengthen HR processes, improve operational efficiency, and support the delivery of effective people management services.

Commenting further, Mr Botchey thanked his employer, mentors, colleagues, friends and family for their support. He said the award reminds him that there is still more to learn, more to contribute and more lives to impact.

“This award bears my name, but behind it is the contributions of many mentors in my HR Journey. I share this recognition with all of you,” he added.

The recognition marks an important milestone in a career characterised by continuous learning, professional development and a commitment to improving people management practices.

Mr Botchey’s journey into Human Resources began with a background in Telecommunications Engineering, in which he graduated with First Class Honours.

His transition into HR reflects an unconventional but rewarding career path that combines analytical thinking, systems development and people management.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: At least 13 Niger soldiers killed in Sanam armed attack
World.content:
It remains unclear who carried out the attack on Niger’s National Guard in Tillaberi, near the Mali border.

Share At least 13 Niger soldiers killed in Sanam armed attack on social media

At least 13 members of Niger’s National Guard have been killed and 20 wounded in an attack on their compound in Sanam, in the west of the country, the Defence Ministry has said.

In a statement read on state television, the ministry said the attack on Thursday was carried out by “numerous heavily armed assailants”, referring to the incident as a “terrorist attack”.

The ministry gave a provisional toll and said soldiers killed several attackers and destroyed their logistical infrastructure. Operations to track down the attackers are ongoing, it added.

The assault took place at about 5am local time (04:00 GMT), local and security sources told the Nigerien outlet ActuNiger.

Sanam is in the Tillaberi region, near the Mali border, where armed groups regularly attack security forces.

It was not clear who was behind the attack.

The attack comes two days after the ministry said 11 soldiers were killed in an attack attributed to Boko Haram in the Diffa region, in the southeast.

Violence across the border

In neighbouring Nigeria, suspected members of an armed group killed at least 30 people in villages in the central state of Niger on Tuesday.

They described it as retaliation for the killing of many Fulani herders days earlier.

In Nigeria’s northeast, President Bola Tinubu promised on Wednesday to restore peace to a region hit by a rebellion led by Boko Haram and the ISIL (ISIS) affiliate in West Africa Province, as he campaigns for re-election.

World.title: Trump downplays Russia, China support for Iran during talks with US troops
World.content:
Trump praises US troops for their role in the war on Iran and says he has spoken to Netanyahu in recent days.

Share Trump downplays Russia, China support for Iran during talks with US troops on social media

United States President Donald Trump has claimed Iran possesses missiles capable of reaching Europe and downplayed Russia and China’s support for Tehran while speaking to US military personnel by phone for the Thanksgiving holiday.

Taking questions from reporters at his Mar-a-Lago residence in Florida on Thursday, Trump said without “peace in the Middle East”, Iran could launch nuclear attacks against Israel and other countries in the region.

“We don’t need Middle East oil. But what we do need is we need peace in the Middle East,” Trump said, as OPEC ministers are scheduled to meet on Sunday to weigh 2027 oil production targets.

The US president and First Lady Melania Trump called US service members deployed across the region to praise their role in the war on Iran, including personnel at the al-Dhafra airbase in the United Arab Emirates and the Prince Sultan airbase in Saudi Arabia.

“Each of you is playing an essential role to protect not only our country today but future generations of Americans by ensuring that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon,” he said.

When asked if the US would renew strikes on Iran, the president said: “If we do something, we will definitely hit Pickaxe Mountain.” Trump also told reporters he spoke with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in recent days.

The US is still offering Iran an opening to negotiate, according to Trump, who said: “We’re trying to be nice. We’re giving them every chance to make a deal and save a lot of lives, but I’m not sure if they are gonna take advantage of that.”



He downplayed the importance of intelligence-sharing by Russia and China with Iran, amid reports that the two countries helped Tehran target US bases.

“My meeting with President Xi was an incredible meeting. I think that they’re very little involved with Iran. They could get involved, but involvement to me would mean shooting, not giving them little information,” Trump said during the short news conference.

“We do the same thing, by the way. And you know, when they say that they may be spying on us, well, we spy on them too,” he added.

Trump’s statements come as Iran steps up attacks on US military targets across the region. On Saturday, Bahrain reported an Iranian attack on a civilian industrial facility while Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed it targeted US air defence radars in the country.

Kuwait said on Thursday that an Iranian drone attack on a “vital site” killed two Italian workers and injured four others. Tehran has denied involvement in the attack.

Trump told deployed service members, “You’re going to continue that deployment, and we have victory at hand,” referring to the war on Iran.

“It’s [victory] going to be whenever I want it to be, to be honest,” he added.

World.title: Asian stock markets rise after earlier tech rout
World.content:
Indices in Japan, South Korea, Australia and Hong Kong rise, as New Zealand stocks dip on election uncertainty.

Asian stocks have opened higher as technology firms enjoy a period of calm following ructions at the start of the week.

Japan’s benchmark Nikkei 225 on Friday added 0.7 percent to 57,919.30 in morning trading. Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 rose 0.4 percent to 8,800.50. South Korea’s Kospi surged 2.2 percent to 4,812.65.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng edged up 0.4 percent to 22,310.11.

Stocks in Indonesia, Singapore and the Philippines also rose, while New Zealand’s bourse edged down as Prime Minister Christopher Luxon’s right-wing coalition lost its parliamentary majority, plunging the country into political uncertainty with a centrist party set to play a decisive role in forming the next government.

Buying of stocks tied to artificial intelligence (AI) has been pushing benchmarks higher, despite some profit-taking that has kept those gains in check.

In Japan, Tokyo Electron and Advantest Corp stocks dropped in morning trading but quickly recovered their losses, underlining the continuing appeal of stocks in the semiconductor and AI sectors.

With Wall Street closed for the Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday, traders had no new business-driving catalysts heading into the weekend, though they remain on edge over concerns about the AI boom.

They were also keeping an eye on possible retaliation against US President Donald Trump’s proposed tariffs of up to 20 percent on some of the United States’ biggest trading partners, including China, the European Union, India, Japan and South Korea.

Also in view is the Federal Reserve’s next interest rate decision next month, with speculation swirling that it could opt for a hefty 50-basis-point increase instead of the usual 25 points.



Oil prices extended Thursday’s gains of more than 1 percent amid fresh concerns over an escalation of hostilities in the Middle East after Iran-aligned Houthis struck a Saudi refinery, temporarily halting some operations. That came after an attack on another hub in the Gulf earlier in the week.

In company news, Japan Tobacco rallied more than 4 percent following a report that it was considering joining up with US giant Altria for a takeover of Britain’s Imperial Brands. Imperial jumped 13 percent in London on Thursday.

Japan Tobacco is dealing with an $8.9bn hit after the Russian government seized all seven of its local subsidiaries, as relations with Tokyo worsen following the arrest of a Japanese journalist on spying allegations.

World.title: Spain and Morocco under-17 stars target World Cup 2030
World.content:
NewsFeed Spain and Morocco under-17 stars target World Cup 2030

Spain and Morocco are two of the co-hosts of the next Men’s World Cup in 2030. Both nations faced off at the under-17 World Cup in Qatar, and Al Jazeera’s Sohail Malik asked players whether they believe playing top level international football is in their future.

World.title: Zelenskyy warns of major Russian attack as Trump urges Putin to ‘pull back’
World.content:
Trump says he urged Putin to ‘pull back’ military aggression in Europe amid escalating Russian and Ukrainian attacks.

Share Zelenskyy warns of major Russian attack as Trump urges Putin to ‘pull back’ on social media

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Ukraine has information that Russia is preparing a new mass strike on the country in the coming days.

“Unfortunately, we have information about a new mass strike being prepared by the Russians,” he said in his nightly video address on Thursday. “In the coming days, please pay attention to the alarms of missile threats.”

It was the second such warning from Zelenskyy this week. He also had a message for Moscow: “We will rebuild what is ours and retaliate against every Russian strike.”

Trump urges Putin to pull back

US President Donald Trump said he had pressed Russian President Vladimir Putin to ease Russia’s military actions in Europe.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump said he spent “a lot of time” in talks with Putin in China on the issue of Putin pulling back “all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe”.

“Thousands of people are being killed each and every month, A COMPLETE BLOODBATH,” Trump wrote. He said he hoped that would allow a deal between Russia and Ukraine to be “made quickly”, which he called “a strong possibility”.

Trump said he updated NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte on the talks during a meeting at his Mar-a-Lago club in Florida on Wednesday night.

Latest attacks

Russia struck Kyiv with ballistic missiles overnight, wounding seven people and hitting a shopping centre and two other buildings, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said.

Moscow said it hit drone-related sites in the city. Russian forces have attacked Kyiv and other cities almost continuously since September.



Ukraine said its drones hit an oil refinery in Russia’s southern Krasnodar region, oil reservoirs at a Transneft facility in Bashkortostan and the Marinovka military airfield in the Volgograd region.

Ukraine has also widened its attacks at sea. On Monday, Zelenskyy said Ukraine used seven naval drones to hit the Russian corvette Merkury and the cargo ship Angara off Libya. Libyan officials told the Associated Press news agency that the Merkury was heavily damaged but not sunk.

At about the same time, a suspected Ukrainian drone struck the Russia-bound cargo ship Sparta II in the Baltic Sea, near Finland. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov called the attacks a “very dangerous trend“.

At least four Russian vessels have been targeted this month.

Europe’s funding for Ukraine

European Union leaders are struggling at a summit in Brussels to agree on a new 45 billion euro ($49bn) loan to help Ukraine meet its economic and military needs next year. It would come on top of a 90 billion euro ($99bn) loan, agreed nearly a year ago, that covers most of Ukraine’s government needs for 2026 and 2027.

Early on Friday in Brussels, European Council President Antonio Costa said that 24 member states supported the new loan, as talks on the bloc’s next seven-year budget stretched on.

The loan is tangled up with the EU’s budget for 2028 to 2034, which includes about $110bn for Ukraine over seven years. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has threatened to hold up the budget unless all member states make a “collective commitment” to Ukraine.

North Korea ‘pauses’ arms deliveries

Ukraine’s military intelligence agency (GUR) said on Thursday that North Korea has temporarily halted some military cooperation with Russia after diplomatic tensions between the allies.

It said this includes deliveries of KN-23 ballistic missiles and artillery shells, and Russian military flights over North Korean territory.

GUR said North Korea’s Foreign Minister Choe Son-hui announced the pause last month in response to a Russian deputy foreign minister’s assertion that Moscow would help ease tensions between Seoul and Pyongyang.

GUR also said Pyongyang is holding off on a Russian request to raise North Korea’s military presence in Russia from about 8,500 to 50,000 troops.

It added that North Korean units remain in Russia’s Kursk region and that a North Korean missile unit has been in the Voronezh region since mid-summer, from where Russia strikes Ukraine.

South Korean and Western intelligence agencies have said Pyongyang sent more than 10,000 soldiers to Russia’s Kursk region in 2024, along with artillery shells, missiles and long-range rocket systems.



Strikes continue

On November 20, Russia fired more than 400 drones and 110 missiles at Ukraine, killing eight people, Zelenskyy said.

It was one of the largest attacks of the war and followed Putin’s vow to retaliate for Ukrainian strikes on the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to Crimea.

World.title: Trump says the US has ‘close to 50%’ of world’s oil
World.content:
Trump says the US has ‘close to 50%’ of world’s oil

NewsFeed Trump says the US has ‘close to 50%’ of world’s oil

On a call to soldiers deployed to the Gulf, US President Donald Trump claimed that the US does not ‘need Middle East oil’ and that they were maintaining their presence there to protect ‘Israel and other countries’.

World.title: Clashes halt match as Turkiye football fans raise Palestinian flags
World.content:
NewsFeed Clashes halt match as Turkiye football fans raise Palestinian flags

Clashes broke out between Georgian police and Turkish club Besiktas supporters during a UEFA match. Besiktas was playing against Israel’s Hapoel Be’er Sheva. Play was halted for 30 minutes when scuffles began after fans raised Palestinian flags and chanted anti-Israel slogans.

World.title: Global news agency AFP reports cyberattack, shuts down content platform
World.content:
Agence France-Presse (AFP) has been hit by a cyberattack, requiring the AFP Forum content platform to be taken offline.

The France-based international news agency’s management said on Thursday that it is currently investigating the circumstances of the cyberattack, including who was behind it.

“AFP was hit by a cyber attack overnight, starting at 1:30 am (Paris time) [00:30 GMT]. The target was AFP Forum, one of the platforms our clients use to browse and download our content,” an internal email from AFP management said.

“As soon as the intrusion was detected, our teams moved immediately to contain the intrusion and took AFP Forum offline as a precautionary measure. AFP Forum remains unavailable until further notice.”

AFP is reportedly offering backup solutions to the agency’s subscribers while the portal is offline.

France’s cybersecurity chief, Vincent Strubel, warned on Thursday that the country faces an unprecedented level of cybersecurity threats and called for collective efforts to strengthen defences against attacks.

“We are facing a level of threat that is unprecedented, with an intensity we have never experienced before,” Strubel said in an interview with France Inter radio.

The incident is the latest in a slew of cybersecurity disruptions across European countries. FIFA, which is based in Zurich, Switzerland, confirmed to Al Jazeera on Thursday that it had been the victim of a cyberattack that gave unauthorised access to personal and business information.

In October, several French supermarkets were hit by an “unprecedented” cyberattack that raised the temperature of fridges and freezers to as high as 50 degrees Celsius (122F).



Temperature spikes were also recorded in stores in 10 other European countries in early November, including the United Kingdom, Germany, Belgium and Sweden.

France accused Tehran of being behind the October attack and summoned Iran’s ambassador to Paris to “lodge a very strong protest”.

Iran called Paris’s accusations “baseless” and condemned the “hackneyed policy of levelling accusations against the Islamic republic”.

World.title: US too focused on Middle East and not pushing Russia hard enough, Zelensky tells BBC
World.content:
Volodymyr Zelensky has voiced deep frustration with the US, saying delays in delivering vital anti-ballistic missiles are costing Ukrainian lives and complaining that the US is not pushing Russia hard enough in peace talks.

In an interview with the BBC at his central Kyiv office, Ukraine's president also said it was "strange" that Donald Trump had posted a photo of himself embracing Vladimir Putin as "my friend".

"Of course it's up to the President of the United States, but... it's strange," Zelensky said, speaking in English.

"He's an aggressor, and a killerâ¦He can't be a friend. Just cannot be," he said, adding it was like saying you were friends with Adolf Hitler during World War Two.

Since a bruising encounter with Trump in the Oval Office in 2025, Zelensky has been careful how he handles relations with the United States.

Trump's two envoys have been trying to negotiate a peace deal between Russia and Ukraine - to end the huge loss of life. But they often seem more in tune with Moscow's position, than that of Kyiv.

The latest round of peace talks, mediated in Abu Dhabi earlier this month, made no obvious progress: "The more we know, the more problems", is how Zelensky described it.

He said talks were expected to resume in December.

On Thursday, Donald Trump posted on his Truth Social platform that at his own summit with Putin in China last week he had urged Russia to "pull back all military aggression against territories throughout Europe" and said he believed a peace deal with Ukraine was "a strong possibility".

But from its public statements, Russia appears to have regressed to its initial, hardline negotiating positions â on everything.

And Zelensky revealed that it was not clear whether European negotiators would be at the table, as the US envoys had announced.

The Kremlin appears to be resisting.

World.title: Major Thanksgiving storm brings flooding, flight delays across US
World.content:
On Thursday, a powerful storm hit the eastern US, bringing damaging winds of up to 70mph, torrential rain, and major coastal flooding.

New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill declared a state of emergency as several communities along the Jersey Shore saw widespread flooding.

New York Governor Kathy Hochul also declared a state of emergency for New York City, Long Island and Westchester County.

In New York City, organisers of the annual Macy's Thanksgiving parade have postponed the event to Saturday.

Bridges closed in Maryland due to severe winds and waves battered beaches in Delaware as water seeped onto the boardwalk.

In Maryland, almost two million customers have been asked by the water utility to use water for essential use only due to "intermittent power disruptions".

On the wettest Thanksgiving on record in Washington DC, tidal waters surged and soaked runways at Reagan Washington National Airport, according to the National Water Prediction Service.

More than 980,000 households were reporting power outages by Thursday evening, with Pennsylvania, Virginia, Maryland and New Jersey hit particularly hard.

Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro said that utility providers were working tirelessly to restore power. Meanwhile, energy companies in Virginia and New Jersey warned it may take some time, even days, for power to return, as crews had to wait until it was safe to access damaged areas.

On Thursday afternoon, President Donald Trump said he would consider releasing emergency funds for the east coast as it faces down the holiday storm.

Across the US, severe weather is also descending on the West Coast. The NWS has warned of a series of Pacific storms that are expected to bring rain, mountain snow and strong winds.

World.title: Watch: Roofs torn off and streets under water as severe weather hits US
World.content:
Powerful storms are battering both US coasts as the Thanksgiving holiday weekend gets under way.

Hundreds of flights have been cancelled and hundreds of thousands are without power, in states including Virginia, North Carolina and New Jersey.

Strong winds have blown roofs off houses and floodwater has submerged streets.

World.title: New Zealand's ruling coalition falls short of parliamentary majority by one seat
World.content:
New Zealand's ruling coalition has fallen short of a parliamentary majority by one seat, following a campaign shaped by a sluggish economy and disillusioned voters.

It now needs the support of the centrist Opportunity Party to remain in power. If they cannot reach a deal, the country may have to go back to the polls.

The incumbent National Party led by Prime Minister Christopher Luxon secured 40 out of 130 seats, while its coalition partners ACT and New Zealand First took 13 and 12 respectively.

A government led by the centre-left Labour Party is not possible, official results on Friday show, as the bloc would not have enough seats even if Opportunity threw its weight behind it.

Luxon on Friday acknowledged that negotiations "may be challenging" and will take some time.

"Kiwis won't thank us for rushing to an agreement that falls apart or for sending them back to the polls," he told reporters.

Labour leader Chris Hipkins said his party "ran an incredible campaign" but acknowledged that it doesn't have negotiating power despite winning the popular vote. "More New Zealanders voted for change at this election than for the status quo," he said.

New Zealand's mixed-member proportional voting system means most governments are coalitions. Each person casts two votes â one for their preferred political party and another for their choice of local representative.

Labour secured 36 seats, The Greens took 17, while Te PÄti MÄori, which represents MÄori interests, picked up five.

Opportunity, which has been described as this election's kingmaker, secured seven seats. Opportunity's leader Qiulae Wong told reporters her party will negotiate with National, but that all options remain on the table.

"There are seven parties in parliment and everyone is responsible for making sure we do everything we can to deliver a stable government for New Zealand. It's not just up to us," she said on Friday.

Preliminary results on 7 November, election day, had projected that National combined with its coalition partners would have a slim lead over the left-leaning bloc.

But today's official tally shows it had lost two seats on special votes - cast by citizens who were overseas or outside of their registered electorate on election day - which typically skew left.

Some of National's key election pledges include lower taxes, cheaper energy, more renewable generation, and a greater focus on defence.

Labour, meanwhile, had campaigned to cut healthcare, public transport and fuel costs, more government support for social housing, among other things.

In earlier interviews with the BBC, many voters had expressed frustration over spiralling costs of living and high unemployment across the country, with declining faith in their political leadership.

"There's this kind of apathy and a bit of dread," said 21-year-old Imogen Vlutger.

A 40-year-old man said he didn't vote as he could not bring himself to tick any of the boxes on the ballot paper.

More than half of the country no longer see New Zealand as a land of opportunity, according to a survey by the Helen Clark Foundation, a public policy think tank.

Kiwis have been leaving the country in record numbers, with many of them, including former prime minister Jacinda Arden, moving to Australia.

World.title: German boat dealer suspected of supplying Channel smuggling gangs, BBC finds
World.content:
A German boat dealer is suspected by European authorities of being a key supplier to migrant smugglers operating in the English Channel, the BBC can reveal.

Nearly a third of small-boat crossings in the first four months of this year allegedly involved boats or engines from MaReBoote, a small firm in western Germany, according to files we have seen.

The managing director, Marvin Reuter, is contesting extradition to France, where he could face smuggling, criminal conspiracy and involuntary manslaughter charges.

His equipment is suspected of being linked to two fatal accidents, in which four men died.

We confronted the 35-year-old at his business near Dortmund, but he would not answer our questions. He said he was reporting us to the police.

Reuter cannot be formally charged until extradited to France but could face jail time, if tried and convicted. He is presumed innocent until proven guilty.

The BBC - alongside German broadcasters WDR and NDR, newspaper SÃ¼ddeutsche Zeitung (SZ) - and France's Le Monde newspaper - has obtained and reviewed hundreds of police, court and tax documents about the case. We have blurred images of Reuter because of German privacy rules.

Investigators, we have learned, believe they have uncovered clear, persistent links between Reuter and smuggling networks.

Evidence has been gathered through the confessions of alleged accomplices and covert jail-cell recordings of an alleged gang chief - as well as the two deadly crossing attempts.
