Former President Ellen Johnson Sirleaf has also called for an independent assessment of the proposed agreement before the country proceeds with its implementation.

Sirleaf wants an independent panel of professionals and technical experts to examine the financial and other provisions of the deal and advise the government on its potential consequences.

Speaking on the proposed arrangement, the former Liberian leader emphasized the importance of having an independent assessment to establish whether the agreement adequately protects Liberia’s interests.

She has also raised concerns about the potential financial obligations associated with the US$5.7 billion arrangement, particularly the implications of using future revenues from the country’s mineral resources to finance infrastructure projects.

Sirleaf’s position reflects concerns about the need to avoid repeating Liberia’s past experiences with substantial debt obligations and financial arrangements that could constrain future governments.

Her call for an independent review comes as the agreement moves from the Executive Branch to the Legislature, where lawmakers are expected to examine its provisions before making a final decision.

Bea Mountain’s Existing Mining Operations

Bea Mountain Mining Corporation is a subsidiary of Avesoro Resources, a privately owned mining company associated with Turkey’s Günal family and its wider business network, including the MNG and Mapa groups.

The company currently operates an active gold mining concession in Grand Cape Mount County under an agreement with the Government of Liberia.

The proposed MIDA would place the company at the center of an ambitious national infrastructure financing arrangement, linking its financial obligations and designated government entitlements to the construction of major public infrastructure.

The government has presented the agreement as an opportunity to address longstanding deficiencies in electricity and road networks while supporting economic growth and investment across the country.

The Ministry of Information has described the arrangement as a five-year infrastructure program, with the proposed power plants expected to add 270 megawatts to Liberia’s generating capacity.

With the agreement now before the House of Representatives, lawmakers face the responsibility of examining its financial structure, project costs, implementation timelines, government obligations and safeguards before deciding whether to ratify it.

The two-week reporting deadline given to the relevant committees is expected to set the pace for the Legislature’s initial consideration of the proposed deal.

For Liberia, the debate extends beyond the construction of roads, dams and power plants. It concerns how the country can leverage its natural resources to finance development while ensuring that the arrangement delivers measurable public benefits and does not undermine the country’s long-term economic interests.

World.title: Liberia: Cummings Warns Boakai Against ‘Mortgaging Liberia’s Future’ in US$5.7B Bea Mountain Deal
World.content:
ANC Political Leader Raises Procurement, Transparency and Debt Concerns, Urges Government to Suspend Implementation Pending Independent Review of Agreement

By Gerald C. Koinyeneh

MONROVIA – Alternative National Congress (ANC) Political Leader Alexander B. Cummings has warned President Joseph Nyuma Boakai against committing Liberia’s future mineral revenues to finance a proposed US$5.7 billion infrastructure agreement with Bea Mountain Mining Corporation, cautioning that the arrangement could impose significant financial obligations on generations of Liberians.



Cummings’ warning comes a day after President Boakai signed the proposed Master Infrastructure Development Agreement (MIDA) between the Government of Liberia and Bea Mountain Mining Corporation, a subsidiary of Avesoro Resources, a privately owned mining company linked to Turkey’s Günal family and its business network, including the MNG and Mapa groups.

The President signed the agreement in the presence of several senior government officials, including Justice Minister Betty Lamin Blamo, Finance and Development Planning Minister Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan, Mines and Energy Minister Matenokay Tingban, National Investment Commission Chairman Morley Kamara and Presidential Legal Adviser Bushuben Keita, among others.

In a statement delivered Thursday at the ANC headquarters in Monrovia, Cummings described the decision as grave, arguing that the proposed arrangement raises fundamental questions about the management, ownership and future utilization of Liberia’s mineral wealth.

He stressed that while Liberia urgently needs roads, electricity and other critical infrastructure, the country’s development ambitions should not come at the expense of transparency, prudent financial management and the interests of future generations.



“We must not become an Esau Generation,” Cummings warned, invoking the biblical account of Esau, who traded his birthright for a meal to satisfy an immediate need.

He argued that Liberia risks making a similar mistake if it commits decades of future national revenues to an infrastructure arrangement without first establishing whether the country is receiving adequate value and sufficient protection.

“Our infrastructure deficit is real. Our desire for development is legitimate. But in our urgency to solve today’s problems, we must not mortgage tomorrow’s possibilities,” he said.

Questions Over US$5.7 Billion Financing Structure

Cummings acknowledged that Liberia’s infrastructure deficit is severe, citing poor road networks, unreliable electricity, high energy costs and limited opportunities for farmers and businesses.

However, he questioned the proposed financing structure, which seeks to fund approximately US$5.7 billion in infrastructure projects using future revenues generated from Liberia’s natural resources.

According to him, the arrangement may appear attractive because it promises large-scale infrastructure development without requiring immediate expenditures from the national budget. However, he argued that the government must explain the actual financial cost and long-term implications before proceeding.

“There is no such thing as free infrastructure. Someone ultimately pays. The only question is whether Liberia will receive fair value for what future generations will be required to surrender,” he said.

The ANC leader identified several concerns, including possible violations of the Public Procurement and Concessions Act, the absence of competitive bidding, inadequate independent valuation and engineering assessments, potential infrastructure overpricing and significant fiscal and contingent liabilities.

He also raised concerns about environmental and social risks, governance and potential conflicts of interest, as well as the possibility that future national revenues could be committed outside traditional public debt transparency mechanisms.

Cummings said the final financial exposure facing Liberia remains uncertain, arguing that provisions within the proposed framework could permit additional costs, adjustments and government obligations beyond the publicly cited US$5.7 billion figure.

He called on the government to disclose the full extent of its financial commitments, the duration of the proposed revenue deductions and the independent assessments supporting the projected infrastructure costs.

Warns Against Pledging Future Mineral Revenues

One of Cummings’ central concerns is the possibility that future royalties, income taxes, dividends and other government revenues generated from Liberia’s natural resources could be redirected toward financing or repaying the infrastructure arrangement over an extended period.

He warned that committing these revenue streams without adequate valuation and oversight could leave future administrations with limited fiscal flexibility and reduce the benefits Liberians receive from their natural resources.

“This is not merely an accounting issue. It is a sovereignty issue. It is a human rights issue. It is an intergenerational justice issue,” he said.

The former presidential candidate argued that Liberia must learn from the experiences of resource-rich countries where inadequate transparency, competition and accountability have undermined the benefits of natural resource extraction.

He maintained that the country’s mineral wealth belongs to its people and should not be committed through arrangements that lack sufficient public scrutiny and independent oversight.

Cummings Demands Independent Review, Public Disclosure

To address the concerns, Cummings called on the Boakai administration to suspend further action on the proposed arrangement until a comprehensive set of safeguards has been satisfied.

Among the measures he wants the government to undertake are:

Independent valuation of the underlying mineral resource base.

Independent engineering and feasibility assessments of proposed infrastructure projects.

Transparent and competitive procurement processes.

Full publication of all transaction documents.

Legislative review and public hearings.

Comprehensive environmental and social impact assessments.

Independent fiscal risk and debt sustainability analysis.

Engagement of internationally credible transaction advisers.

Independent certification of project costs and completed works.

Public disclosure of all contingent liabilities and future revenue commitments.

He argued that these measures would help establish whether the proposed arrangement represents the best possible deal for Liberia and whether the country can achieve the same infrastructure objectives through alternative financing arrangements at lower costs.

“ANC Is Not Opposed to Infrastructure Development”

Cummings sought to distinguish his criticism of the proposed agreement from opposition to infrastructure development or foreign investment.

He said the ANC supports responsible investment, public-private partnerships and the utilization of Liberia’s natural resources to accelerate national development.

However, he maintained that development must be accompanied by transparency, accountability and safeguards that protect the country’s long-term economic interests.

“We are not opposed to infrastructure development. We are not opposed to investment. We are not opposed to public-private partnerships. And we are certainly not opposed to responsible utilization of Liberia’s natural resources to accelerate national development,” he said.

“What we oppose is lack of transparency. What we oppose is secrecy. What we oppose is committing future generations to massive obligations without the protections and safeguards that responsible governance requires.”

He further argued that Liberians should not be forced to choose between infrastructure development and accountability, insisting that both objectives can be achieved simultaneously.

A Long-Term Test for the Boakai Administration

Cummings said the true measure of the agreement would not be the speed with which it was signed or the infrastructure promised, but whether its terms withstand public scrutiny and deliver lasting benefits to the country.

He warned that the consequences could extend 20, 30 or even 40 years into the future, potentially determining whether subsequent generations inherit improved infrastructure and economic opportunities or substantial financial obligations.

He therefore urged the government to pause, review, disclose and consult before proceeding with the arrangement.

“The resources under our soil belong equally to the market woman in Red Light, the farmer in Lofa, the fisherman in Grand Kru, the hunter in Bong, the student in Maryland, and the child yet unborn,” he said.

World.title: Mercy Corps Rebrands as Prosper Global After 24 Years in Liberia
World.content:
Organization Says Name Change Will Not Affect Ongoing Programs, Donor-Funded Projects or Partnerships as It Pledges Stronger Focus on African Leadership and Community-Driven Development

MONROVIA – International humanitarian and development organization Mercy Corps has officially rebranded as Prosper Global, marking a new chapter in its more than two-decade presence in Liberia while reaffirming its commitment to community-led development, economic empowerment and resilience.

The transition, announced Tuesday, November 24, in Monrovia, forms part of the organization’s global rebranding initiative aimed at strengthening its focus on locally driven solutions, African leadership and sustainable economic opportunities for vulnerable communities.



Despite the change in name and visual identity, Prosper Global said its mission, programs, partnerships and donor-funded projects in Liberia would continue without disruption.

The organization, which began operations in Liberia in 2002, has worked alongside government institutions, local communities, civil society organizations and private-sector actors to address development challenges and improve livelihoods.

Over the years, its interventions have covered youth employment, education, food security, economic inclusion, renewable energy, governance, climate resilience and humanitarian response.

Speaking at the transition ceremony held at the Royal Grand Hotel in Monrovia, Melaku Yirga, Prosper Global’s Vice President for Africa, said Liberia occupies a special place in the organization’s history in West Africa.



He noted that the organization’s work in the country over the past two decades has been shaped by the resilience, aspirations and leadership of Liberians.

Yirga said the transition presents an opportunity to build on that legacy by strengthening local leadership and supporting development solutions that reflect the priorities and needs of communities.

“While our name may be changing, our commitment to Liberia and our longstanding partnerships remain as strong as ever,” he said.

Among the organization’s major interventions in Liberia are the Ebola Community Action Plan (E-CAP), Economic Recovery from Ebola for Liberia (EREL), Promoting Sustainable Partnerships for Economic Recovery (PROSPECTS), Liberia Employment and Entrepreneurship Program (LEEP), and Liberia Empowerment through Attendance, Reading and Nutrition (LEARN).

Through these initiatives, the organization has supported youth employment and entrepreneurship, improved agricultural productivity, strengthened education outcomes and promoted social inclusion.

Meanwhile, Ambassador Charles A. Snetter, who represented the Minister of State for Presidential Affairs, Samuel A. Stevquoah, welcomed the organization’s new identity and commended its contributions to Liberia’s development over the years.

Snetter particularly highlighted the challenges confronting young Liberians graduating from universities and other institutions of higher learning, questioning how they would secure employment and establish sustainable livelihoods in an increasingly challenging economic environment.

He encouraged young people to engage organizations such as Prosper Global to learn about available programs and opportunities that could help them acquire relevant skills, establish businesses and achieve economic independence.

He also recalled President Joseph Nyuma Boakai Sr.’s repeated emphasis on youth empowerment, noting that the government remains concerned about the welfare, economic prospects and future of young Liberians.

Snetter congratulated Prosper Global on its transition and encouraged the organization to sustain and expand its development interventions across the country.

Speaking on behalf of international partners, Foday C. Bayoott of the Embassy of Ireland acknowledged Mercy Corps’ contributions to Liberia over the past two decades, particularly in promoting economic opportunities, resilience and inclusive development.

Bayoott emphasized that sustainable development requires placing local communities at the center of decisions and solutions that affect their lives.

He encouraged Prosper Global to build on the foundation established under Mercy Corps, strengthen existing partnerships and continue investing in climate resilience, inclusive development and community empowerment.

He also reaffirmed Ireland’s interest in continued collaboration with the organization and congratulated its leadership and staff on the new identity.

Under its new name, Prosper Global said it would continue working with communities throughout Liberia to expand economic opportunities for young people, improve food security and educational outcomes, strengthen resilience to climate and economic shocks, and advance inclusive and sustainable development in line with national priorities.

The organization maintained that the transition reflects its belief that lasting development depends on strong partnerships, local leadership and evidence-based approaches that address the root causes of poverty, vulnerability and exclusion.

About Prosper Global

Prosper Global, formerly Mercy Corps, is an international humanitarian and development organization working with communities affected by climate change, conflict and crises.

In Liberia, the organization partners with government institutions, civil society organizations, local communities and private-sector actors to strengthen resilience, expand economic opportunities, improve food security and education systems, and advance locally led development solutions.

World.title: Boakai Bets His Legacy on US$5.7 Billion MIDA, Promising Light and Roads Without New Debt
World.content:
Monrovia – President Joseph Nyuma Boakai has put his presidency behind a single agreement.

By Rodney D. Sieh

Speaking publicly for the first time on the US$5.7 billion Master Infrastructure Development Agreement (MIDA) with Bea Mountain Mining Corporation (BMMC), the President cast Wednesday’s signing as a turning point for the country.



“Today marks a historic day for Liberia as we lay the foundations for tomorrow,” Boakai said, according to prepared remarks obtained by FrontPageAfrica. “As I have always said, it is time that we ‘Think Liberia, Love Liberia, and Build Liberia.’ And this is being demonstrated here today.”

It is the boldest move of his administration: a bet that one company-backed deal can do what decades of donor programs have not, and give Liberia reliable power and roads that connect every region.

Two Problems, One Deal

Boakai framed MIDA as a direct attack on what he called “two longstanding binding constraints that limit Liberia’s growth”: the lack of electricity and the lack of roads.



On power, the numbers he presented are significant. Four new plants are expected to add 270 megawatts, more than three times the capacity of Mount Coffee, the country’s main hydro plant. The President said the system could eventually “support over 1000 megawatts down the road.”

He presented the VIA and SP-4 dams as the answer to the dry-season blackouts that have long frustrated Liberians and businesses. Together they would hold “around 10 billion cubic meters of water, so that the lights stay on all year round, even in the dry season.”

New transmission lines and grid upgrades are meant “to ensure that the power generated is transmitted beyond Monrovia,” he said. The 14 road and bridge projects, he added, fit his ARREST Agenda “to ensure that development reaches every region of our country.”

“Da What Will We Eat?”

Boakai anticipated the most common Liberian question about any large deal: what is in it for ordinary people?

“I know some will ask, ‘Da What will we Eat?'” he said. “The fact is, this Agreement holds more for every Liberian.”

His answer was concrete. He promised steadier power so “children [can] study at night” and families can store food for longer; clinics and hospitals that “keep their machines running”; and “power for the welder, the tailor, the barber, and the shopkeeper, without the daily cost of generator fuel.” He also pointed to market access for farmers and “thousands of new jobs and skills for our young people.”

The message was clear: MIDA is presented not only as an engineering project but as a kitchen-table promise.

Answering the Debt Question

The President also faced the issue head-on. A day earlier, former President Ellen Johnson Sirleaf had warned on ELBC Radio that the US$5.7 billion “has to be paid back” and urged an independent African Development Bank review.

“There have also been concerns about debt to Liberia under this Agreement and how we will pay for it as a country,” Boakai acknowledged.

His answer is the core of the bet. “Leveraging the rise in gold price,” he said, the government has arranged with BMMC “to ring-fence new revenue streams from the Corporation beginning 2027 to pay for the cost of all projects.” Government talking points add that BMMC “will continue to contribute to the Consolidated Account” and that these are “entirely new revenue sources.”

To reassure doubters, Boakai noted that BMMC has agreed to a US$500 million bridge financing facility “to ensure the projects do not run out of money and stall during the construction period.”

In short, the President is saying that Liberia can build without borrowing in the traditional sense, by using a gold windfall that did not exist before.

The Promise and the Clock

Boakai ended with a firm commitment. “My promise is this: we will deliver within five years, with the Biomass plant and transmission lines completed in just two years. In short, MIDA will build the economic backbone of a modern Liberia.”

That promise defines the gamble. The two-year projects would arrive around late 2028, ahead of the October 2029 elections, and give the President visible results to show voters. The dams and the full road program are due by about 2031, after his term ends in January 2030. His legacy will depend on work his successor must complete.

What Has to Go Right

For Boakai’s bet to pay off, several things must hold:

• Gold must stay strong. The financing explicitly depends on “the rise in gold price.”

• Delivery must be fast. Two dams, four plants, three transmission corridors and 14 road projects in five years is extremely ambitious.

• The money must add up. Government documents give the cost as both “more than US$5.45 billion” and “about US$5.7 billion.”

• Trust must be built. Sirleaf’s call for independent technical review, and her question about whether the President is getting “the right information,” still need an answer.

Sirleaf does not oppose the goals. “We want more roads; we want more lights,” she said, “but we have to be careful.”

The Stakes

If MIDA delivers, Boakai could be remembered as the President who switched on the lights in the counties and finally connected the country by road, something his supporters would say no post-war leader managed. If it stumbles, the deal could follow him into the 2029 campaign and well beyond.

Either way, the President has made his choice clear. As he put it on Wednesday: “This is being demonstrated here today.”

World.title: Rights Groups Warn Senate War Crimes Court Bill Could Undermine Independence, Urge Court by November 2027
World.content:
Monrovia – A coalition of human rights organizations has called on the Liberian Senate to revisit a provision that would give the country’s Supreme Court final appellate authority over the proposed Special War Crimes Court for Liberia (SWACCOL), warning that it could damage the court’s independence and credibility.

By Rodney D Sieh

The groups made the recommendation in a joint statement submitted to the Senate Judiciary Committee’s public hearing on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, on the Senate’s harmonized bill, “An Act to Establish a Special War Crimes Court for Liberia.”



The statement was issued on behalf of The Advocates for Human Rights, the Center for Justice and Accountability (CJA), the Civil Society Human Rights Advocacy Platform, Civitas Maxima, the Global Justice and Research Project, the Global Justice Center and Human Rights Watch.

Supreme Court Concern

The groups noted that, unlike some earlier proposals, the Senate bill gives the Liberian Supreme Court the last word on appeals. While they recognized the Supreme Court’s constitutional role, they said the arrangement “could affect the Court’s independence, impartiality and effectiveness or appearance thereof.”

The concern, they said, is “heightened by longstanding and well documented challenges facing the domestic justice system, including in relation to its capacity and independence.”



The coalition urged lawmakers to keep a majority international panel of judges serving alongside Liberian judges, and to consult experts who helped set up other hybrid courts, including the Special Criminal Court in the Central African Republic, the Extraordinary African Chambers in Senegal and the Special Tribunal for The Gambia.

“Let Us Maintain This Momentum”

Despite their concerns, the groups strongly backed the push for a court and urged all legislative committees to move “without delay,” with the aim of establishing the court by November 2027, in line with the Executive’s stated timeline.

“Our call is simple: let us maintain this momentum,” the statement said, adding that Liberia now has “a real chance to secure accountability for grave crimes committed during the country’s civil wars.”

They noted that Liberia will hold the rotating presidency of the UN Security Council in December, saying that advancing the bill now “would demonstrate Liberia’s leadership on justice and accountability.”

The groups cited war crimes trials of Liberians in France and Switzerland as proof that such crimes can be prosecuted, adding that “survivors rightly expect to see justice delivered at home.”

Other Concerns

The coalition raised several other issues with the bill:

• Timeframe: The bill reaches back to crimes committed from 1979. The groups recommended a later start date tied more closely to the outbreak of war in 1989, which they said would be “more feasible for the Court to manage.”

• Child offenders: The bill appears to allow prosecution of people who were aged 15 to 18 when the alleged crimes took place. The groups urged lawmakers to exclude anyone under 18 at the time, in line with international standards.

• Genocide: Since Liberia’s Truth and Reconciliation Commission (TRC) found that genocide was not committed during the wars, the groups suggested lawmakers consider whether including the crime is necessary.

• Definition of gender: The bill limits gender to “the two sexes, male and female.” The groups recommended dropping the definition entirely, as with comparable terms such as race in the Rome Statute, and relying on interpretation in line with international law.

• Victims: They welcomed provisions on victims’ participation and reparations but called for a clearer definition of “victim” and “harm,” and suggested reparations could be handled by a separate body, similar to the ICC’s Trust Fund for Victims.

• Investigative unit: They said the Independent Investigative Unit for Liberia (IIU-L), as a separate institution, should be governed by its own legal framework rather than the court’s statute.

• UN role: The bill provides for extensive UN participation, which the groups support, but they said this should be “confirmed and worked through” before the statute is adopted.

What They Welcomed

The groups praised the bill for including key international law principles: that official position offers no immunity, that following superior orders is no defense, limits on amnesties, and strong fair-trial protections.

They also welcomed the inclusion of sexual and gender-based crimes, including rape, sexual slavery, forced marriage and reproductive violence, as well as requirements for gender parity and at least 10 years of relevant experience for judges.

The statement credited the TRC, whose final report recommended a war crimes court, the Liberian National Bar Association’s 2021 draft statute, and the Office for the Establishment of War and Economic Crimes Court for Liberia (OWECC) for laying the groundwork.The groups urged the Senate plenary, House committees and the Joint Plenary of the Legislature to continue holding public hearings and consulting victims, civil society and legal experts as the bill moves forward.

World.title: Liberia: Jewel Howard Taylor Seeks Separate Trial, Wants Judge Feika Removed from US$317M Cocaine Case
World.content:
MONROVIA – Former Vice President Jewel Howard Taylor has launched two legal challenges in the US$317 million cocaine trafficking case, asking Criminal Court ‘C’ to separate her trial from those of 19 co-defendants and seeking the recusal of presiding Judge Ousman F. Feika.

By Willie N. Tokpah

The two motions, filed as pretrial proceedings commenced on Wednesday, November 25, introduce fresh legal questions in one of Liberia’s most closely watched drug-related prosecutions.



In one application, Taylor’s lawyers are seeking severance, which would allow her to stand trial separately from the other 19 defendants indicted in connection with the alleged international cocaine trafficking operation.

In a separate motion, the defense is asking Judge Feika to withdraw from presiding over the case, placing his continued participation in the proceedings before the court for consideration.

The applications present two distinct procedural questions: whether Taylor should face a separate trial and whether Judge Feika should continue presiding over the matter.

The specific grounds advanced by the defense in support of the motions will be central to the court’s determination. Neither application, however, amounts to a dismissal of the charges or establishes wrongdoing by the prosecution or the presiding judge.



Two Motions, Two Legal Challenges

The motion for severance seeks to remove Taylor from the joint prosecution involving 20 individuals accused of various roles in the alleged trafficking operation.

If granted, the application would allow the former Vice President to face a separate trial rather than proceed alongside the other defendants.

The second application seeks Judge Feika’s recusal, effectively asking him to relinquish control of the proceedings.

Although the motions raise different legal issues, their combined implications could significantly affect the direction and pace of the prosecution.

A ruling on severance would determine whether Taylor’s case proceeds independently, while a decision on recusal would determine whether Judge Feika remains assigned to the matter.

The court must consider the merits of both applications before the substantive trial can proceed.

From Airport Arrest To High-Profile Prosecution

Taylor’s legal battle follows her arrest on August 19 at Roberts International Airport, where security authorities stopped her as she prepared to travel to Accra, Ghana, to attend a women’s forum.

Following hours of questioning at Liberia National Police headquarters, former Justice Minister Cllr. N. Oswald Tweh announced that she had been formally charged with several offenses, including drug trafficking, criminal conspiracy, criminal facilitation, criminal solicitation, and money laundering.

She was subsequently detained at the Monrovia Central Prison.

However, citing concerns about her health, Judge Feika granted her compassionate medical release on September 4, placing her under strict home detention at her residence.

Her legal team later filed a bail application seeking to remove the restrictions imposed under the medical release arrangement.

On September 24, Judge Feika denied the application, maintaining the restrictions while the criminal proceedings continued.

The court subsequently ordered the permanent seizure of electronic devices recovered from her court-designated residence following allegations that she had violated the conditions of her medical release.

The Us$317 Million Cocaine Discovery

The prosecution stems from the July 21, 2026 seizure of approximately 3,971 kilograms of suspected cocaine at a compound along Cement Road in the VOA Community, Duazon, Margibi County.

Authorities estimated the shipment’s value at approximately US$317 million, making it one of the largest cocaine seizures in Liberia’s history.

Two foreign nationals, identified as Srdan Seles and Johann David Garces Grajales, were arrested at the scene.

The discovery triggered a wider investigation involving individuals from the security, aviation, and business sectors, as investigators examined allegations of an organized network transporting cocaine through Liberia for onward shipment to international markets.

On October 7, a Montserrado County grand jury returned a 55-page indictment naming 20 individuals, including Taylor.

Among the prominent Liberians indicted are Gerald Foley Smith, former Deputy Director for Administration of the National Security Agency, and Mark Quiah, former Deputy Director for Operations of the Liberia Civil Aviation Authority.

Other defendants include Nikola Ivancic, whom prosecutors identified as an alleged principal in the trafficking network; Croatian nationals Mihovil Vrovac and Taras Zadereiko; and several other Liberian and foreign nationals accused of various roles in the alleged operation.

The indictment contains multiple charges, including unlicensed possession, importation, transportation and exportation of controlled substances, illicit trafficking, criminal conspiracy, criminal facilitation, criminal solicitation, and money laundering.

What The State Alleges Against Taylor

According to the prosecution, Taylor was introduced to individuals linked to the suspected trafficking network while serving as Vice President.

The indictment alleges that she met some of the foreign nationals through Sheik Bashiru Kante, whom prosecutors describe as an intermediary between her and members of the alleged network.

Prosecutors further allege that Taylor traveled to Dubai to meet individuals associated with the operation and received financial benefits totaling approximately US$162,000.

The payments identified in the indictment include US$27,000 for travel, US$45,000 described as a shopping gift, US$75,000 allegedly donated to her Jewel Starfish Foundation, and another US$15,000 allegedly transmitted through Kante in August 2026.

The State also relies on WhatsApp voice recordings it attributes to Taylor, alleging that the communications form part of its evidence concerning her relationship with members of the suspected network.

Taylor has denied the allegations, while her legal representatives have questioned the prosecution’s evidence and the basis for linking her to the alleged trafficking operation.

In earlier comments to FrontPage Africa, her lawyer, Cllr. Gbawou Kowou, argued that the allegations against his client rely heavily on the account of Sheik Bashiru Kante, who is himself among those indicted.

Legal Questions Before The Court

The two defense applications have placed separate legal issues before Criminal Court ‘C’.

The severance motion raises questions about whether the allegations and evidence involving the other defendants should be considered in a joint proceeding with Taylor’s case.

The recusal application, meanwhile, challenges Judge Feika’s continued participation in the proceedings.

A recusal request must be determined on its specific legal and factual grounds. Its filing does not, in itself, establish judicial bias or misconduct.

Similarly, seeking a separate trial does not amount to an admission of guilt, an acquittal, or a dismissal of the charges.

The court must determine whether the defense has established sufficient grounds to warrant either request before the case advances to a substantive determination.

For the prosecution, the challenge remains establishing the alleged connections among the defendants and proving the individual criminal responsibility of each accused person.

For Taylor’s defense, the immediate legal objectives are to secure a separate proceeding for the former Vice President and have Judge Feika removed from presiding over the case.

Taylor, who served as Vice President under former President George Manneh Weah, maintains her innocence and remains entitled to the constitutional presumption of innocence unless proven guilty by a court of competent jurisdiction.

As the US$317 million cocaine case enters another critical phase, the court’s handling of the two applications could shape the next direction of the prosecution and determine the procedural course through which the former Vice President will face the charges.

World.title: Arthur Energy Africa Meets MME Deputy Minister, Announces Workers’ Arrival Ahead of May 2027 St. John Hydro Project Construction
World.content:
Monrovia, Liberia – Arthur Energy Africa (AEA), developer of the proposed St. John Hydropower Project, has held a meeting with the Deputy Minister of Energy at the Ministry of Mines and Energy (MME), Charles Umehai, and his team as part of ongoing efforts to advance the implementation of the project.

By Victoria G Wesseh

During the meeting, representatives of Arthur Energy Africa informed the Ministry that the company’s workers have arrived in Liberia and are preparing for the commencement of construction activities, which are expected to begin in May 2027.



The meeting also served as a follow-up on the project’s progress and an opportunity for the company to reaffirm its commitment to working closely with the Ministry to advance the development of the hydropower initiative.

Speaking during the meeting, Deputy Minister for Energy Charles Umehai said the Government of Liberia remains committed to expanding electricity generation and improving access to reliable power across the country.

Minister Umehai disclosed that Arthur Energy Africa, with support from Liberian and international professionals, is currently conducting field assessments along the St. John River Basin in Bong and Grand Bassa Counties.

According to him, the assessments include topographical surveys, environmental and social impact data collection, geological and geotechnical surveys, as well as sampling activities.



He explained that these activities form part of the ongoing preparatory work for the St. John Hydropower Project, which is expected to support the establishment and operation of several hydropower stations along the river.

The Deputy Minister noted that the assessments and other preparatory activities will continue as the project progresses toward implementation.

He further emphasized that the government is positioning itself to improve the living conditions of citizens through increased electricity generation and infrastructure development.

Umehai described Liberia as a country with significant potential in the energy market, noting that the government welcomes investments and initiatives that will contribute to expanding national electricity generation capacity.

He added that the St. John Hydropower Project is expected to play a significant role in strengthening Liberia’s energy sector, increasing electricity generation, improving access to reliable power, and supporting the country’s broader national development agenda.

World.title: Keynote Speaker Calls for Innovation, Ethical Leadership and Entrepreneurship, Urging Graduates to Apply Their Knowledge to Solving Liberia’s Development Challenges
World.content:
MONROVIA – Starz University has graduated 294 students at its ninth convocation and commencement ceremony, with keynote speaker Dr. Thomas Nimene Tweh Jr. challenging the graduates to transform their academic knowledge into practical solutions through technological innovation, entrepreneurship and ethical leadership.

By Patience Jones

The ceremony, held Tuesday, November 24, brought together members of the university’s Board of Trustees, administrators, faculty, government officials, parents, guardians and other distinguished guests to celebrate the achievements of the Trailblazer Class of 2025/2026.



According to the university, the graduating class comprised 266 undergraduate and 37 graduate students who received degrees in various academic disciplines.

Delivering the keynote address under the theme, “From Knowledge to Impact: Shaping Liberia’s Future Through Innovation and Leadership,” Tweh stressed that academic qualifications alone cannot transform a nation unless graduates apply their knowledge to address real-world challenges.

“Knowledge is important, but knowledge by itself does not build a nation. People who apply knowledge are the ones that build a nation,” he said.

He encouraged the graduates to look beyond academic certificates and traditional employment opportunities, urging them to embrace entrepreneurship, innovation and community service as pathways to national development.



Drawing from his personal experiences, Tweh recounted his humble beginnings in Trowein, New Kru Town, where he sold polo, Kool-Aid, doughnuts and meat pies to support his family before becoming a taxi driver.

He also recalled spending approximately 10 years as a refugee in Ghana following Liberia’s civil war, where he shined shoes and played musical instruments to survive before relocating to the United States. There, he pursued further education, established businesses and explored professional opportunities.

Using his personal journey to inspire the graduates, Tweh reminded them that their backgrounds should not determine the limits of their ambitions.

“Never allow the circumstances of your beginning to convince you that they are the boundaries of your future,” he told them.

Turning to emerging technological opportunities, Tweh identified artificial intelligence, digital finance and information technology as areas graduates could explore to help address Liberia’s development challenges.

He particularly emphasized the need for innovative approaches to improving education in rural communities, expanding healthcare access, strengthening agricultural production and connecting local farmers to markets.

“But technology alone will not develop Liberia. We must develop the people who can use technology intelligently and responsibly to solve Liberian problems,” he said.

On leadership, Tweh cautioned against the tendency to measure leadership solely by political appointments, public offices or positions of authority.

“We have spent too much time equating leadership with position. Leadership is not about being served, it is about serving,” he stated.

He further warned graduates against sacrificing their integrity in pursuit of wealth and professional advancement, stressing that character, honesty and personal responsibility must remain central to their definition of success.

By Patience Jones

“Success without character is ultimately failure wearing expensive clothing,” Tweh declared.

The keynote speaker also highlighted his contributions to education through the Nimene-Tweh Foundation, which provides scholarships and educational opportunities to Liberian students.

He concluded by reminding the graduates that the true value of their education would ultimately be determined by the contributions they make to society.

“Your degree is your achievement. But your impact will be your legacy. And the Liberia you help build will be your contribution to generations yet unborn,” he added.

Meanwhile, Starz University Founder and Chairman of the Board of Trustees, Ambassador Latim Dathong, urged the graduates to become entrepreneurs, innovators and responsible citizens capable of creating opportunities and contributing meaningfully to Liberia’s development.

In his commencement message, Dathong challenged the graduates to move beyond waiting for employment and instead explore opportunities to establish businesses, create jobs and develop solutions to societal problems.

“Liberia needs you. Our nation needs young people who are prepared to create businesses, develop technology, solve problems, serve their communities, and lead with integrity,” he said.

He also encouraged them to demonstrate courage, humility and integrity in their professional and personal lives, emphasizing that success should be measured not only by individual accomplishments but also by contributions to others.

“Success is not only about what you achieve for yourself; it is also about what you are able to give back to others,” Dathong added.

For his part, Starz University President Dr. Isaac Usung challenged the graduates to pursue professional excellence, embrace technological innovation and translate their academic training into meaningful contributions to their workplaces, families and communities.

“Your degree is a qualification, but what you do with it will define your legacy,” Usung said.

He also recognized the sacrifices made by parents, guardians, faculty members and university staff in supporting the graduates throughout their academic journeys.

Representing the undergraduate class, valedictorian Unison Nagbeh Meantuo emphasized resilience, ethical leadership and national responsibility, urging his colleagues to become problem solvers rather than merely holders of academic certificates.

“Liberia needs competent professionals. Liberia needs ethical leaders. Liberia needs entrepreneurs who create opportunities,” Meantuo said.

He encouraged his fellow graduates to remain committed to lifelong learning, protect their integrity and pursue their aspirations despite the challenges they may encounter.

Meanwhile, Graduate School Class President Yassah Saway Baysah shared her personal journey of overcoming depression, family responsibilities and academic setbacks following the death of her mother.

Baysah also disclosed that she had established a nonprofit initiative that has empowered more than 200 women through village savings and loan programs, operating four branches across Montserrado County.

Reflecting on the difficulties she encountered while pursuing her education, Baysah emphasized that perseverance and determination were essential to overcoming life’s challenges.

“Success is not measured by how easy the journey was. Success is measured by the courage to keep going when every reason to quit stood before us,” she said.

She encouraged her fellow graduates to remain resilient, pursue their professional ambitions and use their education and skills to create opportunities for others.

World.title: TECH Global University, recognized with the Google Partner Premier award
World.content:
The university has received a prestigious recognition reserved for only 3% of the top-performing companies worldwide

TECH Global University has been recognized as a Google Partner Premier, an annual distinction granted to the world’s most outstanding online companies. With this designation, Google highlights the work of just 3% of companies committed to offering high-quality digital services. For the university, it certifies that it has a technological infrastructure that provides students with both the most advanced virtual learning platform on the market and a dynamic, highly efficient web environment.

To achieve Google Partner Premier status, companies must meet rigorous requirements related to digital infrastructure performance. One key criterion is the optimization of web services, rewarding institutions that provide users with an efficient, flexible experience tailored to their needs. Studies show that the average loading time for a website is 3 seconds. If content isn’t displayed during that time, users abandon the site.

This is why Google places such high importance on web performance, as it directly affects the time a user spends on a specific page. In this regard, TECH Global University boasts a digital environment with a loading time of less than 3 seconds. All of this is made possible thanks to the optimization of its virtual platform and the quality of its educational resources.

Additionally, this award recognizes the quality of the specialists working at the university, evaluating the team of experts in digitalization and educational innovation that is part of the project. TECH Global University is home to dozens of specialists in marketing, SEO, SEM, and other fields, all continuously working to enhance the digital platforms. This all aims to improve the student experience and offer greater reliability in the processes.

This recognition also reflects the growing influence of the educational sector in the technological realm. Aside from increasing the presence of EdTech companies in a space previously dominated by other types of corporations, the synergy between the educational and digital sectors is working perfectly, shifting the paradigm from analog to new online pedagogical models.

According to recent reports by Research and Markets, the e-learning market is projected to generate revenues of approximately $701 billion by 2030, with an estimated compound annual growth rate of 14.6% for the period between 2026 and 2030.

TECH Global University, in the exclusive 3% of Google

The Google Partner Premier distinction not only accredits TECH Global University’s rigorous performance, investment, and digital infrastructure but also positions the university as one of the world’s leading institutions. This recognition further highlights the strong relationship the university has built with Google over the years, using the American giant’s functionalities in an ethical manner, tailored to the demands of today’s digital world. From this new badge, the university strengthens its close collaboration with Google in technology, promotion, and innovation.

Furthermore, this award aligns with the positive recognition TECH has received over the years. This success is driven by the perfect combination of cutting-edge technology and the highest level of learning methodologies, such as Relearning and the Harvard Case Method.

TECH Global University, the highest-rated university by its students

TECH is the world’s largest online university. With an impressive catalog of more than 14,000 educational programs available in 11 languages, it is positioned as a leader in employability, with a 99% job placement rate.

It is officially recognized in America, such as TECH Universidad (Mexico). It also has a strong presence in Africa, with TECH RUCU University (Tanzania) and TECH Euromed University (Morocco), and in Europe through TECH Global University (Andorra) and TECH Universidad (Spain).

Thanks to its international scope, TECH has a presence in more than 150 countries and has twice been recognized by the Financial Times as one of the 250 fastest-growing companies in Europe in recent years.

On the other hand, the prestigious Forbes magazine has distinguished it as the “world’s best online university,” highlighting its innovative learning methodology, Relearning, as well as the implementation of the Harvard Case Method.

In addition, it boasts an Ivy League faculty, at the level of Harvard or Stanford. Its more than 6,000 professors work in the best companies, organizations and institutions in the world. The largest multinationals (Amazon, Apple, Google, Nike…), the best hospitals (Mayo Clinic, MD Anderson Cancer Center…) and the best sports institutions (Boston Celtics, Dallas Cowboys…) collaborate with their best professionals to lead TECH’s academic programs.

The quality of its digital infrastructure and its high educational standards have been recognized by Google with Google Premier Partner status, a distinction reserved only for the top 3% of online institutions.

TECH is also considered the top-rated university by its students, with an average rating of 4.9 out of 5 in more than 25,000 public ratings on leading international portals.

World.title: State Not Ready as Court Adjourns Archbishop Banda’s Hilux Case to 9 December
World.content:
The Lusaka Magistrates’ Court has adjourned the case of Catholic Archbishop of Lusaka Dr Alick Banda, who is charged with possessing a motor vehicle suspected to have been unlawfully obtained. The adjournment came after the State told the court it was not ready to proceed. The matter will return on 9 December, after the prosecution team said its members were attending to an urgent matter before the High Court.

The State applied for the adjournment and told the court the High Court matter had not been on its diary. The defence did not object. Magistrate Mwandu Nakazwe granted the application but cautioned the State to be ready to proceed on the next date, and she extended Dr Banda’s bail.

This is not the first time the trial has stalled. Archbishop Banda was first due to stand trial on 3 November, a date the prosecution had said it was ready for when the matter came up for mention in October. On that day the case was adjourned to 6 November, and it has now been pushed into December without the State opening its case.

The hearing had been expected to deal with an application by the defence seeking clarity on exactly what the State alleges against the Archbishop over the Toyota Hilux. Dr Banda has filed a notice seeking an order compelling the prosecution to state whether it alleges that the vehicle was reasonably suspected of having been stolen or of having been unlawfully obtained.

The defence wants the State to amend the charge and specify which of the two alternatives it will rely on. It says each allegation calls for a different line of investigation and preparation. Without that clarity, the defence says, it cannot identify the documents, witnesses and other evidence it needs to answer the charge.

The defence is also asking the court to suspend the start of evidence until the application is decided. It wants the Archbishop to be given reasonable time to prepare his defence after any amendment to the charge. The application, it says, is meant to secure clarity on the accusation and protect Dr Banda’s right to a fair trial, not to delay the proceedings.

The particulars of the offence are that between 22 April 2021 and 27 December 2023, Dr Banda was found in possession of a blue Toyota Hilux, registration number ALF 7734, reasonably suspected to have been unlawfully obtained from the Zambia Revenue Authority (ZRA). Ownership of the vehicle was reportedly transferred into his name in April 2021, and the Drug Enforcement Commission (DEC) seized it in December 2023.

The DEC arrested and charged the Archbishop in September under Section 319 of the Penal Code, after questioning him at its offices in Lusaka. He spent time at Lusaka Central Correctional Facility, commonly known as Chimbokaila, while his lawyers worked to meet the bail conditions set by Magistrate Nakazwe. He has denied the charge.

The case now returns before Magistrate Nakazwe on 9 December. The State has been warned to be ready to proceed, and the defence application on the wording of the charge is still waiting to be heard.

World.title: Court Grants Makebi Zulu Laptop, Printer and Library Access to Prepare Treason Defence
World.content:
The Lusaka High Court has ordered that lawyer Makebi Zulu be given a laptop, a printer and access to the High Court Library so he can prepare his defence in a treason-related case. The ruling gives Mr Zulu, who is conducting his own defence, the means to carry out legal research and put his case together while he remains in detention.

The application was brought by his legal team of State Counsel Chifumu Banda, Mr Bonaventure Mutale and Mr Sakwiba Sikota. They told the court that Article 18 of the Constitution guarantees an accused person adequate time and facilities to prepare a defence. A laptop and a printer, they said, would allow Mr Zulu to do the research his case requires and build his defence properly.

The court granted the application in full. Mr Zulu will be allowed to use the equipment between 08:00 and 16:00 hours, which gives him a full working day for his preparation. He will also be able to work from the High Court Library in either Lusaka or Kabwe.

Mr Sikota said the arrangement was not unusual and that the courts had done the same thing before. He cited lawyer Edward Shamwana, who also chose to represent himself in a treason trial and was given similar facilities to prepare his case.

The Lusaka High Court also ruled on a second matter involving the same group. It allowed National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP) presidential candidate Mr Brian Mundubile, Mr Zulu and 16 others to file an affidavit in opposition. That order followed a preliminary issue raised by the State, which is seeking to stay the ruling.

The court then set a timetable. The applicants must file their papers by 1 December 2026, and the State must respond by 8 December. The State’s application to stay the ruling will be heard on 14 December, so both sides will have set out their positions in writing before the hearing.

Defence lawyer Mr Milner Katolo said the court has set 18 and 19 January and 25 to 29 January 2027 to hear the main petition. That petition challenges the legality and constitutionality of the applicants’ detention. Mr Katolo said the court will use those sittings to decide whether their continued detention is lawful.

Mr Katolo also explained where the case stands procedurally. He said that committing the matter to the High Court does not mean the trial has started. The State must still file the witness depositions and other evidence it intends to rely on and disclose them to the defence before the trial can begin.

The defence lawyer added that four of the 18 people first arrested have been left out of the treason indictments. They are former Anglican Bishop Trevor Mwamba, Mr Francis Mulenga, Mr Emmanuel Mulenga and Mr Darius Mwila. All four appeared before the Lusaka Magistrates’ Court and do not face treason charges.

For Mr Zulu, the new facilities arrive just before a run of deadlines. The applicants’ affidavit is due on 1 December, the State’s reply follows a week later, and the stay application comes before the Lusaka High Court on 14 December. The petition on the lawfulness of the detention will follow in January.

World.title: Makeni stun champions Power
World.content:
Newly promoted side Makeni All Stars produced the shock result of Matchweek 9 in the MTN Super League 2026 Transitional Season, beating Power Dynamos 2-1 on Thursday as Nkana FC and Green Eagles maintained their leads in Stream A and Stream B respectively.

Playing at home, Makeni fell behind when Congolese striker Andy Boyeli converted a penalty for Power Dynamos in the 25th minute.

The hosts responded before half-time, with former Chipolopolo striker Augustine Mulenga equalising in the 41st minute.

Micheal Hachipuka then completed the comeback for the minnows four minutes after the break, scoring in the 49th minute to seal a 2-1 win.

Despite the victory, Makeni remain bottom of Stream A on 4 points from 8 games.

Nkana FC continue to lead Stream A with 19 points from 9 games, followed by FC MUZA and Konkola Blades FC, both on 16 points.

Nchanga Rangers are fourth on 14 points, while Power Dynamos drop to fifth on 13 points after the defeat.

Zanaco FC are sixth on 11 points, NAPSA Stars seventh on 8 points, and Kansanshi Dynamos FC eighth on 7 points.

Trident FC, on 6 points, and Makeni All Stars, on 4 points, occupy the relegation places.

STREAM B: EAGLES HELD, ZESCO WIN

In Stream B, leaders Green Eagles FC were held to a 2-2 draw away to Mutondo Stars at Arthur Davies Stadium in Kitwe.

Joy Yolamu gave Eagles the lead in the 12th minute, before Emmanuel Mukosha doubled the advantage on the stroke of half-time in the 45th minute.

Mutondo fought back in the second half, with Chongo Chileya pulling one back in the 54th minute and Peter Makwati equalising in the 85th minute.

Elsewhere, Zesco United kept pressure on the leaders Eagles with a 2-1 away win over Chirundu United.

Veteran Nebert Musamba gave Chirundu an early lead in the 3rd minute, but Allan Mumba equalised for Zesco in the 26th minute, before Kabaso Chongo scored the winner in the 32nd minute.

In the other Stream B fixture, Red Arrows and Green Buffaloes shared the points in a 2-2 draw.

Golden Mashata put Buffaloes ahead in the 36th minute, with John Bukata making it 2-0 in the 40th minute. Jonathan Mada reduced the deficit for Red Arrows in first-half stoppage time, 45+2 minutes, before Eliya Mandaji equalised in the 52nd minute.

On the Stream B log, Green Eagles remain top with 18 points from 9 games, followed by Zesco on 16 points and Green Buffaloes on 13 points.

Chirundu United are fourth on 11 points, Kabwe Warriors and Nkwazi FC are on 10 points each, while Red Arrows are seventh on 9 points and Roan United eighth on 7 points.

Mufulira Wanderers, on 5 points, and Mutondo Stars, on 4 points, are in the relegation zone.

World.title: Pupil, 17, dies after being hit by train in Zimba
World.content:
A 17-year-old Grade 10 pupil of Naakowa Secondary School in Zimba District has died after being struck by a goods train travelling from Lusaka to Livingstone.

The deceased, identified as Arnold Hamangaba, died on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, at around 14:00 hours after being struck along the railway line near Treasure Compound.

Southern Province Commissioner of Police Moono Namalongo said in a statement issued on November 26 that the accident was reported to Zimba Police Station at 14:50 hours by Fred Mainza, 31, of Treasure Compound.

Mr Namalongo said the deceased, Arnold Hamangaba, was originally from the Mayoba area under Chief Sipatunyana’s chiefdom in Kalomo District and was residing in Treasure Compound while attending school.

He said preliminary information indicated that Hamangaba left home for school around 06:30 hours and returned at approximately 12:30 hours before leaving home again later.

Mr Namalongo said Mr Mainza, who resides in the same compound as the deceased, later heard a train horn and was subsequently informed that the pupil had been struck by a goods train.

He said police officers who visited the scene found the body lying face down on the railway line.

“Police visited the scene and found the body lying face down on the railway line. Upon inspection, multiple injuries, deep cuts on the head and crushed feet were observed. Headphones and a smartphone were also found at the scene.

The train did not stop after the accident”, stated Mr Namalongo.

He said the body had since been deposited at Zimba Mission Hospital mortuary, awaiting a post-mortem examination and burial.

World.title: Manyinga education official stresses need for stronger child
World.content:
Manyinga District Education Board Secretary Bornface Kawiza has urged stakeholders to intensify efforts aimed at safeguarding children from abuse and ensuring that they receive the education and support they deserve.

Mr Kawiza made the call through the Education Standards Officer responsible for Special Education, Bupe Mwewa during a child protection training conducted at Sikufele Teachers Resource Centre.

Mr Mwewa said the responsibility of protecting children should not be left to one institution but should be embraced by all stakeholders, including other government departments, traditional leaders, parents and cooperating partners.

He noted that children were more likely to attend school regularly, perform well academically and develop positively when they were raised and educated in safe environments.

Mr Mwewa further stated that circumstances such as poverty, abuse and inadequate support should not become barriers to a child’s right to education.

At the same training, Provincial Child Protection Officer Brian Banda called on stakeholders to familiarise themselves with the correct channels for reporting child abuse.

He explained that suspected cases should be brought to the attention of the police, social welfare officers or school authorities without delay, adding that strict confidentiality was necessary to protect victims from exposure and further suffering.

Mr Banda also urged stakeholders to strengthen their skills in identifying and responding to child abuse, saying proper training was essential in providing appropriate psychosocial assistance and referring affected children to relevant support services.

He said those involved in child protection needed to handle victims carefully to avoid actions that could worsen their experiences.

Mr Banda further reminded participants that government had established policies, laws and guidelines to prevent child abuse, protect victims and ensure that offenders faced the law.

The training concluded with stakeholders committing themselves to improving cooperation and strengthening child abuse reporting systems to ensure that affected children receive timely assistance and protection in Manyinga District.

World.title: Chilanga Council commits to forming collaboration
World.content:
Chilanga Town Council Chairperson, Buumba Mulunda, has reaffirmed the council’s commitment to strengthening stakeholder partnerships and driving sustainable development in the district.

Mr Mulunda stated that the council remains committed to creating an enabling environment for investment and ensuring that development initiatives respond to the needs of communities.

He noted that decentralisation, inclusive governance and environmental sustainability are essential to achieving meaningful development.

Mr Mulunda stressed that women, youths and persons with disabilities must have opportunities to participate in shaping the future of their communities.

He noted that the call by President Hakainde Hichilema for local authorities to attract investment, promote entrepreneurship, improve infrastructure and utilise their districts’ economic potential, speaks directly to the responsibility carried by local leaders.

“I believe that through shared responsibility, cooperation and accountable leadership, we can build stronger local institutions and deliver sustainable development,” said Mr Mulunda.

He called on all stakeholders to work together in making local government a driving force for economic opportunity, better service delivery and improved livelihoods for the people of Chilanga.

World.title: Chief Chibale wants construction of his palace expedited
World.content:
Chief Chibale of the Lala people of Serenje District of Central Province has called on the government to expedite the construction works of his palace.

Speaking when Serenje District Commissioner, Ellen Mibenge, paid a courtesy call on him at his palace, the traditional leader observed that the works on the palace has been slow and a source of concern.

“The house is currently incomplete, electrical connections are pending, the boundary wall has not been constructed, and several interior fittings remain to be installed,” he said.

He said the government’s decision to build chiefs modern palaces is a welcome initiative that supports their welfare and enables them to live in dignity while discharging their administrative duties diligently.

Serenje District Commissioner, Ellen Mibenge, assured the chief that government remains eager to complete the remaining works and pledged to engage the relevant authorities to ensure that works resume.

Ms Mibenge called on the traditional leader to engage his community and encourage residents to benefit from ongoing government programmes and initiatives

World.title: NUST  students get newsroom masterclass at AMH
World.content:
FROM the lecture theatre to the newsroom, the printing press and the fast-evolving digital marketplace, a group of 45 journalism students from the National University of Science and Technology (NUST) this Thursday received an immersive introduction to the business and craft of modern media during an educational tour of Alpha Media Holdings (AMH) in Harare.

HIGHER and Tertiary Education permanent secretary Fanuel Tagwira has challenged legislatures to enact policies to improve university lecturers’ working conditions.

World.title: TIMB orders destruction of 1ha tobacco crop grown from unapproved seed
World.content:
THE Tobacco Industry and Marketing Board (TIMB) has ordered the destruction of a Zvimba farmer’s tobacco crop after discovering that he had used an unapproved seed variety.

According to TIMB, the farmer bought the seed from an unauthorized dealer in Harare who allegedly claimed it had been sourced from Kutsaga, the country’s leading tobacco seed producer.

By the time the violation was detected, the farmer had already applied 750 kilogrammes of basal fertilizer and 150 kilogrammes of ammonium nitrate fertilizer, in addition to other production costs.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - November 26, 2026
World.content:
Fuel Tanker Explosion on Cairo Highway Kills 31 People

At least 31 people were killed and 21 others injured when a fuel tanker overturned and caught fire on a busy highway in Cairo, Egypt. The fire in the Warraq neighborhood, which also burned several nearby cars, left victims suffering from burns and smoke inhalation. The tanker, which belonged to a private contractor, was on the highway when a high-voltage cable fell on its path, and the driver lost control. The incident is being investigated by authorities. Emergency services have since cleared the wreckage and reopened the highway. The health ministry deployed 39 ambulances to assist victims, while hospitals treated those injured in the fire.

South African President Ramaphosa Wins Phala Phala Court Battle



South African President Cyril Ramaphosa has won a legal challenge against a parliamentary independent panel report that found he had a case to answer over the theft of $580,000 from his Phala Phala farm. The Western Cape High Court declared the report unlawful and set it aside in its entirety, ruling that the panel had exceeded its mandate and made legal errors. The decision effectively removes the basis for the current impeachment process. However, the opposition parties may challenge the verdict. The judgment does not find any wrongdoing. The scandal, which emerged in 2022, has continued to hang over Ramaphosa's presidency despite several investigations clearing him of any wrongdoing.

Nigeria Seizes 1.5 Tonnes of Meth in Cartel-Linked Lab Raid

Nigerian authorities have arrested five Mexican nationals and a local businessman following the discovery of an industrial-scale methamphetamine laboratory in Enugu State. More than 1.5 tonnes of the drug, valued at $227 million, were seized. The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency said that the operation followed a seven-month international investigation. The suspects are allegedly linked to a wider drug trafficking network involving Mexican cartel specialists and Nigerian collaborators. Nearly seven tonnes of chemicals and industrial equipment were also recovered. This marks the fourth suspected cartel-linked meth laboratory uncovered in Nigeria in recent months. The agency said the latest arrests bring to 10 the number of suspected Mexican meth production specialists detained in the country in recent months.

EU Extends Mozambique Military Mission to 2028

The European Union has extended its Military Assistance Mission in Mozambique until December 2028. It has allocated €17.17 million to support the country's fight against Islamist insurgents in Cabo Delgado. The funding will cover the period from January 2027 to December 2028, under a decision adopted by the Council. The mission will continue training, mentoring and advising Mozambican armed forces in military planning, intelligence, logistics and operational readiness, but will not participate directly in combat. The extension aims to strengthen the country's ability to independently plan and sustain military operations while promoting human rights and civilian protection. The renewed mandate follows a September strategic assessment that found continued EU support necessary to build sustainable capabilities within Mozambique's armed forces.

Egypt, Sudan Agree on Post-War Reconstruction

Egypt and Sudan have agreed to prioritise Sudan's post-war reconstruction, expand economic cooperation and strengthen coordination on Red Sea security. During talks in Cairo, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi and Sudanese Prime Minister Kamal Idris reaffirmed their support for Sudan's sovereignty and rejected attempts to militarise the strategic waterway. They insisted that its governance belongs to coastal states. The two sides also underscored the importance of respecting freedom of navigation in the Red Sea while rejecting attempts to "militarize the waterway or take unilateral actions that infringe on the sovereignty of its coastal states." The discussions also covered the voluntary return of Sudanese nationals, the repatriation of prisoners and efforts to restore Sudan's participation in African Union institutions. Idris also called for an inclusive intra-Sudanese dialog to build national consensus, address humanitarian concerns and lay the groundwork for reconciliation.

Close 

AI Fears Mount Ahead of Nigeria's 2027 Elections

Nigeria's electoral commission is investigating suspected AI-generated images and other irregularities in the country's preliminary voter register, ahead of the 2027 general elections, raising concerns about electoral credibility and preparedness. The irregularities reported included manipulation of facial features, duplicated identities, and dead voters' names. The Independent National Electoral Commission has established a special unit to monitor AI-related threats and deepfakes, as experts warn artificial intelligence could fuel disinformation, manipulate voters and erode public trust in the electoral process. Concerns were heightened by the history of online misinformation during elections in Nigeria and a record-low voter turnout of 27% in 2023.

World.title: South Africa: More Arrests Expected in Tembisa Hospital Scandal - South African News Briefs - November 26, 2026
World.content:
press review

More Arrests Expected in Tembisa Hospital Corruption Scandal

The Special Investigating Unit (SIU) has said that further arrests are expected in the alleged R2 billion Tembisa Hospital corruption scandal, involving businessmen accused of siphoning funds from the facility, reports EWN. The update comes as businessman Hangwani Maumela seeks to recover his Ferrari, which was preserved by the SIU. The State's curator sold the car for R10.1 million. The SIU is also engaging with alleged syndicate member Rudolf Mazibuko. Businessman Stefan Govindraju and his alleged accomplices are set back in court in February 2027.

Ramaphosa Extends TRC Cases Inquiry to 2027



President Cyril Ramaphosa has extended the term of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission (TRC) Cases Inquiry to March 31, 2027, reports SABC News. The deadline to submit its final report to Ramaphosa has also been extended to May 31 next year. The Presidency said that the third extension is necessary to allow more witnesses to testify before the inquiry, chaired by Justice Sisi Khampepe, concludes its work. The inquiry is investigating alleged efforts to obstruct the prosecution of apartheid-era crimes.

ConCourt Weighs Alternatives to Medical Negligence Payouts

The Constitutional Court is considering whether victims of state medical negligence should be allowed alternatives to once-off lump-sum compensation payments, reports EWN. The Eastern Cape Department of Health and other applicants are challenging a Supreme Court of Appeal ruling that overturned an order allowing victims to receive healthcare services instead. The department argued that large payouts place pressure on public healthcare finances. The court is set to hear arguments opposing the appeal.
