World.title: Uganda: 15,000 Young People Acquired HIV in 2023, 80 Percent of Them Girls, Parliament Warns
World.content:
Uganda's ambition to end AIDS as a public health threat by 2030 could be undermined by inadequate HIV prevention awareness and limited access to services among young people, Parliament's Committee on HIV/AIDS and Related Matters has warned.

The warning follows the committee's assessment of learning institutions in northern Uganda, where it found that many young people aged 15 to 24 still lack adequate knowledge about HIV prevention.

The committee, led by its chairperson, Stephen Kisa, the MP for Luuka South County, said the information gap, coupled with stigma and inadequate prevention services, threatens progress in the fight against HIV.

"Many young people lack adequate knowledge about HIV prevention. If we do not close this information gap now, we risk losing the gains we have made," Kisa warned.



At UNITE Unyama Campus, Dean Pario Lot Ewaku told the committee that HIV prevalence among the institution's approximately 600 students is below five per cent.

The institution works with nearby health facilities, maintains confidentiality and uses trained peer educators to promote HIV awareness.

However, Ewaku identified inadequate funding, deep-rooted stigma and a lack of clear intervention guidelines as persistent challenges.

Stigma also discourages some students from testing and seeking information or services, raising concerns about whether existing interventions are reaching those who need them.

At Gulu University, students and health workers cited staff shortages, inadequate condom supplies and the location of the HIV service unit as barriers to accessing prevention and care.

The concerns point to gaps not only in awareness but also in the availability and accessibility of services within learning institutions.

At Gulu Senior Secondary School, head teacher Irene Mwaka said the school works with partner organisations and student clubs to promote HIV awareness among its more than 3,000 learners.

However, she called for increased funding, noting that the school's day-school arrangement limits its ability to monitor learners beyond school hours.

Student leader Moses Okello said peer-to-peer engagement was essential in encouraging open discussions about HIV/AIDS and breaking the silence surrounding the epidemic.

He also called for continuous teacher training to equip educators to support learners seeking guidance without judgment.

The concerns raised in northern Uganda come against the backdrop of national figures showing that young people continue to account for a significant number of new HIV infections.

Uganda AIDS Commission estimates indicate that approximately 15,000 people aged 15 to 24 acquired HIV in 2023, with adolescent girls and young women accounting for about 80 per cent of infections in this age group.

Close 

Preliminary results from the 2025 Uganda Population-Based HIV Impact Assessment (UPHIA) put HIV prevalence among young people aged 15 to 24 at 1.5 per cent, compared with 2.0 per cent among young women and 1.0 per cent among young men.

The figures highlight the disproportionate burden of HIV among young women and the need to strengthen prevention interventions targeting this population.

Despite the challenges, Kisa said Uganda could still achieve its 2030 target if investment in awareness campaigns and accessible, youth-friendly HIV services is prioritised.

The committee's findings point to the need for learning institutions to strengthen prevention education, improve access to HIV testing and other services, address stigma and equip teachers and peer educators to guide young people.

For Uganda, the challenge is to ensure that the national ambition to end AIDS as a public health threat is matched by practical interventions in the schools and universities where young people spend much of their time.

World.title: Kenya: President Ruto Signs Law Outlawing Traditional Settlements of Sexual Offences
World.content:
Nairobi — President William Ruto has signed into law legislation barring the use of traditional dispute resolution mechanisms to settle sexual offence cases, requiring such cases to be handled through the formal court system.

The new law invalidates agreements reached outside the judicial process, including settlements through traditional practices such as maslaha, amid concerns that informal arrangements allow perpetrators to escape prosecution while victims are denied justice.

The Sexual Offences (Amendment) Act, 2025, sponsored by Garissa County Woman Representative Udgoon Siyad Kuno, also requires sexual offence cases to be heard on a day-to-day basis and concluded within six months from the date a plea is recorded.



The legislation further prohibits the withdrawal of sexual offence complaints through coercion, intimidation or inducement of victims, while barring courts from discontinuing proceedings solely because parties have reached an out-of-court settlement.

The law follows concerns that traditional dispute resolution arrangements have been used to resolve serious criminal offences, including rape and defilement, outside the formal justice system.

During the presentation of the Bill at State House, government officials said the measure was intended to prevent perpetrators from evading accountability through informal settlements.

"Things like maslaha, which are largely practised in part of Kenya, are now outlawed," an official said while explaining the legislation to the President.

He added that the Director of Public Prosecutions would not be able to withdraw sexual offence cases on the basis that parties had reached an agreement through traditional dispute resolution.

The National Council on the Administration of Justice (NCAJ), chaired by the Chief Justice, backed the legislation, arguing that alternative dispute resolution in sexual offence cases could allow offenders to escape justice while exposing victims to further victimization.

Officials said the six-month timeline was intended to address delays in the determination of sexual offence cases, which can prolong the suffering of survivors and undermine access to justice.

The legislation is anchored on the constitutional right to expeditious administration of justice under Article 50 and the provisions governing the administration of justice under Article 159.

The President also assented to the Sexual Offences (Amendment) Bill, 2023, which introduces measures to strengthen public awareness and prevention of sexual offences.

The law requires nationwide public education and awareness campaigns on sexual offences and available legal remedies, while directing the education sector to establish programmes protecting the right to education of survivors, including girls who become pregnant following sexual violence.

Close 

The measures seek to ensure that victims are not excluded from education because of sexual violence or its consequences.

President Ruto said the two laws would promote a better understanding of the provisions and limitations of the law and strengthen the country's response to sexual offences.

World.title: Africa: CAS Verdict Puts CAF Leadership Under Pressure As Experts Demand Accountability
World.content:
The Court of Arbitration for Sport's (CAS) decision to reinstate Senegal as winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations has triggered strong reactions from Nigerian football administrators and stakeholders, with some describing the ruling as a major embarrassment for the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and a defining test of its credibility.

Former chairman of the Gombe State Football Association, Ahmed Shuaibu Gara Gombe, said the verdict had far-reaching implications for both CAF and CAS, warning that the continental body's leadership could face questions over the controversial decision to strip Senegal of the title.

Speaking with LEADERSHIP Sports, Gara Gombe described the ruling as a defining moment for CAS, arguing that its authority, neutrality and credibility as the highest adjudicating body in global sports would depend largely on its ability to enforce its decisions.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

He noted that international institutions often faced challenges when their decisions conflicted with the interests of member countries, adding that the Senegal-Morocco dispute would test the willingness of football authorities to respect the jurisdiction of CAS.

"If this stands, that means the authority in global sports affairs as the policeman or the Supreme Court of global sports affairs is then assured and sealed, because this is a serious test case for CAS," he said.

Gara Gombe warned that any failure to enforce the ruling could undermine the court's legitimacy and credibility in international sports administration.

Turning his attention to CAF, he described the development as an embarrassment for the continental governing body, insisting that the decision to overturn the outcome of the final could have serious consequences for its leadership.

He argued that if CAF's decision to award the title to Morocco had been overturned, those responsible should be held accountable, adding that calls for resignation, including at the presidential level, might not be out of place.

Also reacting, former General Secretary of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF), Ambassador Fanny Amun, criticised the haste with which the decision to reverse Senegal's victory was taken, describing it as a controversial precedent for football administration.

Amun, who spoke with LEADERSHIP Sports, said football administrators must exercise caution when making decisions with far-reaching consequences, particularly after a match has been concluded and a winner declared on the pitch.

He argued that although there might have been lapses during the final, CAF should have handled the matter more carefully rather than take a decision that generated widespread controversy.

"Some decisions you don't take in haste. The reversal of the AFCON victory is controversial forever. This one is not a good reference point," he said.

The former NFF scribe maintained that Senegal had already secured victory on the pitch and celebrated as champions before the subsequent administrative decision to hand the title to Morocco.

He likened the controversy to football moments that become permanent reference points in the history of the game, arguing that administrators should understand the implications of overturning decisions after matches have been concluded.

Amun added that the experience should serve as a lesson to football administrators on the need to avoid hasty decisions, irrespective of their perceived competence or authority.

Meanwhile, chairman of the Advocacy for Nigeria Football Reform Initiative, Prince Harrison Jalla, described CAF's initial decision to award the trophy to Morocco as a shameful development that had embarrassed African football.

Jalla said African football stakeholders and supporters had widely condemned what he described as boardroom politics, insisting that Senegal were the rightful champions based on the outcome of the match.

Close 

He maintained that the CAS ruling had reinforced the principle that decisions taken by referees during football matches should be respected.

"It's a shame and embarrassment to CAF as a continental body, but African football stakeholders and fans outrightly condemned the CAF shameful decision to hand the AFCON trophy to Morocco in their boardroom politics. Senegal are the true champions on the field of play," he said.

On whether Morocco would be required to return the trophy following the CAS verdict, Jalla expressed uncertainty, questioning whether Senegal had returned the trophy to CAF after the initial decision.

The reactions come amid renewed scrutiny of CAF's handling of the dispute, with the CAS ruling restoring Senegal's status as 2025 AFCON champions and raising fresh questions about decision-making and accountability within African football administration.

World.title: Nigeria: Gunmen Open Fire At Peter Obi's Rally in Edo
World.content:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi in the midst of the people of Edo State in Benin City

The latest attack comes a few days after gunmen suspected to be political thugs killed six people, including a former state lawmaker, at an NDC rally in the neighbouring Delta State.

The police command in Edo State says it has intensified efforts to apprehend three gunmen who opened fire during a rally by presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, in Benin on Wednesday.

The command said the assailants, who arrived in a black Toyota Hilux, opened fire on people at the scene after encountering police operatives stationed at the Benin airport exit gate.

Eno Ikoedem, the command's spokesperson, disclosed this in a statement in Benin.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Ms Ikoedem, an assistant superintendent of police, said the gunmen made a U-turn after sighting the police operatives and opened fire before fleeing the scene.

She said one person, identified as Aimionkhale Micheal, sustained gunshot injuries to his thighs and was rushed to hospital, where he was receiving medical attention.

According to the spokesperson, the Commissioner of Police in Edo, Patrick Daaor, visited the scene and later went to the hospital to assess the victim's condition.

She said Mr Daaor also deployed additional personnel to the rally venue and hospital to prevent further attacks.

Ms Ikoedem added that tactical operatives had been mobilised, while strategic locations were alerted to track and apprehend the fleeing suspects.

"The commissioner has directed the Deputy Commissioner of Police in charge of the State Criminal Investigation Department to conduct a thorough investigation in collaboration with eyewitnesses.

"The command condemns the shooting and warns individuals and groups against actions capable of threatening public safety or disrupting the peace of the state, particularly during the ongoing political activities," she said.

Ms Ikoedem, however, urged residents to remain calm, continue their lawful activities and provide credible information that could assist the investigation.

She assured the public that all necessary measures were being taken to apprehend those responsible for the attack.

The latest attack comes a few days after gunmen suspected to be political thugs killed six people, including a former state lawmaker, at an NDC rally in the neighbouring Delta State.

World.title: Kenya: Ruto Orders Study Into Link Between Drug Economy and National Security
World.content:
Nakuru — President William Ruto has directed the National Defence University-Kenya to undertake a comprehensive study into the relationship between the illicit drug trade and national security.

Ruto wants the institution to establish how drug trafficking networks operate, their financing mechanisms and how they sustain organised crime and substance abuse across the country.

Speaking during the university's fourth graduation ceremony in Lanet, Nakuru County, on Thursday, the President said the findings would inform a coordinated, evidence-based government response to the drug and alcohol abuse menace.

He directed the University to work with the National Authority for the Campaign Against Alcohol and Drug Abuse, the National Intelligence Service and the Ministry of Interior in undertaking the research.



"We must understand how these networks operate, how they are financed, how they sustain organised crime and perpetuate substance abuse," Ruto said.

The President identified the drug economy as one of four emerging defence and security challenges that require urgent attention.

The other areas include climate-induced conflicts, security threats facing the urban informal economy, and the implications of artificial intelligence and cyber-security for national sovereignty.

Ruto said the research should generate practical solutions to strengthen the country's capacity to address emerging security threats.

Ruto further directed the National Defence University-Kenya to spearhead research into artificial intelligence and cybersecurity as part of efforts to safeguard national sovereignty and strengthen the country's technological independence.

Ruto has tasked the university's College of Defence Technology, working with relevant stakeholders, with developing a National Defence AI and Cyber Resilience Strategy to protect critical infrastructure and strengthen Kenya's technological capabilities.

Speaking during the institution's fourth graduation ceremony in Lanet, Nakuru County, on Thursday, the President said Kenya must develop its own capacity to create, deploy and regulate emerging technologies in line with national interests.

"We must build our own capacity to develop, deploy and govern emerging technologies in the service of our national interests," he said.

The President further directed the Ministry of Defence, through the National Research Fund, to allocate 100 million shillings to the university to support research into four emerging defence and security challenges.

World.title: Uganda: 10 Dead As Truck Plunges Into River in Zombo
World.content:
At least 10 people have been confirmed dead and four others seriously injured after a truck carrying cassava flour and passengers lost control and plunged into River Nyagak in Zombo District, marking the second fatal accident at the same spot in nine months.

The accident occurred at about noon on Thursday, November 26, 2026, at Nyagak Bridge in Mathawele Village, Oyeyo Parish, Nyapea Sub-county.

The truck, a white Fuso registration number UBF 816R, was travelling from Arua towards Lira when it reportedly suffered brake failure at the bridge.



The driver lost control, causing the vehicle to overturn and plunge into the river with its passengers and cargo.

Police said the truck had left Loro Market in Oyam District on Wednesday, November 25, carrying animals to Arua. On its return journey on Thursday, it passed through Zombo District loaded with bags of cassava flour, assorted items and passengers.

Police responded to the scene, documented the accident and evacuated the four seriously injured survivors, comprising two men and two women, to Nyapea Hospital and other health facilities for treatment.

The bodies of the 10 deceased were taken to Nyapea Hospital mortuary for postmortem examinations and further management.

The deceased have been identified as Fuambe Jennifer, Makwonga Kane, Olumu James, Oryema Valente, Judy Adubango, Jurama, Odongo from Palei, Odongo from Patek, Fosca Akumu and Okwir, the driver.

Divers were still searching for more bodies and possible survivors who could have been trapped underwater, with the truck remaining submerged in the river.

Preliminary investigations point to suspected brake failure as the cause of the accident. Inquiries are ongoing under Zombo District TAR 83/2026.

Second fatal accident at the same spot

The latest accident recalls a similar incident on February 23, 2026, when at least six people died after a commuter taxi, registration number UBJ 956G, plunged into the same river at Nyagak Bridge.

The Toyota Drone taxi was travelling towards Zombo/Alangi from the Hoima, Masindi and Bweyale area when it reportedly lost control while negotiating a sharp curve on the steep, rough approach to the narrow bridge.

Preliminary police investigations, registered under Zombo TAR 25/2026, pointed to suspected brake failure and loss of control.

The six fatalities included eight-year-old Sarah Akello, whose body was recovered on February 25; John Adriko; the conductor, Joshua; Kasamba; an unidentified woman; and a UPDF officer identified as Mungukende, whose body was recovered on February 28.

Close 

Local divers, sand miners, police and rescue teams from Nyapea Hospital helped retrieve victims and rescue injured occupants, several of whom were admitted to Nyapea Hospital. The driver and at least one other person were reported missing during the recovery operation.

West Nile Regional Police spokesperson SSP Josephine Angucia cautioned vehicle owners and drivers against using vehicles that have not been properly serviced.

"As inquiries continue, we urge owners of business motor vehicles and drivers to do proper services on their motor vehicles including repairs to the brake system before being used on the road, to prevent such deadly accidents," Angucia said.

World.title: Mike Tomlin calls Steelers situation following Aaron Rodgers vs. Mike McCarthy feud 'a dumpster fire'
World.content:
Mike Tomlin coached the Pittsburgh Steelers for 19 years, and although there was a Super Bowl high and that low earlier this year when he decided to quit, he never presided over something like the Aaron Rodgers vs. Mike McCarthy feud going public the past couple of days.

And Tomlin didn't like it. He said the prevailing feeling about the situation now is "just general sadness."

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

And worse.

SUPER BOWL-WINNING COACH MIKE TOMLIN LANDS NBC ROLE ON 'FOOTBALL NIGHT IN AMERICA' BROADCAST

"I'm upset about it," Tomlin said during a halftime interview with play-by-play voice Mike Tirico on NBC's Sunday Night Football broadcast. "Um, you know, it's a dumpster fire. And I don't say that in a judgmental way.

"I've presided over a few dumpster fires in my 19 years. But it certainly is upsetting, and I'm sure, Steelers nation is upset."

AARON RODGERS AND MIKE MCCARTHY DISAGREEMENTS AT HEART OF QUARTERBACK'S BENCHING BY THE STEELERS

On Tuesday the Steelers announced they were benching Rodgers and making him inactive for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos.

On Wednesday, Rodgers responded by going on the "Pat McAfee Show" and claiming McCarthy falls asleep in meetings, snores in those meetings, isn't prepared with the game play as late as Tuesday, misstated what team he coaches while breaking down the team at halftime of a game against the Philadelphia Eagles, and is generally "unwell."

Within hours, the Steelers released Rodgers. McCarthy denied falling asleep and missing meetings, and accused Rodgers of presenting him with "an ultimatum" about taking the play-calling away from the coach or he'd ask to be released – something Rodgers confirmed.

AARON RODGERS NFL CAREER SEEMS OVER BUT THREE TEAMS COULD CONSIDER QUARTERBACK AS A LATE-SEASON OPTION

"I had a range of emotions watching those course of events play out yesterday," said Tomlin, who coached the Steelers from 2007 through last season. "I think the prevailing [feeling] is just general sadness. Sad that we might be looking at the end of a legendary career of the quarterback, Aaron Rodgers.

"And just on the macro level, whether it's organizationally or for the game of football at large, to see laundry aired out that way in a public forum. Those are things that kind of run counter-culture to professional football."

Tomlin coached Rodgers last season and it is no secret he respected and admired Rodgers for year before that. That's one reason the Steelers were interested in signing Rodgers last season.

But Tomlin said it nonetheless shocked him when Rodgers pulled back the curtain on his feelings for McCarthy on national TV.

"It certainly did," Tomlin said. "But, you know, particularly because I know both men involved. Certainly had a lot of intimate work and and development of relationship with Aaron over the last couple of years and have known and competed against Mike, you know, respected and appreciated him as a coach for a long time."

There has been no Steelers player that either publicly or privately has said what Rodgers said untrue. Tomlin was asked how the quarterback is viewed in the Steelers locker room.

"He was beloved, and I'm not, you know, over-exaggerating that," Tomlin said. "He worked at it, and people appreciated his openness to getting to know and understand the Steeler culture, to be engaged with teammates."

How?

"Particularly from my perspective, I worked with a lot of veteran players over the years, and at times, they lose a little patience for the process," Tomlin said. "Or they lose patience for relationships with younger guys.

"Man, he seemed to embrace all of that and really embrace it in a real natural way."

STEELERS TEAM PRESIDENT CHOOSES SIDE IN AARON RODGERS, MIKE MCCARTHY SPLIT

So does Tomlin believe McCarthy can effectively lead the Steelers the rest of the way this season after what Rodgers uncovered?

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

And here's a hint to his answer: It's not a definitive yes.

"You know, it certainly created some challenges and challenges is probably an understatement if all of those things are true," Tomlin said. "...But his ability to overcome that, or inability to overcome that, in my opinion, is based on relationships."

That is an unvarnished view of the situation from someone who lived within that Steelers organization and culture for nearly two decades.

It doesn't suggest the Steelers are going to be fine.

World.title: Strobe Talbott, former deputy secretary of state and Brookings Institution president, dies at 80
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Strobe Talbott, a former deputy secretary of state whose deep expertise on the Soviet Union shaped U.S. foreign policy before he went on to lead the Brookings Institution, died Thursday at the age of 80.

Talbott’s son, Devin Talbott, said his father died peacefully after a long illness at his home in East Hampton, New York, The Associated Press reported.

An Ohio native, Talbott began his journalism career as an intern at Time magazine while studying at Yale and Oxford, where he was roommates with future President Bill Clinton. Clinton later joked that his job in their shared apartment was to make Talbott breakfast every morning.

NATO WARNS PUTIN COULD STRIKE BEFORE EUROPEAN ARMY RESPONDS, POINTS TO US AS MILITARY MODEL

While at Time, Talbott was tapped to translate the leaked memoirs of Nikita Khrushchev, the former Soviet leader ousted in 1964, which earned him a full-time role at the magazine.

Over a 21-year career there, he focused on U.S.-Soviet relations, led the Washington bureau, and wrote as a foreign affairs columnist.

In 1994, Talbott joined the Clinton administration as deputy secretary of state, helping guide U.S. relations with Russia and other post-Soviet states.

In a statement, Bill Clinton said no one was better suited to advise him on Russian affairs than Talbott, noting that former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton also relied on his counsel.

TRUMP PUSHED NATO TO SPEND BIG — NOW COMES THE HARDER QUESTION: CAN EUROPE ACTUALLY FIGHT?

"He was analytical, completely devoted to diplomacy, and on the level," Bill Clinton said. "With his expertise, we made real progress building trust between two former adversaries — moving beyond decades of confrontation to reduce the nuclear dangers future generations would inherit and build a Europe where more people could live in freedom and peace, including through the expansion of NATO and resolving ethnic conflicts in the Balkans. Together we laid the groundwork for greater cooperation while putting Russia on a path to democracy."

"Sadly, its current leader has taken the country in a different direction," Clinton added, referring to Russian President Vladimir Putin.

He described Talbott as a "good and brilliant man who made our world more peaceful and secure," and said, "Hillary and I will miss him very much."

After leaving government, Talbott served as president of the Brookings Institution from 2002 to 2017 and chaired the State Department’s Foreign Affairs Policy Board.

He is survived by two sons, Devin and Adrian, and six grandchildren. His first wife, Brooke Shearer, died in 2009; he later married author Barbara Lazear Ascher.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

World.title: Putin's grip on Crimea tested amid major blackout as Zelenskyy warns of looming Russian strike
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Russian President Vladimir Putin's control over Crimea faced renewed pressure Thursday as a massive blackout crippled the Russian-occupied peninsula, disrupting public transport and leaving people without heat, according to reports.

The blackout came after Ukrainian strikes had damaged the Kerch Strait Bridge last week, disrupting a key Russian military supply route, and as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Moscow was preparing another large-scale attack on Ukraine.

Russian-controlled utilities blamed the Crimea blackout on an accident at energy facilities outside the region, after reports of explosions and air raid sirens sounded across the Black Sea peninsula, according to the Kyiv Post.

PUTIN LAUNCHES UKRAINE BARRAGE HOURS AFTER TRUMP MEETING AMID ALLEGED RUSSIAN MISSILE BREACH OF NATO AIRSPACE

Meanwhile, Zelenskyy said Ukrainian intelligence suggested that Russia was preparing to target the country's energy infrastructure, logistics networks and essential services.

"Unfortunately, the Russians are already completing preparations for a new massive strike," Zelenskyy wrote on X Thursday following a coordination meeting. "According to intelligence, energy facilities and logistics infrastructure, as well as essential services facilities in cities and communities, will once again be the targets."

The Ukrainian leader also urged residents to remain vigilant, warning of renewed missile attacks.

"In the coming days, please pay attention to the alarms of missile threats," Zelenskyy said in his nightly video address Thursday, according to Reuters. "And in Russia, they should know that we will rebuild what is ours and retaliate against every Russian strike."

In Crimea, Russian-controlled electricity provider Sevastopolenergo said that Sevastopol had lost power, while electricity restrictions affected Simferopol, Kerch, Alushta and Yevpatoria, according to Ukrainian news outlet Ukrainska Pravda.

ZELENSKYY SAYS RUSSIA STRIKES HOMETOWN, CRITICIZES PUTIN-TRUMP MEETING

Streetcar services were also suspended in Yevpatoria and buses replaced trolleybuses on some routes in Simferopol. Parts of Kerch were also reportedly left without heating.

Russian-installed authorities had issued air raid alerts Thursday morning amid reports of explosions.

The blackout is the latest in a series of disruptions that have hit Crimea since late October, with Russian authorities blaming damage to power infrastructure.

The disruptions come amid mounting pressure on Crimea, which Moscow annexed in 2014 and has since used as a military and logistics hub for its operations against Ukraine.

The Kerch Strait Bridge, which connects the peninsula to mainland Russia, serves as a critical transportation link for Russian forces and has been targeted by Ukraine since Putin launched his invasion in 2022.

KUSHNER ENTERS UKRAINE PEACE TALKS AS TRUMP EYES SECURING SAFEGUARDS AGAINST ANOTHER RUSSIAN INVASION

The bridge was built after the Russian annexation and opened in 2018, serving as a symbol of Moscow's control over the peninsula.

Meanwhile in Kyiv, Mayor Vitali Klitschko also said seven people were wounded in an overnight Russian attack on the Ukrainian capital that damaged a shopping center and two other buildings, Reuters reported.

Zelenskyy also called for additional air defense assistance Thursday, emphasizing the need for interceptors for Patriot air defense systems and National Advanced Surface-to-Air Missile Systems (NASAMS).

"I expect a report from Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry on the results of its communication with our partners regarding the supply of air defenses — interceptors for Patriots and NASAMS are the key priority," Zelenskyy wrote.

It was the second time this week Zelenskyy had warned of preparations for another major Russian attack, according to Reuters.

World.title: Eagles erase 21-point deficit to stun Cowboys with biggest Thanksgiving comeback in NFL history
World.content:
Look, if you saw the 3-7 Philadelphia Eagles visiting the 5-6 Dallas Cowboys and figured it was time for your Thanksgiving nap, I get it. The NFL stuck them between Bears-Lions and Chiefs-Bills. When Dallas went up 31-10 late in the third quarter, it looked like you’d timed it perfectly.

Hopefully, someone in your family had the decency to wake you up for the fourth quarter. The Eagles took their first lead Thursday with two seconds left, when Jake Elliott drilled the game-winner from the Cowboys’ star at midfield. Philly’s 39-38 win was the biggest comeback in NFL Thanksgiving history.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

If you did sneak in a nap, the first half was the time to do it. By the time the Eagles and Cowboys kicked off, you’d already watched Caleb Williams hit Rome Odunze with three seconds left to give Chicago a 39-35 win. The Bears and Lions came in tied atop the NFC North, and Chicago left Detroit with a one-game lead.

CALEB WILLIAMS, WHO SEEMED TO DISRESPECT NATIONAL ANTHEM MONTHS AGO, SHOWS PATRIOTISM ON THANKSGIVING

Besides, you had to save some energy for Josh Allen vs. Patrick Mahomes on Thanksgiving night. The 9-1 Buffalo Bills were hosting the 8-2 Kansas City Chiefs in arguably the biggest game of the regular season so far.

Javonte Williams scores three touchdowns before halftime

Philly had already seen what this Cowboys offense could do. Dallas’ 38-21 win in Philadelphia last month kicked off a five-game stretch in which the Cowboys averaged 37.2 points per game. Two Dallas possessions into the rematch, they were already up 14-0.

Javonte Williams capped the 11-play, 77-yard opening drive with a 1-yard touchdown run. Then, on the ensuing Eagles possession, Quinnen Williams stuffed Saquon Barkley on fourth-and-1. Five plays later, KaVontae Turpin caught a short pass from Dak Prescott and sprinted up the sideline for a 31-yard score.

The Eagles finally got on the board with a 48-yard Jake Elliott field goal on their third drive, but Dallas answered right back. Prescott hit CeeDee Lamb for gains of 10 and 19 yards before Javonte Williams ran it in from the 12 for his second touchdown.

Eagles quarterback Joe Milton found DeVonta Smith on a 50-yard bomb to cut the deficit to 21-10 with 4:06 left in the first half. Dallas answered again, and the officials got plenty of screen time.

Three Eagles penalties gave the Cowboys 44 yards, including back-to-back pass interference calls that moved Dallas from the Philly 40 to the 1. After two Eagles stops, an offensive pass interference call on CeeDee Lamb wiped out a touchdown pass to Brevyn Spann-Ford and made it third-and-goal from the 12. Javonte Williams caught Prescott’s pass at the 8, dragged an Eagles defender to the goal line and fell across it for his third touchdown of the half.

By halftime, it looked a lot like Sunday against Tennessee. For the second time in five days, the Cowboys scored four first-half touchdowns and took an 18-point lead into the locker room. They led the Titans 27-9 and the Eagles 28-10.

Eagles roar back in the second half

For most of the third quarter, it looked like the second half would go the same way, too. Tennessee never got closer than 11 after halftime, and Brandon Aubrey drilled a 59-yard field goal to put Dallas up 31-10 with 3:35 left in the third. Then came two plays worth waking up for.

Milton found Smith for another bomb, this one a 45-yard touchdown with 15 seconds left in the quarter. Just 89 seconds of game time later, Ty Robinson blocked Bryan Anger’s punt, and Kenny Moore II scooped it up at the Dallas 3 and ran it in. Suddenly, it was 31-24 with nearly the entire fourth quarter left.

WHERE DOES AARON RODGERS’ INTERVIEW WITH PAT MCAFEE RANK AMONG THE WILDEST IN SPORTS HISTORY?

Prescott answered by hitting Lamb for 39 yards on second-and-16 and another 12 on third-and-8 before scrambling for a 14-yard touchdown himself. That put Dallas up 38-24 with 10:11 left. The two-touchdown cushion lasted all of 62 seconds.

Britain Covey returned the kickoff 55 yards, Milton found Smith twice, and then the Eagles quarterback ran one in himself from the 15. The Eagles went for two after cutting the deficit to eight, but Milton’s pass to Zach Ertz fell incomplete.

Philly forced a three-and-out, and Covey returned the punt 23 yards. With 7:37 left, the Eagles had the ball at the Dallas 49 with a chance to tie.

But DeMarvion Overshown sacked Milton on second down, and on third-and-15, Cobie Durant picked off a pass intended for Makai Lemon and returned it to the Eagles’ 48.

Dallas drove to the Philly 22, where Aubrey had a chance to make it a two-score game. Naturally, the guy who drilled one from 59 in the third quarter pulled this one wide left from 40. With 3:27 left, the Eagles still trailed 38-30 and had another shot to tie.

Milton took the Eagles 70 yards in four throws, the last a 24-yard touchdown to Makai Lemon with 2:10 left. He went right back to Lemon for the tie. This time the pass fell incomplete, and Dallas still led 38-36.

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

Because Philadelphia had all three timeouts and the two-minute warning, the Dallas offense needed two first downs to seal the victory. They got the first on a 15-yard strike from Prescott to Brevyn Spann-Ford on a second-and-8 play.

But they couldn't get the second. Javonte Williams had three straight carries to gain nine yards, leaving the Cowboys with a fourth-and-1 on the Eagles' 41-yard line and 55 seconds remaining. Instead of attempting a long field goal or punting, the Cowboys elected to go for a first down and the win.

Ty Robinson, who’d already blocked a punt, sacked Prescott on fourth-and-1. The Eagles got the ball back near midfield with 50 seconds left.

With seven seconds left and the ball at the Dallas 41, Philly sent Elliott out to win it.

He drilled it.

Hopefully everyone was awake to see it.

World.title: FLASHBACK: Two presidents pulled off secret Thanksgiving surprises for US troops — see the moments
World.content:

Under a cloak of secrecy, two American presidents made surprise Thanksgiving visits to war zones, bringing a taste of home to U.S. troops serving thousands of miles from their families.

Sixteen years apart, President George W. Bush celebrated with American troops in Iraq in 2003, while President Donald Trump served Thanksgiving dinner to service members in Afghanistan in 2019. Both visits were carried out under tight secrecy, catching troops by surprise as they spent the holiday far from home.

Trump secretly traveled to Bagram Airfield in Afghanistan on Nov. 28, 2019, where he served turkey, posed for photos and thanked American troops for their sacrifices amid the ongoing war.

INSIDE TRUMP’S INTIMATE MEETING WITH NATION’S BRAVEST SOLDIERS DURING WHIRLWIND TEXAS TRIP

"There's nowhere I'd rather celebrate this Thanksgiving than right here with the toughest, strongest, best, and bravest warriors on the face of the Earth," Trump told the troops at the time, later adding, "And you don't even know how much the people of our country love and respect you."

The visit came as roughly 12,000 American troops remained in Afghanistan more than 18 years after the U.S. invasion.

ARMY VET LAWMAKER MARKS ABBEY GATE ANNIVERSARY WITH BLISTERING MESSAGE FOR BIDEN-HARRIS: 'ABJECT FAILURE'

During the visit, Trump met with Afghan President Ashraf Ghani to discuss efforts to end the war and told American troops that the Taliban wanted to reach a deal with the United States. He said his administration was reducing America's military presence in Afghanistan while pursuing a political solution to the more than 18-year conflict.

Less than two years later, President Joe Biden oversaw the chaotic U.S. withdrawal from Afghanistan in August 2021.

WOUNDED MARINES RELIVE THE HARROWING KABUL AIRPORT ATTACK IN EXPLOSIVE NEW FOX NATION DOCUMENTARY

The withdrawal unfolded as the Taliban rapidly seized control of Afghanistan, culminating in the fall of Kabul and a frantic evacuation at the city's airport.

Sixteen years earlier, Bush pulled off a similar Thanksgiving surprise in Iraq , secretly flying into Baghdad International Airport on Nov. 27, 2003, to celebrate with American troops just eight months after launching the U.S.-led invasion that toppled Saddam Hussein's regime.

GEORGE BUSH WELCOMES TOP OFFICIALS TO HIS HOME STATE FOR 9/11 REMEMBRANCE ON 25TH ANNIVERSARY OF ATTACKS

Bush stunned hundreds of service members when he appeared at their Thanksgiving dinner, emerging to cheers and applause before helping serve a traditional holiday meal and posing for photos with troops stationed far from home.

"I can't think of a finer group of folks to have Thanksgiving dinner with than you all," Bush told the troops at the time.

"We're proud of you," he added. "Today, Americans are gathering with their loved ones to give thanks for the many blessings in our lives."

News of his trip was not even released until Air Force One had already left Iraq.

US FACES ANOTHER MAJOR MIDDLE EAST TROOP WITHDRAWAL, BUT THREAT REMAINS

Bush's visit came as American forces battled a growing insurgency following the fall of Saddam Hussein's government earlier that year. Despite Bush's declaration in May that major combat operations had ended, U.S. troops continued to face deadly attacks as the military worked to stabilize the country.

World.title: Olympic trailblazer Anita DeFrantz, longtime advocate for women in sports, dies at 74
World.content:
The sports world is mourning the loss of an Olympic trailblazer.

Anita DeFrantz has died, the International Olympic Committee and U.S. Olympic Committe said. She was 74. No cause of death was not immediately disclosed, although DeFrantz was believed to have been in declining health in recent years.

DeFrantz won a bronze medal in rowing at the 1976 Olympics, later becoming a powerful advocate for women in the male-dominated world of Olympic policymaking. She broke barriers throughout her career, becoming the first American woman and first Black American appointed to the IOC in 1986 before becoming the first woman to serve as an IOC vice president in 1997.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

DeFrantzalso was vice president of the organizing committee for the LA Olympics in 1984 and served as chair of the IOC’s Women in Sport Commission for two decades.

IOC President Kirsty Coventry, an Olympic swimmer who has credited DeFrantz with helping her rise to the highest position in the Olympic movement, described DeFrantz as "a mentor, a friend and a true inspiration to me, and to so many others around the world."

FIFA AWARDS 2031 WOMEN'S WORLD CUP TO THE UNITED STATES WITH MAJOR REVENUE EXPECTATIONS LEADING THE WAY

"From my earliest days in the Olympic Movement, she showed me what courageous leadership looked like, and what was possible for women in sport," Coventry said.

Edwin Moses, the record-setting hurdler and a contemporary of DeFrantz, said, "every woman who has a high-level position in sports today, they can thank Anita DeFrantz."

DeFrantz won bronze in the 1976 Olympics as captain of the women’s eight team in Montreal. She trained for an Olympic return and, in 1980, gained a sense of the disconnect between athletes and the boardrooms that made decisions on their behalf.

DeFrantz was part of the U.S. team that never made the trip to the boycotted 1980 Moscow Olympics. As spokeswoman for the U.S. athletes’ advisory council, she later led a lawsuit against the U.S. Olympic Committee, which had authorized the boycott under pressure from the Carter administration.

That experience marked the beginning of her effort to earn a seat at the table where those decisions were made.

Before her induction into the Team USA Hall of Fame, DeFrantz recalled realizing how much work remained when she attended her first IOC meeting in 1986.

JAPANESE BOWLING PIONEER RITSUKO NAKAYAMA, FIRST WOMAN TO BOWL PROFESSIONAL PERFECT GAME, DIES AT 84

"I walked in and I thought, ‘This is odd,’" she told The Associated Press in 2025. "It was this cavernous room" and of the 90 or so committee members, she was one of only five women.

"We had to help people open their minds a little," she said.

Women made up half of the 10,500 athletes at the 2024 Paris Games. Today, 46 of the IOC’s 106 members are women.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

U.S. Olympic and Paralympic Committee CEO Sarah Hirshland and chairman Gene Sykes remember DeFrantz as "one of the most consequential Olympians our nation has ever known."

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

World.title: Unforgiving rim denies Arkansas a miracle comeback against Michigan State on Thanksgiving
World.content:
With 1:18 left in a game played on Thanksgiving, Arkansas trailed No. 11 Michigan State by 10 and the Spartans were at the free-throw line. If you’d offered John Calipari one shot to send the game to overtime, I’m guessing he’d have taken it before you finished the question.

Well, he got his shot. Jordan Smith Jr. pulled up from 29 feet, and the ball found just about every part of the rim at Little Caesars Arena before it finally bounced out. Michigan State escaped Detroit with a 70-67 win to move to 6-1, and Arkansas fell to 4-3.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Arkansas took a 31-27 lead into halftime, pushed it to eight early in the second half and still led 47-40 with 13:31 left. If you’re a Michigan State fan who watched the Spartans lose at Tennessee nine days earlier, I can’t blame you for thinking, "Uh-oh." They’d made all of three baskets in the second half in Knoxville and shot 18% for the game.

MICHIGAN STATE'S PUTRID SHOOTING PERFORMANCE IN LOSS TO TENNESSEE PRODUCES LAUGHABLE FINAL BOX SCORE

Down seven in Detroit, Jeremy Fears Jr. hit a three. Then he found Jesse McCulloch for a hook shot and Coen Carr for the dunk that tied it.

Michigan State scored 15 straight, and by the time Kur Teng buried his third three in less than two minutes, the Spartans led 64-51 with 4:55 left. That’s a 24-4 run. The same team that went 3-for-26 after halftime at Tennessee went 17-for-21 (81%) in the second half against Arkansas.

Michigan State still led 68-58 when Fears stepped to the line with 1:18 left. He missed the front end of a one-and-one, but Arkansas still needed 10 points just to pull even.

COLLEGE BASKETBALL GETS A NEW NO. 1 AS THREE TEAMS FALL OUT OF THE AP TOP FIVE IN A SINGLE WEEK

So how did the Razorbacks make it interesting in the final seconds? For starters, Michigan State just couldn’t grab a defensive rebound. The Razorbacks missed two threes on the same possession before Billy Richmond III tipped the ball in with 1:03 to go.

Then Smith picked off a Fears pass. On the ensuing possession, Arkansas rebounded a missed free throw AND a missed three before Smith found Richmond for the three that cut it to 68-64.

Arkansas gets a very generous and-one

Jeremy Fears Jr. made both free throws with 16 seconds left to put Michigan State back up six. Then came the call I’d still be asking about if I were Tom Izzo.

Smith drove to the basket and spun past Fears for a layup. The officials called Fears for a foul, counted the basket and gave Smith a chance to cut it to three with 10 seconds left.

Did Fears foul Smith? Absolutely. Smith still had his back to the basket and was about 13 feet from the hoop when the contact came. Smith finished his spin, took another full step and then laid the ball in. How much continuation are we giving this guy? Even the CBS crew thought the foul should have been ruled on the floor.

Smith made the free throw with 10 seconds left, Fears missed the front end of a one-and-one with eight seconds left, and guess who came down with the rebound? Smith had six seconds and the length of the floor to find a three. From 29 feet, he came about as close as you can get.

A Thanksgiving bad beat for Michigan State bettors

If you laid 5.5 with Michigan State, how good did you feel with 1:18 left? Your team was up 10, and you had a career 81% free-throw shooter at the line. You could give up a couple of garbage-time buckets and still cash.

Fears missed the front end, Arkansas grabbed four offensive rebounds in two possessions, and Michigan State threw the ball away in between. And after all that? You were still covering when Fears hit both free throws to make it 70-64 with 16 seconds left.

It took that generous continuation call to put Arkansas back inside the number. Then your 81% free-throw shooter went back to the line with eight seconds left and missed the front end of another one-and-one.

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

That left Michigan State bettors rooting for the same guy who’d just cost them the cover. If Smith’s three drops, you get five more minutes to win by six. If you had Arkansas +5.5, on the other hand, you had every reason to cheer when that ball finally bounced out.

Which probably raised a fair question from across the Thanksgiving table: "Wait, didn’t you bet on Arkansas?"

World.title: ‘Shocking’ decline seen in hep B vaccination against incurable virus, including babies with infected mothers
World.content:
Fewer newborns are being vaccinated against hepatitis B, an incurable infection that can lead to liver disease, including babies whose mothers are known to have the virus, a large new analysis has found.

As of June, just 66% of newborns got the hepatitis B vaccine within a day of their birth, down from 80% in 2022. The birth dose serves as a safety net especially for babies whose pregnant mothers are unaware they’re infected with the virus and unknowingly transmit it during childbirth.

Up to 90% of babies with the virus develop chronic infections, putting them at risk for liver failure and liver cancer later in life. Vaccinating them at birth dramatically lowers those odds.

The new study from Truveta, a health care and analytics company, included medical records from more than 1.3 million babies born in the United States from January 2018 through June this year.

During that time period, newborn vaccination rates increased from 76% in 2018 to 80% in 2022 before declining in mid-2023, falling to 66% by June this year.

“It’s shocking to see a nearly 15% decline in three years,” said Nina Masters, lead author and principal applied research scientist at Truveta. “Infants born to mothers with hepatitis B have a 90% chance of perinatal infection. That can mean a lifetime of chronic liver disease, cirrhosis and early death. This is a real preventable tragedy.”

The decline began before federal vaccine advisers voted in December to abandon a decades-old recommendation that all babies be vaccinated against hepatitis B at birth. (That decision was later halted by a federal judge in response to a lawsuit filed by the American Academy of Pediatrics. The block remains in effect.)

The findings mirror increasing trends in anti-vaccine behavior in general. A recent NBC News data investigation found three-quarters of U.S. counties that track kindergarten immunization rates no longer meet the minimum threshold to prevent measles outbreaks.

Now, measles outbreaks are popping up nationwide, with nearly 6,000 cases and at least 13 deaths, according to state health departments. The U.S. lost its measles elimination status Nov. 16, reversing one of the country’s greatest public health achievements this century.

“We talk about measles being the canary in the coal mine. We’re seeing those outbreaks,” said Dr. Richard Besser, a pediatrician and president of the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation. “This one — hepatitis B and the rise in unvaccinated newborns — these are the kinds of things that are silent, that you don’t see for years and years until these babies grow up and end up having liver disease.”

The study, published Tuesday in NEJM Evidence, also revealed that hepatitis B vaccination rates have fallen among babies born to mothers known to be infected with the virus. Up to 98% of those babies were vaccinated between 2018 through 2025. But between January and June, that rate dropped to 94%.

Cases of acute hepatitis B fell dramatically in children after the the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention began recommending a universal birth dose in 1991, falling 99% from 1990 to 2019. A CDC analysis of children born from 1994 to 2023 estimated that hepatitis B vaccination prevented more than 6 million infections and nearly 1 million hospitalizations.

Last year, the University of Minnesota’s Vaccine Integrity Project published a review of more than 400 studies, finding no evidence of short- or long-term health problems from the hepatitis B shot after birth.

“Reversing the successes of previous public health programs puts individuals’ lives at risk,”

Dr. James Conway, a pediatric infectious disease physician and medical director of the UW Health Immunization Program in Madison, Wisconsin, wrote in an email. “It’s sad, tragic and preventable.”

World.title: Trump to visit maker of semiconductor chips, including Nvidia's
World.content:
A White House official said Thursday that President Trump is planning to visit the groundbreaking of a Phoenix facility for a manufacturer of semiconductor chips, including for Nvidia, a trip that comes as the company is under increasing scrutiny for the president's involvement in reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO after he had an affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy.

On Dec. 4, Mr. Trump will tour and deliver remarks at the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company facility in Phoenix, Arizona, a White House official confirmed Thursday. The Taiwan-based company has been expanding in Arizona since 2020, according to the company's website, and next week's visit will be to the latest expansion of its facilities.

A TSMC spokesperson also confirmed to CBS News in a statement that the president was expected to attend the groundbreaking.

The White House official said the new expansion is expected to fund more than 10,000 direct jobs and another 11,000 indirect jobs in the surrounding community.

It's unclear whether Arizona Democratic Gov. Katie Hobbs or the state's Democratic Sens. Mark Kelly and Ruben Gallego would attend the event next week.

The planned visit comes amid scrutiny of Nvidia, one of the world's most valuable companies, with its high-powered chips emerging as integral to the race for AI dominance between the U.S. and China. Co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang earlier this month resigned after the news broke of his alleged affair with Alice Huang, a former top executive at Singapore-based tech firm Megaspeed and who U.S. intelligence agencies suspected of spying for China. China has denied it.

Mr. Trump advocated for Jensen Huang to be reinstated at Nvidia, with an official saying earlier this week that reinstating him would "preserve America's technological edge over China, strengthen our national security" and ensure the future of AI will be built in the U.S. Sources also told CBS News that Mr. Trump was privately concerned about the broader implications for the U.S. economy should Nvidia's value collapse.

Nvidia's board reinstated Huang on Monday, and Mr. Trump touted his return in a social media post shortly afterward.

World.title: Powerful Thanksgiving Day storm causes flooding, power outages
World.content:
A Thanksgiving storm brought foul weather to the East Coast and Midwest on Thursday, causing major power outages, disrupting holiday travel and prompting the historic postponement of New York City's Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade.

More than 900,000 customers were without power Thursday evening across the Midwest and Northeast, according to the utility tracking website PowerOutage.us. Of those, more than 200,000 customers were without electricity in Pennsylvania, along with more than 100,000 in each of Virginia and Missouri.

By Thursday evening, more than 2,000 flights to or from U.S. destinations had been delayed and more than 420 were canceled, according to the flight tracking service FlightAware.

The storm hammered sections of the East Coast with torrential rain, high winds and flooding. All of New Jersey was under a state of emergency, declared by Gov. Mikie Sherrill on Wednesday night, as were parts of New York, following a declaration from Gov. Kathy Hochul. The weather service posted wind advisories from northern Georgia to most of the mid-Atlantic to southern New England.

Two men kayak down Hampton Boulevard as rain continues to fall, flooding streets and stranding drivers, on Thanksgiving morning, in Norfolk, Va. Stephen M. Katz/The Virginian-Pilot via AP

Stormy weather creates havoc in New York City

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Thursday morning that two people had to be rescued from their cars because of flooding. He cautioned people not to attempt to walk, bike or drive through flooded areas.

"We want to remind everyone to stay safe and there is no destination worth your safety," Mamdani said.

The New York City Emergency Management agency reported that the city received 1.5 to 2 inches of rain on Thanksgiving, with some parts seeing up to 3 inches. High tides brought flooding to the city's coastal areas, including portions of Staten Island and Long Island.

A person wears a poncho in high winds and rain during a Thanksgiving Day storm in New York City on Nov. 26, 2026. Adam Gray / Reuters

Central Park saw wind gusts higher than 30 mph, the agency said, while LaGuardia Airport recorded winds of 56 mph.

Macy's postponed the annual Thanksgiving parade until Saturday because of concerns about how the parade's massive balloons would fare in the wind-swept canyons between Manhattan's skyscrapers.

A car is seen stalled out in flood waters in Far Rockaway in New York City, on Nov. 26, 2026. Theodore Parisienne/New York Daily News/Tribune News Service via Getty Images

A high school marching band from Pearland, Texas, near Houston, said it raised a staggering $350,000 to allow its 500 members to stay in New York City for two extra nights.

"This was quite a challenge for us, and there was a very frantic and large call to action to our community to let the kids stay here and finish it out," Ryan Demkovich, the director of the Pride of Pearland Marching Band for Pearland High School, told CBS News on Thursday.

Visitors who had traveled to New York to attend the parade were forced to make last-minute changes to their travel plans. Amanda Anderson, a Florida-based makeup artist who was hired to do makeup for parade performers, told CBS News New York she was able to rebook her flights so she could stay an extra day.

A child stands in front of a chain-link fence looking towards idle parade floats in New York, Thursday, Nov. 26, 2026. Yuki Iwamura/AP Photo

"I was in Macy's, actually, when I found out, and I look up and there was like three girls crying already," Anderson said when she learned the parade had been postponed. "People were sitting down, very somber. It was an experience."

Major roadways flooded, holiday travel disrupted

The storm flooded coastal villages and cities from North Carolina through New Jersey as the high tide rolled in Thursday morning. Roads were closed and emergency workers were rescuing people from cars stranded in water.

Avalon, New Jersey, was seeing some of the worst flooding in its history, Borough of Avalon Business Administrator Scott J. Wahl said.

"Not quite Hurricane Sandy," Wahl said of the benchmark storm for his village on the far south of New Jersey's Atlantic coast.

Floodwaters washed debris over the road next to the shore, and a few drivers had to be rescued after driving around barricades and into floodwaters, but no injuries were reported, Wahl said.

Heavy rain and strong winds from a powerful coastal storm cause flooding across streets in Ocean City, New Jersey, on Nov. 26, 2026. Lokman Vural Elibol/Anadolu via Getty Images

Lance Miller, 54, said floods in his neighborhood of Ocean City, a small coastal town in New Jersey, are about a foot deep and that driving to the nearest grocery store would probably "destroy your car."

"I wouldn't do that, I'm a car guy," said Miller. "You're gonna have a good foot of water that you'd have to drive through."

Miller, who had his Thanksgiving Day meal preparations set, said he would be staying indoors and have dinner with his wife and daughter. But he said some of his friends in the area were "not so lucky" and had flooding inside their homes.

"So they're dealing with cleanup, you know," he said.

Flooding in Margate City, New Jersey, on Nov. 26, 2026. Margate City Fire Department

The Margate City Fire Department near Atlantic City, New Jersey, posted a video on Facebook of water pouring through the city's streets on a gray day even before heavy rains started.

A firefighter there said the tide was coming in ferociously and it was still an hour before its peak. Water closed in on steps to houses, and businesses had sandbags piled in front of their doors.

A stretch of U.S. Route 30, a major artery that goes into Atlantic City, was shuttered in both directions due to heavy flooding, the Absecon Police Department reported.

"Please stay off the roads until conditions improve," Absecon police said. "Do not attempt to drive through flooded roadways or around barricades."

Chester County Hospital in West Chester, Pennsylvania, sustained a partial power outage on Thursday afternoon, but power was restored before patients had to be transported to other facilities.

Residents of the Pennsylvania community of Springfield Township north of Philadelphia were asked to temporarily evacuate out of caution after a tree fell on a propane tank, local officials said. That evacuation advisory was later lifted.

A Lime scooter is swallowed up by floodwaters on Thanksgiving morning, in Norfolk, Virginia, on Nov. 26, 2026. Stephen M. Katz/The Virginian-Pilot via AP

The storm prompted the temporary closure of some coastal highways and bridges. The nearly 18-mile Chesapeake Bay Bridge-Tunnel over the Chesapeake Bay in Virginia was closed for several hours Thursday morning because of high winds, while NC 12, the only highway connecting Hatteras Island on the North Carolina Outer Banks to the mainland, was closed after seawater breached the dunes again and covered the two-lane highway.

In Maryland, nearly 2 million water customers in Montgomery and Prince George's counties, which are in the Washington metropolitan area, were asked to conserve water by the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission because of intermittent power disruptions associated with the storm. The water conservation request, which applied to all 1.9 million WSSC customers, was due to the risk that power outages posed to the agency's two water filtration plants.

World.title: Iowa lead detonation results expected soon, EPA says
World.content:
The Environmental Protection Agency said Thursday it expects to begin receiving sample results as early as Friday following the U.S. Army's detonation of a stockpile of degrading explosives at a munitions plant in Iowa.

The EPA collected more than 1,500 air, water, soil and dust samples ahead of Wednesday's destruction of the lead azide stockpile, followed by more than 1,000 samples after the detonation, the agency said. Samples were sent to multiple EPA and private labs for testing.

"The agency is expecting to start receiving lab results on post-detonation sampling as early as tomorrow," the EPA said in a news release.

The EPA said it collected samples at more than 130 structures, including homes, schools, daycare centers and churches, as well as at parks, nearby farms, drinking water sources and the Mississippi River watershed.

A contractor with the Environmental Protection Agency collects water in Augusta, Iowa, on Nov. 25, 2026. Austin Johnson/AP Photo

As of Thursday, no airborne lead had been detected throughout the region, the EPA said.

The agency said it is also testing for other compounds that may have been released during the detonation.

"The agency is testing for everything we were anticipating could potentially be released as a result of the controlled detonation," it said in Thursday's news release.

The Army on Wednesday detonated 5 tons of deteriorating explosives at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant located in the small community of Middletown, citing the risk of an unplanned explosion. Local residents and environmental groups had sought to block the detonation over concerns that a plume of toxic lead dust could threaten public health and agriculture.

EPA on-scene coordinator Sharon Kennedy, left, catalogs soil samples collected by her hired contractors in Augusta, Iowa, Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026. Austin Johnson/AP Photo

The Middletown plant housed about 10,000 pounds of lead azide, which has been used in ammunition since World War I. The EPA said the lead azide had degraded over the last 20 years it had been in storage. It had undergone a recrystallization process that increased "the material's sensitivity to friction and shock" and made it more susceptible to the "risk of unintentional detonation," the EPA said.

The 8th Circuit Court of Appeals temporarily halted the detonation last week while it considered whether to impose a longer-lasting ruling. On Monday, the court said the environmental groups challenging the plan had failed to show they were likely to succeed.

The chaotic lead-up to the detonation reached the White House, prompting questions within the Trump administration about what went wrong and who was to blame for not elevating the matter to senior officials sooner, sources familiar with the matter told CBS News.

President Trump praised the detonation as having "exceeded expectations."

World.title: High school band raises $350K to stay for Macy's Thanksgiving parade
World.content:
One high school marching band from Texas says it has raised $350,000 to cover the cost of its 500-member group remaining in New York City after the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade was rescheduled until Saturday due to a potentially historic storm hitting the region on Thursday.

"It's been exhausting and emotional to figure this out, but it has been incredibly humbling to see an outpouring of kindness," Ryan Demkovich, the director of the Pride of Pearland Marching Band at Pearland High School in Texas, told CBS News about raising the funds required to cover the extended trip.

"I started scrambling through that," Demkovich said. "Can we find a hotel to stay in? Can we get our transportation back? How, at the last second on a holiday weekend, how astronomical are the prices going to be?"

Other marching bands that traveled to New York from across the country are also raising money to cover the cost of their extended stays. For many of the high school musicians, the parade is a once-in-a-lifetime chance to perform for millions of spectators along the route and watching at home, and the postponement has made the trip significantly more expensive.

"This was quite a challenge for us, and there was a very frantic and large call to action to our community to let the kids stay here and finish it out," Demkovich added.

In just the span of a few hours, the Pearland community came together to raise hundreds of thousands of dollars.

"They organized a fundraiser, they went on news stations, they broadcasted it, they posted it to get the word across," Pearland High School senior and band member Deborah James told CBS News.

By Thursday, the band had raised enough money to pay for two extra nights at a hotel and to charter buses back to Texas after the parade on Saturday. One logistical challenge: They'll have to relocate from the Marriott Marquis in Times Square, which is booked for the weekend, to a hotel near the Meadowlands Sports Complex in New Jersey.

And they'll travel home by bus on Saturday because flights are booked until late Monday or Tuesday, Demkovich said. The donations also cover extra meals for the ensemble.

"We are going to make sure you stay there," Kevin Cole, Pearland's former mayor, said of the band. "We are going to make sure you get to perform."

The parade's delay also scrambled plans for tourists and family members who had traveled to New York to see the parade on Thursday. Among them was the Sims family, who traveled from Florida to see their daughter perform as part of the Great American Marching Band.

"We came up to see her. It's our first time in New York City," Dustin Sims told CBS New York. "We've had a great week, but now we gotta decide whether we're gonna stay another day or not."

Outpouring of support

Demkovich told CBS News that the group's fundraising push quickly spread across social media, soliciting contributions from Pearland businesses with a history of charitable giving and from strangers alike.

Several Texas businesses, including Gringo's Mexican Kitchen in Pearland and Houston's Mattress Mack and CenterPoint Energy, opened their wallets by making generous donations through a fundraising link on the marching band's website.

Eight other marching bands are scheduled to perform on Saturday. The Dobyns-Bennett High School Band from Kingsport, Tennessee, also issued a plea on social media, calling on its community to help defray the cost of the band staying in New York through Saturday.

"While we are grateful that our students will still have the opportunity to perform in this historic 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade during the Dobyns-Bennett Band's own centennial year, this unexpected change presents significant logistical and financial challenges for our program," the group said in a post on social media on Wednesday.

"Extending our stay in New York City means additional expenses that were never anticipated in our original trip budget, including extended charter bus rentals, additional nights of hotel accommodations, and meal stipends for our students," the group added.

By Thursday morning, the Dobyns-Bennett Band said it had met its undisclosed fundraising goal and that the band would be staying in New York through Saturday to perform in the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade.

"We have secured the necessary funding for the band to stay the extra night and to pay for the extended bus contract to get the kids home on Saturday!" the group said in the post.

World.content: Texas town keeps band in Thanksgiving parade After the Thanksgiving Day Parade was postponed, a Texas high school saw an outpouring of support to make sure the marching band could still perform. More

World.title: Trump claims "fake economic numbers" were released before election
World.content:
President Trump is spending Thanksgiving in Florida, where he had a policy meeting early Thursday morning and then headed to his golf club nearby.

He and first lady Melania Trump, who are staying at Mar-a-Lago, called U.S. service members on Thursday evening, including members of a unit that was involved in Operation Epic Fury, saying Iran "will never have a nuclear weapon."

President Trump and first lady Melania Trump speak to service members on Thanksgiving Day at Mar-a-Lago. Kent NISHIMURA /AFP via Getty Images

On Thursday morning, Mr. Trump posted a holiday message on social media, wishing a happy Thanksgiving to the "American patriots who have worked so hard to make our country great!" He continued in the lengthy post to wish a happy Thanksgiving to several others with whom he has grievances, including the Commerce Department, immigrants, "the radical far left" and more.

Mr. Trump claimed that before the midterm elections where Republicans suffered heavy losses, there were "fake Economic Numbers" released. Mr. Trump cited the Commerce Department on Wednesday revising the gross domestic product in the third quarter to 4.3% on an annual basis, up from a prior estimate of 3.4%. The Commerce Department regularly updates its monthly economic data to improve its accuracy, including not just the GDP but also the monthly employment data.

Although he did not present any evidence, the president demanded an investigation.

Mr. Trump also wished a happy holiday to "all of those people that have worked so hard to bring our Country to the Radical Far Left, those that are looking to change our Court System to that of Sharia, those who want to redistribute Property, so that all of the hardworking people that have built up, over a lifetime, a certain Wealth, will now be forced to distribute it throughout the Country, even to those who refuse to work."

The president continued his post with messages about the Somali community, deported immigrants and those who he believes do not appreciate the White House ballroom he is constructing.

Overnight, Mr. Trump praised the Army's controlled detonation of about five tons of degraded lead azide in Iowa, blaming former President Barack Obama for the situation and writing that no "carcinogens were released into beautiful Iowa air." Although Mr. Trump and other administration officials have praised the detonation, sources familiar with the matter told CBS News on Wednesday that prior to it, there was a chaotic lead-up inside the Trump administration about what went wrong and who was to blame for not elevating the matter to senior officials sooner.

On Wednesday night, Mr. Trump met with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, and the pair issued a joint statement describing the meeting as "very impactful" and focused on Russia, Ukraine and Iran. The statement said they discussed "the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war."

Mr. Trump earlier in the week continued the annual tradition of pardoning turkeys, sending turkeys named Freedom and Feathers to live on a farm in Texas. Melania Trump, meanwhile, welcomed the official White House Christmas tree on Monday.
