World.title: Croatia Can Expect €15.9 Billion in Revenue From Tourism
World.content:
November the 27th, 2026 – Croatia can expect to bring in €15.9 billion in revenue from tourism alone, with the prime minister discussing the second most important visitors.

Croatia should finish this year with slightly better tourism results than it recorded last year, and the value of fiscalised invoices is growing significantly faster than the number of invoices issued. Croatia should end 2026 with approximately €15.9 billion in tourism revenue, around 22 million tourist arrivals and 110 million overnight stays, Prime Minister Andrej Plenković stated on this week at a government session.

Reflecting on the results presented during last week’s Days of Croatian Tourism (Dani hrvatskog turizma) in Poreč, the Prime Minister emphasised that positive movements were recorded this year both in arrivals and overnight stays, as well as in the value of tourist spending. According to the data presented at that event, during the first ten months 21.3 million arrivals and 109 million overnight stays were recorded, representing growth of two percent in arrivals and one percent in overnight stays compared with the same period last year.

an 18% increase in fiscalised invoices in tourism

Particularly notable is the growth in the value of fiscalised invoices in the tourism sector. In the first ten months of the year, invoices worth approximately €8.6 billion were fiscalised, which is 18 percent more than in the same period of 2025. At the same time, around 410.4 million invoices were issued, or six percent more than last year. The value of invoices is thus growing significantly faster than their number, which points to an increase in the average fiscalised amount. A distinction should be made here between fiscalised turnover and revenue from foreign tourists, which is recorded separately in the statistics of the Croatian National Bank.

croatian tourists are now right behind the germans

Plenković particularly singled out the importance of domestic guests for Croatian tourism. According to him, Croatian tourists occupy second place among the most important tourist markets, right behind guests from Germany. Data presented at the Days of Croatian Tourism show that domestic guests recorded approximately 3.1 million arrivals and 13.6 million overnight stays this year. The Prime Minister also emphasised the importance of further investments in the development of continental tourism, especially projects that connect healthcare services, rehabilitation and the tourist offer. The government expects the continuation of positive trends during the post-season as well, along with preparations for the next tourist year. Although the final financial result for 2026 still needs to be confirmed, the indicators so far point to another year of growth for Croatian tourism.

World.title: Conference League: Sint-Truiden Beats Hajduk 2-0 at Poljud
World.content:
Hajduk were beaten 2-0 by Sint-Truiden at a near-empty Poljud on Thursday night in the fourth round of the Conference League, with Samed Baždar’s strike in first-half stoppage time and a superb Shinkawa goal after the break leaving Garcia’s side on six points with two league-phase matches to play.

Hajduk hosted Belgian side Sint-Truiden at Poljud on Thursday night in the fourth round of the Conference League league phase. A win would have taken Gonzalo Garcia’s side a big step towards the knockout phase and a first European spring in 32 years.

Because of UEFA’s punishment for crowd trouble at the Ajax match, Hajduk played without their usual support. Under UEFA rules, organized groups of children under 14 were still allowed to attend, and around 8,000 of them filled the east stand.

Sint-Truiden had backing of their own. The Belgian club bought 195 VIP tickets for a total of €15,600 and handed them out to their supporters free of charge.

Lineups

Hajduk (4-2-3-1): Silić; Acapandié, Hadžikadunić, Marešić, Hrgović; Fayad, Del Moral; Bamba, Dalisson, Šotiček; Martin

Sint-Truiden (4-3-3): Kokubo; Hata, Taniguchi, Musliu, Pupe; Shinkawa, Sissako, Ishiwatari; Vanwesemael, Baždar, Sebaoui

García left first-choice striker Michele Šego on the bench and handed Martin the start up front, with Marko Livaja ruled out by back pain.

Match report

he match got under way in windy conditions at Poljud, and Hajduk threatened from the first attack. Martin played in Hrgović, whose shot was blocked, though the Spanish striker had already strayed offside. Bamba looked for Martin at the far post with a cross from the right in the 5th minute, but it was too high.

Sint-Truiden’s first real attack came in the 8th minute, when Baždar’s shot from 18 meters was blocked behind for a corner, to the delight of the small group of visiting fans in Hajduk’s VIP section. A minute later the visitors had the ball in the net. Pupe crossed from the right, Shinkawa headed it down, and Musliu escaped the Hajduk defenders to score from close range. After a VAR review lasting more than three minutes, the goal was ruled out for offside against Musliu.

Hajduk almost broke quickly in the 15th minute, but Pupe got to the ball before Martin. There had been a heavy foul on Bamba in the build-up, though the referee kept his cards in his pocket.

Hajduk’s first big chance came in the 19th minute. Hrgović sent a superb ball into the box, but Martin could not connect properly. Hrgović then found Šotiček with another pass into space, but it was cleared behind for a corner, and Šotiček could not head down a Fayad delivery for a teammate.

Sint-Truiden had more of the ball for a spell without creating anything clear. Hajduk responded in the 28th minute with a neat one-two between Hrgović and Šotiček, after which Šotiček went down in the box following a challenge. The referee was close by and waved at the winger to get up. The ball broke to Hrgović, whose shot flew over.

Silić comfortably claimed a Shinkawa free kick in the 32nd minute, and a minute later Hajduk had their best chance of the half. Fayad beat his man brilliantly and slipped the ball into space for Martin, who was through alone in the box, but Kokubo saved. Šotiček headed off target in the 36th minute.

In the 39th minute Hajduk were awarded an indirect free kick when Kokubo picked up a pass from Pupe. The Japanese goalkeeper protested that Martin had deflected the ball, and replays backed him up, but the referee was having none of it. Dalisson’s thunderous strike from the edge of the box was superbly saved by Kokubo.

Dalisson was booked in the 42nd minute for a foul in midfield. Two minutes later Hadžikadunić took a risk on the ball but won a foul from Shinkawa, though he appeared to pick up a knock in the process and needed treatment. Five minutes of stoppage time were added.

Sint-Truiden then took the lead in the first minute of added time. Bosnia and Herzegovina international Samed Baždar picked up the ball around 30 meters from goal, skipped past a sliding challenge from Hadžikadunić, made space for himself and beat Silić with a powerful strike from 20 meters to make it 0-1.

Hajduk went into the break 1-0 down.

Garcia then made a triple change, sending on Šego, Pajaziti and Dendoncker for Martin, Dalisson and Šotiček.

It did not help. In the 51st minute Dendoncker lost the ball around 20 meters from goal, Shinkawa pounced, cut inside slightly and fired a superb shot into the top right corner to make it 0-2.

Sint-Truiden could have caused more trouble in the 55th minute, but Vanwesemael’s cross went wide of the goal. The visitors brought on Matsuzawa for goalscorer Shinkawa four minutes later.

Hajduk tried to respond in the 62nd minute. Pajaziti won the ball in midfield and carried it 20 meters before finding Bamba, who cut in slightly from the right, but his shot struck the head of the defender.

Apart from the Japanese midfielder’s stunning goal, the second half offered little, and Hajduk did not look like a team capable of turning the match around.

Sint-Truiden should have scored a third in the 68th minute. Vanwesemael crossed from the right for Ishiwatari, who was unmarked at the left-hand post but headed wide. A minute later the visitors replaced Pupe with Muja.

Fayad tried his luck from distance in the 72nd minute, but Kokubo saved.

Sint-Truiden made a double change in the 79th minute, bringing on Diouf and Merlen for Sebaoui and goalscorer Baždar. Huram was booked for a foul two minutes later. In the 85th minute Šego shot from distance but missed the target, and Garcia sent on Šutalo for Bamba.

A minute later Merlen tried to catch Silić off his line with a long-range effort, but it went wide. Three minutes of stoppage time were added.

Hajduk could not find a way back, and Sint-Truidense held on to win 2-0, leaving Garcsa’s side on six points after four rounds. Two league-phase matches remain, both against Danish opposition: Hajduk hosts Nordsjælland at Poljud in the fifth round on December 10, then travels to Midtjylland on December 17.

Mistakes are part of football. We did not deserve the victory. We had a few chances in the first half; maybe we could have gone ahead even. I am not mad at the situation itself, but I am angry at the game.

“The players are doing a lot of good things. But the reality today was that we didn’t do what we needed to do. We have a lot of quality, but we need to play 100%,” said Garcia after the match. “It’s normal that after so many games, something like this happened.”

“We are a young team. I am very happy with the team, always. I am proud of the work, but my job is also to make sure they don’t fall asleep.”

World.title: Ivan Anušić’s New 24-Year-Old Adviser Earns More Than a Retired General
World.content:
November the 26th, 2026 – Ivan Anušić’s new 24-year-old adviser Nina Mikulandra will allegedly earn more than a retired general. She is otherwise the vice-president of the Šibenik-Knin County HDZ Youth.

Defence Minister Ivan Anušić has seven special advisers. Ilko Cimic reports for Index that the highest individual net earnings among them will go to the newest member of his team, 24-year-old Nina Mikulandra, a recently graduated political scientist and vice-president of the HDZ Youth of Šibenik-Knin County. Her net salary will amount to around €1,850, which is more than the fees received by retired generals, war commanders and Anušić’s other advisers. No previous work experience was required for the position she holds. According to official data from the Ministry of Defence (MORH) analysed by Index, the highest fee among the previous advisers, €1,700 net, is received by Ivan Hampovčan. Željko Živanović, Božo Kožul, Ivica Ušljebrka and Luka Bandalo each receive €1,100, while Zvonimir Gvozdanović advises the minister without compensation.

The form of engagement also differs. Mikulandra is employed in the minister’s cabinet for a fixed term, at the latest until the end of his mandate, while the other advisers, according to the MORH form, are engaged with an advisory fee and without an employment relationship. We looked at who Anušić’s advisers are, what experience they have, how much they’re paid and what they are actually responsible for.

from the university classroom to the minister’s cabinet

Mikulandra graduated in political science this year from the Faculty of Political Science in Zagreb. She is the vice-president of the county HDZ Youth and a member of the Youth Council of Šibenik-Knin County. She was appointed Anušić’s special adviser on the 20th of November, following a procedure in which nine candidates met the competition conditions. No previous work experience was required for that position. Experience in the defence system, state administration or security policy was not required either. The only condition was a completed appropriate master’s degree in the field of social sciences.

MORH explains her selection with her academic results and performance at the job interview. They state that she completed her studies with the highest praise, summa cum laude, and that she received the Dean’s Award twice, both times with a grade point average of 5.00. She is also attending a postgraduate specialist study in “Security Policy of the Republic of Croatia.” According to the Ministry’s response, she showed the best competences and motivation at the interview. The final decision on the appointment was made by Minister Anušić.

what will she actually do for the salary?

The basic gross salary of the new adviser is €2,794.50. With residence in Zagreb and without additional tax reliefs, that would mean around €1,850 net. The competition lists support tasks for the minister, advising, preparation for strategic planning and cooperation with the media. At the same time it is stated that the person in that position is not a civil servant and “does not perform tasks within the competence of the Ministry of Defence.” MORH replied to Index that her tasks will include “support to the minister and assistance in the implementation of the established policy of the Government of the Republic of Croatia.” They did not, however, specify concrete projects she will take on or the results expected of her.

The best-paid adviser from the previous list, Ivan Hampovčan, is a law graduate and former secretary of Osijek-Baranja County. He was appointed to that position back in 2017, when Anušić became county prefect. Earlier he worked at the RODA development agency in Antunovac, the municipality Anušić ran before moving to the county. Since May this year, Hampovčan has also been listed in the register of the Commission for Deciding on Conflict of Interest as the director of the county Pharmacies Srce. For advising the defence minister he receives €1,700. The MORH form states that he is engaged for “drawing up analyses and opinions and giving advice on individual issues within the competence of the defence sector.” Which issues those are is not explained in the document.

retired generals and commanders receive less than 24-year-old loyal hdz member mikulandra

Željko Živanović is a retired major general and Vukovar defender. He took part in the defence of Vukovar and after the war held positions in the military education system. MORH lists him in official announcements as a special adviser to the defence minister. For that work he receives €1,100. The same amount is received by Božo Kožul, the former commander of the 1st Guard Brigade “Tigers.” During the war he held command duties in that unit and was retired back in 2001. Ivica Ušljebrka, a retired colonel and wartime member of the 4th Guard Brigade “Spiders,” also receives €1,100. He was an adviser during the term of Minister Damir Krstičević and remained in that position under Anušić. For none of them does the official MORH form state a concrete area of work; descriptions of their duties are limited to drawing up analyses and giving opinions and advice on issues within the defence sector.

the director of a state-owned company is also among the advisers

Anušić is also advised by Luka Bandalo, whom the state agency ALAN, responsible for trade in arms and military equipment, presents as its operational director. For advice and opinions on issues within the defence sector he receives €1,100. The only one who, according to the official list, advises the minister without compensation is Zvonimir Gvozdanović, a doctor of dental medicine and director of the Vukovar Health Centre. He too is engaged for drawing up analyses and giving advice on individual issues within the competence of the defence sector. What those issues are cannot be determined from the MORH form.

there was also a former journalist among the ranks

It should certainly be noted that Mikulandra is not the first person Anušić employed as a special adviser in his cabinet. That position was also held after his arrival at MORH by former journalist Iva Puljić Šego. In January 2024 the Ministry confirmed to Index that she was appointed after a competition published on 22 November 2023, also for support tasks for the minister and at the latest until the end of his mandate.

Puljić Šego is no longer a special adviser but is listed by MORH as a civil servant employed within the Ministry of Defence system. As a reminder, Minister Anušić said in Parliament that it was he who had leaked information, not his associate and MORH spokesperson Iva Puljić Šego, who after an investigation by the Military Security and Intelligence Agency (VSOA) lost her NATO security clearance.

World.title: Fake Doctor Defrauds Zagreb Woman of 9,000 Euros
World.content:
November the 26th, 2026 – A fake doctor has defrauded a Zagreb woman of 9,000 euros, and it turns out the police are already well aware of the individual in question.

Zagreb police have been met with another case of fraud in which the perpetrators posed as no less than doctors. Index reports that they convinced a Zagreb woman that a member of her family needed urgent surgery, after which she handed them 9,000 euros. Police suspected a 42-year-old man for the fraud, who is already in investigative detention for allegedly committing fraud previously.

His currently unknown accomplice has not yet been located. According to police suspicions, the two men contacted the 70-year-old woman by phone and misled her into believing that a family member of hers needed urgent surgery that had to be paid for. The woman believed their story and handed the money over to the 42-year-old.

he was previously arrested at the croatian-serbian border

This is a man against whom the police have already filed criminal charges multiple times for various criminal offences. Back in October, together with a 70-year-old man, he was arrested at the Bajakovo border crossing while attempting to exit Croatia into Serbia. Police suspect them of defrauding a 69-year-old woman from Zagreb’s Susedgrad district, whom they convinced that her daughter had been injured in a traffic accident. Material damage in that case amounted to around 50,000 euros. During a search of his vehicle, police officers found a hidden pouch with money in a portable cooler, which they suspect came from the fraud.

police have issued a public warning

The police have repeatedly warned the general public about scams in which perpetrators pose as doctors and exploit their fear for family members. They therefore advise people to never hand over any money in the event of such a call, to verify the information with family members, and to notify the police immediately. A special report has been filed against the 42-year-old with the competent state attorney’s office, and the criminal investigation continues.

World.title: Mate Rimac Recalls His Argument With Volkswagen Over Bugatti
World.content:
November the 26th, 2026 – Croatian entrepreneur Mate Rimac recalled his intense argument with Volkswagen over Bugatti in a recent interview with the Classic Driver portal.

In an interview for the automotive portal Classic Driver, Mate Rimac revealed previously lesser-known details about the acquisition of Bugatti and fierce disagreements with the leaders of the Volkswagen Group regarding the future of the French car brand. Index reports that according to his recollection of events, the Germans initially wanted the successor to the Chiron to be an electric SUV with four seats, and later insisted on an all-electric hypercar. Rimac, who built his career precisely on the development of electric hypercars, opposed their plans. He also recounted how he went from being a potential manufacturer of the new Bugatti to acquiring the entire company, reports Motor1.

volkswagen allegedly wanted an electric suv

The story began back in 2020, at a time of great enthusiasm in the automotive industry for electric vehicles. The Volkswagen Group was then considering the possibility of Bugatti’s Chiron being succeeded by an all-electric SUV with four seats. Rimac’s company participated in the development of the electric powertrain for that car, which was supposed to use technology developed for the Nevera. However, it soon became apparent that the realization of the project would be extremely demanding and expensive. For such a car, it was not possible to use any of the existing platforms, so Volkswagen would have to invest billions in developing a completely new one. The project ultimately didn’t prove to be economically viable and as such did not get the green light from the German management.

“why don’t you just take over the entire company?

Since Bugatti did not have a viable plan for a successor to the Chiron, Rimac saw a business opportunity in this. He proposed to the leaders of the Volkswagen Group that his company take over the development and production of the entire car, while Volkswagen would be in charge of its sales. At one of the meetings, he received an answer he did not expect.

“Why don’t you just take over the whole company?” one of the Volkswagen Group leaders asked him.

Rimac initially thought it was a joke. Upon returning home, he didn’t even mention the offer to his associates. However, a few months later, the same man called him and asked why he hadn’t gotten back to him. Only then did Rimac realise that the offer was serious. Negotiations followed that lasted two and a half years.

“i had an extremely serious argument with them”

When the question of Bugatti’s future came up during the negotiations, the leaders of Volkswagen and Porsche told Rimac that the next Bugatti hypercar had to be all-electric. Considering that Rimac had by then developed the electric hypercars Concept One and Nevera and collaborated with major car manufacturers on the development of battery technology, such a choice seemed logical at first glance.

However, Rimac believed that this would be the wrong move for Bugatti. “I had an extremely serious argument with them because I thought it was the wrong move for Bugatti. I said: ‘No, I don’t want to make an electric Bugatti,'” he recounted.

The Volkswagen Group eventually agreed to the development of a car with a hybrid power-train, but in order to reduce costs, it wanted to keep the existing Chiron platform. Rimac opposed this proposal as well. He believed that adapting the existing structure of the car to batteries would require too many compromises. Even before the completion of the negotiations on the acquisition of Bugatti, his company financed the start of the development of a completely new gasoline engine with its own money in collaboration with the British engineering company Cosworth. To test the feasibility of the project, engineers first built a prototype engine with only four cylinders, or a quarter of the planned V16 engine. This allowed them to test performance and emissions and estimate the costs and time required for development. The results, it seems, were good enough for Rimac to convince the other participants in the project of his vision.

now, all the new bugatti units have been sold

The result of multi-year development was the Bugatti Tourbillon, unveiled back in 2024. Instead of an all-electric power-train, it got a new naturally aspirated 8.3-litre V16 engine combined with electric motors. Six years after the start of development, Rimac says his decision paid off. Bugatti has, according to his words, already sold all units of the Tourbillon it plans to produce. Motor1 also points out the irony of the whole story. The man who developed one of the fastest electric cars in the world ended up being the one who convinced the leaders of one of the world’s largest automotive conglomerates that their most prestigious brand should not switch to an all-electric power-train.

World.title: Resolution on Vukovar Undergoes Five Changes
World.content:
November the 26th, 2026 – The resolution on Vukovar will undergo five changes, and now the liberals will support it as well. Here’s all you need to know.

Political groups in the European Parliament have reached an agreement on the text of a resolution marking the 35th anniversary of the fall and destruction of Vukovar. Index reports that five amendments have been incorporated into the proposal initiated by Croatian MEPs, including a reference to the apology by former Serbian President Boris Tadić at Ovčara and a change in the wording regarding the responsibility of political and social actors in Serbia.

Following the compromise reached, the resolution has also been supported by the liberals from the Renew Europe political group, who had previously submitted their own proposal. The European Parliament will therefore vote on a single agreed text in Strasbourg on Thursday, according to Večernji list. The original proposal, initiated by HDZ MEP Karlo Ressler and supported by all Croatian MEPs, was backed by four political groups: the EPP (People’s Party), the Social Democrats, the Conservatives and the Greens.

the five changes

In the final proposal, the formulation about Milošević’s Greater Serbian aggression against Croatia is retained, but the tribute to the victims is expanded to include the victims of other wars during the violent breakup of Yugoslavia. The text also includes the 2010 visit by the then Serbian President Boris Tadić to Ovčara, when, accompanied by the then Croatian President Ivo Josipović, he paid tribute to the victims and apologised for the crimes committed. The importance of reconciliation and clarifying the fate of the missing is also emphasised. The third change stresses that the families of missing persons of all nationalities are still waiting for information about the fate of their loved ones. The fourth change concerns the part of the resolution dealing with responsibility for fomenting ethnic tensions and hostilities through ultra-nationalist rhetoric and the idea of Greater Serbia. Instead of the previous formulation about Milošević and members of the Serbian political and social establishment, influential individuals from Serbian analytical, political and intellectual circles are now mentioned alongside Milošević.

The final change is terminological. Instead of “Territorial Defence of Serbia,” the resolution will refer to the Serbian Territorial Defence.

the alternative proposal is now also supported by non-governmental organisations

The agreement was preceded by disagreements over the content of the resolution. Representatives of Serbian students publicly opposed the proposal of the Croatian MEPs, while seven human rights organisations from the former Yugoslavia supported the alternative text submitted on behalf of the liberals by Austrian MEP Helmut Brandstätter. Among these organisations are the Croatian Documenta and the Serbian Humanitarian Law Centre. Their joint statement was also published by Serbian human rights activist Nataša Kandić. The organisations called for the resolution to also mention Serbian civilians killed or missing in Vukovar before the start of the siege of the city. They advocated equal criteria towards all countries in the region in confronting the wartime past and individual responsibility for war crimes. Unlike the proposal of the Croatian MEPs, the alternative proposal did not mention concentration camps in Serbia.

what are the demands of serbia?

The proposal of the Croatian MEPs calls on Serbia to open wartime archives, provide information on the locations of mass graves, cooperate in the prosecution of war crimes and adopt a law on missing persons. The aim of the initiative is to make the suffering of Vukovar part of the common European historical memory and to emphasise the importance of establishing responsibility for war crimes and clarifying the fate of the missing. If adopted, it will be the first resolution of the European Parliament specifically dedicated to the suffering of Vukovar. The resolution is not legally binding, which means that its adoption will not in itself introduce new conditions for Serbia’s potential membership of the European Union.

World.title: Australia sanctions two alleged Iranian agents over antisemitic attacks
World.content:
SYDNEY: Australia on Friday placed counterterrorism financing sanctions on two people it said orchestrated antisemitic arson attacks in Sydney and Melbourne on behalf of Iran.

Zohair Hassib and Kazem Hamad used a “complex chain of proxies” to attack a kosher restaurant in Sydney and the Adass Israel Synagogue in Melbourne in 2024, Foreign Minister Penny Wong said in a statement.

In August 2025, Australia ordered Iran’s ambassador to leave the country, the first expulsion of its kind since World War Two. It also suspended operations at its Tehran embassy and listed the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a terrorist organization.

Wong said the new counterterrorism financing sanctions would restrict the individuals’ access to funds and disrupt their ability to recruit, plan and conduct attacks.

World.title: Costa Rica bars entry to UN rapporteur over ‘links to terrorist acts’
World.content:
SAN JOSE: Costa Rica’s government said Thursday it had denied entry to UN rapporteur Francesca Albanese, who has accused Israel of genocide, because she was the subject of an “international alert over links to terrorist acts.”

Albanese, the UN special rapporteur on the Palestinian territories, arrived Thursday at the airport serving the capital San Jose to receive an honorary degree from the University of Costa Rica, a public university.

Albanese “is the subject of an international alert over links to terrorist acts,” Omer Badilla, director general of Costa Rica’s immigration authority, which falls under the interior ministry, said in a video posted on social media.

“I hope this clears up any doubts and makes clear the threat this woman poses to national security,” he added.

The rector’s office at the institution, the country’s most important and prestigious university, said in a statement that immigration authorities were “blocking” Albanese’s entry and asked the government to explain the decision.

The government of Costa Rican President Laura Fernandez is a close ally of US President Donald Trump and has pursued closer trade ties with Israel since she took office in May.

Last December, Albanese criticized a free trade agreement between Costa Rica and Israel and called for its ratification to be put on hold, prompting a rebuke from the government, which accused her of interfering in domestic affairs.

‘Face consequences’

The United States, Israel’s main ally, imposed sanctions on Albanese after she criticized Washington’s policy on Gaza.

“You see the face of empire the day you touch a nerve or cross its boundaries,” Albanese wrote from the airport.

The university said it was awarding the honorary doctorate, which it grants annually to a prominent figure, in recognition of her “solid academic background, experience, publications and work exposing wrongdoing.”

The Italian independent expert has faced harsh criticism from Israel and some of its allies over her longstanding accusations that Israel has committed genocide and other war crimes against Palestinians in Gaza and the occupied West Bank.

Israel’s ambassador to the United Nations, Danny Danon, welcomed Costa Rica’s decision.

“Those who exploit their UN mandate to spread vile propaganda, legitimize terrorist organizations, desecrate the memory of the six million Jews murdered in the Holocaust, and relentlessly vilify the US and Israel should face consequences,” Danon wrote.

The war in Gaza — which began following a Hamas attack inside Israel on October 7, 2023 — has killed more than 73,000 Palestinians, according to Gaza’s health ministry, which is controlled by Hamas. Many of the Palestinians killed in Gaza are women and children.

The October 7 Hamas attack killed 1,221 people, according to an AFP tally based on official Israeli figures.

Albanese was appointed by the UN Human Rights Council in 2022 and like other independent experts, does not speak on behalf of the United Nations.

World.title: Seoul repatriates six North Koreans found on drifting fishing boat
World.content:
SEOUL: South Korea repatriated six North Koreans on Friday after they were found drifting in international waters on a fishing boat earlier this month, Seoul’s unification ministry said.

The announcement came following heightened tensions along the heavily fortified border, after a recent mine blast that injured three South Korean soldiers in the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ).

The boat, initially carrying seven North Koreans, was found drifting in international waters off South Korea’s Ulleungdo island on November 3 and towed by the military and coast guard.

Authorities decided to repatriate six on humanitarian grounds after confirming their wishes through a series of inquiries involving government agencies and the United Nations Command, according to authorities.

One of the North Koreans expressed a wish to stay and will remain in the South, according to the ministry.

The fishing boat carrying the six North Koreans on Friday crossed the Northern Limit Line (NLL), the de facto maritime border, in the East Sea — also known as the Sea of Japan — under its own power at 8:33 KST (2333 GMT), the ministry said.

It then joined a North Korean vessel waiting north of the boundary and continued northwards, according to Seoul’s Yonhap news agency.

The UNC is believed to have notified Pyongyang of the repatriation plan in advance, as it did last year, according to Yonhap.

The presence of a North Korean vessel suggests Pyongyang received the notification, although no response from the North has been reported, Yonhap added.

Under Seoul’s constitution, all North Koreans are considered citizens of the Republic of Korea, as the South is officially known, and those who reach its territory and seek to defect are generally allowed to stay.

North Korea is known to brutally retaliate against defectors and their families.

Seoul carried out a similar repatriation last year, returning two North Korean vessels and all their occupants in accordance with their wishes after they were rescued in separate incidents in March and May.

World.title: Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia’s Jazan refinery kills Nepali worker
World.content:
RIYADH: A Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia’s Jazan refinery on Thursday killed a Nepali worker and injured several others.

The Kingdom’s Energy Ministry said the facility was hit by a “hostile aerial projectile,” which sparked a fire and led to the suspension of some operations.

The Coalition to Restore Legitimacy in Yemen said it had destroyed a ballistic missile launch platform in Yemen’s Hodeidah port, which was used in the attack.

The refinery is located in south-west Saudi Arabia, on the Red Sea coast, and can process up to 400,000 barrels of crude oil per day.

The workers injured in the attack are of different nationalities and are being given the necessary medical care, the ministry said. It expressed sincere condolences to the family of the deceased.

Emergency and technical teams set to work immediately after the attack to complete a damage assessment and safety checks, the statement added.

The coalition initially announced an attack had taken place on Thursday afternoon, warning the Houthis that targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure would be met with a firm military response.

The Iran-backed Houthis, who are fighting against Yemen’s internationally recognized government, control Hodeidah port on the Yemeni west coast.

The attack comes the same day that two Italian workers were killed in an attack on a facility in Kuwait, which was blamed on Iran.

The Houthis also attacked Jazan port on Wednesday, causing minor damage and no casualties, the coalition said.

The militia attempted strikes the same day on Jeddah Islamic Port and the Kingdom’s western region.

On Tuesday, a Houthi attack on a tower in Riyadh’s King Abdullah Financial District injured 11 people, according to Saudi Civil Defense.

The attacks come amid an escalating Houthi campaign targeting Saudi airports, oil facilities and other infrastructure.

World.title: Arab states, regional bodies condemn Daesh attack in Syria’s Hasakah
World.content:
RIYADH/DAMASCUS: Arab governments and regional organizations have rallied behind Syria following a Daesh-linked attack on an Interior Ministry facility in Hasakah that killed two security personnel and wounded five others, amid concerns over the militant group’s ability to exploit security vulnerabilities during the country’s fragile postwar transition.

Saudi Arabia was among the countries condemning Wednesday’s assault, with the Kingdom expressing solidarity with the Syrian government and people as they work to preserve the country’s security and stability, the Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA) reported.

In a statement, the Saudi Foreign Ministry strongly condemned the attack and reiterated the Kingdom’s rejection of violence, terrorism and extremism in all forms. Riyadh also extended condolences to the families of those killed.

Jordan joined the condemnation, expressing full support for the Syrian government and people and reaffirming its commitment to Syria’s security, stability, sovereignty and territorial integrity.

Bahrain, Egypt, the UAE, Qatar and Yemen also issued statements denouncing the attack, rejecting terrorism and extremism and expressing solidarity with Syria as it confronts security challenges.

Regional organizations also voiced support. The Arab League, the Organization of Islamic Cooperation and the Arab Parliament condemned the assault and reaffirmed their backing for Syria’s efforts to combat terrorism, safeguard its sovereignty and maintain security.

The Arab Parliament called for stronger Arab and international cooperation to confront terrorist organizations, cut off their sources of support and counter extremist ideologies.

Coordinated assault on security facility

The attack targeted an Interior Ministry facility in the Al-Mushairifah neighborhood, west of Hasakah city, on Wednesday evening.

Hasakah Internal Security Commander Brig. Gen. Marwan Al-Ali said four Daesh militants on motorcycles carried out the assault. One attacker detonated explosives at the facility’s entrance, triggering clashes with security personnel.

Security forces killed two of the assailants during the confrontation, while the other two detonated explosive belts, authorities said.

Preliminary investigations indicated that the attackers belonged to a Daesh cell operating in the region.

Security challenges in northeast Syria

Although the casualty toll was relatively limited compared with some of the deadliest attacks during Syria’s years of conflict, the assault raised concerns because of its potential strategic implications.

The attack comes as the government of President Ahmed Al-Sharaa seeks to consolidate authority across the country and integrate various security structures after years of conflict.

Northeastern Syria, particularly Hasakah province, remains one of the most sensitive areas in that process. Any successful attack against state institutions there carries significance beyond its immediate casualties.

The province is also home to detention facilities and camps holding thousands of Daesh fighters and their family members. Security disruptions could create opportunities for prison breaks, recruitment and the reactivation of dormant extremist networks.

The assault also appeared to depart from the low-level guerrilla tactics and isolated shootings frequently employed by Daesh cells in recent months. The coordinated deployment of multiple attackers, suicide tactics and a direct assault on a government security compound suggested a greater degree of planning and operational confidence.

The incident also challenges Syria’s efforts to establish itself as a stable environment for reconstruction, economic recovery and deeper regional engagement.

Security experts say such attacks, even when quickly contained, are intended to undermine public confidence in state institutions and raise doubts about the durability of recent security gains.

Daesh lost its last territorial stronghold in Syria in 2019, but remnants of the organization continue to operate through clandestine cells, particularly in the country’s north and east.

World.title: Deadlocked final result in New Zealand’s election leaves a new centrist party the decider
World.content:
WELLINGTON, New Zealand: The final vote count in New Zealand’s election published Friday showed neither the right-wing incumbents nor the left-wing opposition bloc won enough seats in Parliament to form a majority government, leaving the prospect of lengthy and fraught negotiations to break the deadlock.

The election on Nov. 7 was the tightest vote in years, and the conservative bloc finished the night with a wafer-thin majority. But after counting of 400,000 so-called special votes, including those cast by New Zealanders living abroad, the Electoral Commission said Friday that the main center-right party National, led by Prime Minister Christopher Luxon, had lost two seats.

That left the right-wing parties with a collective 65 seats in a 130-seat Parliament, with 66 needed for a majority government. The left-wing opposition, led by the Labour party’s Chris Hipkins, won 58 seats, up by one from election night.

The figures leave a new entrant to parliament, the Opportunity party — a centrist group that won seven seats, as the deciders of what the shape of the next government will be. While their seven seats wouldn’t apparently be enough to propel the left to power, Luxon and his right-wing government partners face lengthy negotiations with Opportunity to form a governing deal.

Opportunity, led by 38-year-old business consultant and political newcomer Qiulae Wong, is unaligned with either bloc and Wong has said she could work with either side to form a government. Wong’s pledges of evidence-based centrism and an end to partisan bickering appeared to have appealed to voters, who delivered a stinging rebuke with the result to the major parties, National and Labour, which have long dominated New Zealand politics.

Meet Qiulae ‘Q’ Wong. Leader of the new look Opportunity party! Q has spent her career fighting for better ways to do business. Now she's fighting for a better way to do politics. Meet Q at https://t.co/3xwpydAriL https://t.co/FpdUxXkgOS — The Opportunity Party (@top_nz) November 17, 2025

The final count showed more support for minor parties on the ideological flanks than before. A total of 2.8 million votes were cast.

Among the right-wing parties that have traditionally supported National, libertarian ACT won 13 seats and populist NZ First won 12. Among Labour’s support parties, the left-leaning Greens won 17 seats — up one from election night — and Te Pati Māori, an Indigenous rights group, won five.

New Zealanders cast two votes in elections, one for their preferred political party and another for their choice of local representative. The country has only one house of parliament, and no states, which means that central government has ultimate sway over the country’s direction.

Both Labour and National secured less than 30 percent of the preferred party vote, considered a punishing result for both. At the final count, National won 28.35 percent and Labour 29.88 percent.

National, however, secured more seats in Parliament because more of its candidates won local races. Now Luxon and his party face a grueling negotiation period as they attempt to form a four-way government including Wong’s lawmakers.

Luxon vehemently ruled out working with Opportunity before the election. The new party’s five so-called “bottom line” policies include stronger measures on climate change and an end to bottom-trawling fisheries — both in direct opposition to the stances of NZ First and ACT.

If a government can’t be formed, New Zealand could face a fresh vote. Negotiations hadn’t started before Friday’s final result because the close finish on election night prompted party leaders to wait for the confirmed totals.

World.title: Trump urges Putin to end ‘military aggression’ in Europe
World.content:
WEST PALM BEACH: US President Donald Trump said Thursday he had asked Vladimir Putin to “pull back all military aggression” against Europe, in a fresh shift in tone toward the Russian leader he called his friend just last week.

Trump said he had made the request to Putin when they met in China last week, adding that he thought it would help lead to a deal to end Moscow’s grinding war in Ukraine.

Trump’s comments come a day after he hosted NATO chief Mark Rutte in Florida, after which the two leaders issued a joint statement calling on Russia not to expand the Ukraine war.

“During my conversations in China with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, I spent a lot of time talking about the fact that I would like to see President Putin pull back all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe,” Trump said on his Truth Social network.

Trump said he had done so “in the hopes that a Deal can be made between Russia and Ukraine, and made quickly.”

“I really believe this is a strong possibility,” he added.

The statement did not specify which territories Trump meant — and did not specifically include Ukraine, which Russia invaded in February 2022, kicking off the largest war in Europe since World War II.

European nations have been increasingly concerned by what they regard as Russian provocations, including three Russian cruise missiles landing in NATO-member Poland last week.

In their joint statement on Wednesday, Trump and Rutte said they “discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war.”

In a notable contrast with Trump’s recent criticisms of Ukraine for striking targets deep inside Russia, the US leader made no call for Kyiv to show similar restraint.

Speaking to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida on Thursday, Trump said he was unsure if Putin would be coming to the G20 summit next month in Miami, but “but if he wanted to come, he certainly can.”

‘Deadlock’

Trump’s tone appeared markedly different to when Trump met Putin in the Chinese city of Shenzhen last week, both face-to-face and together with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Trump warmly greeted Putin and called him his “friend” at the summit, renewing concerns in Kyiv and European capitals that he was once again pivoting toward the Russian leader.

Asked Thursday about the apparent firmer tone this week, he said: “I don’t know if I was tougher. I mean, I think I’m the one that gave them the anti-tank busters, right?”

Trump often cites his approval of Javelin missile sales to Ukraine during his first term as saving the country from Russia’s initial assault.

The US envoys on the Ukraine war, Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner and business friend Steve Witkoff, have been accused of a similar willingness to take Moscow’s side.

In an interview with the German MD Meets Podcast on Wednesday, Kushner said that Putin had “showed restraint” because he had “agreed not to use nuclear weapons.”

Kushner also described the Russian leader, whom he has met several times, as a “grandmaster of politics” — while calling the Ukraine conflict “a proxy war where Europe is funding and arming Ukraine against Russia.”

But he acknowledged that the issue of territory in eastern Ukraine claimed by Moscow remained a sticking point with Putin.

“What Steve and I have deciphered from having many, many hours with President Putin and from the Russian team, is that you know the territorial issue is right now a little bit of a deadlock,” he said.

And he warned against any downward spiral in the Ukraine war, saying “it won’t take a lot of miscalculation for this thing to escalate massively.”

World.title: Saudi Arabia records world’s highest growth in inbound tourists since 2019, says minister
World.content:
RIYADH: Saudi Arabia recorded the world’s highest growth in inbound tourist arrivals between 2019 and the end of 2025, Tourism Minister Ahmed Al-Khateeb said, citing reports by UN Tourism, as the Kingdom presses ahead with plans to attract 150 million visitors annually by 2030.

The Saudi Press Agency (SPA) reported on Wednesday that Al-Khateeb made the remarks during a panel discussion on investment opportunities in promising sectors at the Budget 2027 Forum.

He said tourism was among the world’s largest job-creating industries, accounting for about 10 percent of the global workforce.

Saudi Arabia’s tourism sector has sustained strong growth since the launch of the National Tourism Strategy in 2019. The Kingdom achieved its target of attracting 100 million tourists in 2024, six years ahead of the original 2030 deadline, Al-Khateeb said.

He attributed the progress to the economic diversification drive under Saudi Vision 2030, which has expanded investment in tourism, culture, sports and entertainment.

The minister said the clarity of Vision 2030 and the targets set by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman had helped accelerate implementation and advance the sector’s objectives.

Saudi Tourism Minister Ahmed Al-Khateeb speaks during a panel discussion on investment opportunities at the Budget 2027 Forum in Riyadh on Wednesday. (SPA photo)

Reforms attract investment

Al-Khateeb said the development of tourism had required extensive legislative and regulatory reforms, including investments in human capital, new financing channels, easier business procedures and measures to improve the Kingdom’s investment competitiveness.

The introduction of electronic tourist visas and streamlined application procedures had also helped attract visitors, he said. The Tourism Law, announced in 2023, further strengthened the regulatory framework and provided greater clarity for investors.

The Tourism Development Fund has supported more than 300 major projects and over 1,000 small and medium-sized enterprises by offering long-term financing at low cost, Al-Khateeb said, highlighting the importance of smaller businesses to the travel and tourism industry.

The reforms have helped attract more than 50 new international hotel brands to Saudi Arabia, while several global hotel groups have doubled their room capacity and expanded investments in Makkah, Madinah, Riyadh and the Red Sea region.

Tourism investments have generated 250,000 jobs and added more than 200,000 hotel rooms over the past five years, he said.

More than 500 hotels, offering over 100,000 rooms, have opened across the Kingdom in recent years. Another 200,000 rooms are under development for completion by 2030.

Al-Khateeb said an improved regulatory environment, investment incentives, lower costs for investors and Saudi Arabia’s strategic geographical location had helped turn investment opportunities into operational projects.

Infrastructure and major projects

The minister stressed that continued infrastructure development was essential to achieving the target of attracting 150 million tourists by 2030.

He cited the expansion of existing airports and construction of new facilities, including King Salman International Airport and Aseer Airport, as well as the operation of Red Sea International Airport.

The launch of Riyadh Air, the expansion of Saudia’s fleet and the Air Connectivity Program, which encourages international carriers to introduce direct flights to Saudi tourist destinations, were also strengthening the sector, he said.

Improvements to transport networks and the expansion of accommodation, shopping, restaurant and cafe options have further enhanced the competitiveness of Saudi cities as international tourist destinations.

The completion of major developments in Diriyah, Qiddiya and the Red Sea region is expected to broaden the range and quality of accommodation and tourism services.

These projects will also support preparations for Saudi Arabia’s hosting of Expo 2030 and the FIFA World Cup 2034, Al-Khateeb said.

Saudi Tourism Minister Ahmed Al-Khateeb (C) speaks during a panel discussion on investment opportunities at the Budget 2027 Forum in Riyadh on Wednesday. (SPA photo)

Spending and employment rise

Developing qualified national talent remains another priority, with tourism among the sectors that best showcase a country’s culture and history, the minister said.

He pointed to initiatives to raise minimum wages, establish clearer career paths and expand professional training. Programs aim to train around 100,000 young Saudi men and women annually, while providing opportunities to study at leading international specialized institutes.

Tourism spending in the Kingdom rose from approximately SR120 billion in 2019 to SR304 billion in 2025, with a target of SR550 billion by 2030, Al-Khateeb said.

The number of tourists also increased from about 90 million in 2019 to 123 million last year, while employment in the sector grew from 750,000 to one million.

He said these gains reflected the progress made under Vision 2030 and supported the Kingdom’s ambition to establish tourism as a major contributor to economic growth and diversification.

World.title: Thousands of protesters rally in Iraqi Kurdistan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Thousands of protesters rallied in different cities in Iraqi Kurdistan on Thursday to oppose federal government moves to take over oil operations and international border crossings in the semi-autonomous region.

Crowds gathered near Erbil’s citadel and across Duhok waving Kurdish flags and banners rejecting federal interference in the region’s administrative and financial rights. Rival Kurdish political factions also united in opposition to the federal directives.

The protests took place after Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi decided on Tuesday to transfer control of all border crossings in Iraqi Kurdistan to Iraq’s federal Border Ports Authority.

The directives require the federal Oil Ministry’s approval for crude exports and transfer the management of oil fields in four provinces—Kirkuk, Diyala, Salah al-Din, and Nineveh—from Kurdish authorities to the federal government.

On Wednesday, Iraq’s Federal Supreme Court backed the measures, ruling that Baghdad has the constitutional authority to deploy federal forces along all international borders, including within the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

Al-Zaidi stated that the actions reflect Iraq’s independent national will and are part of a broader campaign to combat corruption and stop oil smuggling networks.

The move follows a separate federal crackdown the previous week against alleged oil smuggling by an Iran-aligned militia south of Baghdad.

The Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) described the decisions as unconstitutional, arguing they represent an attempt to return Iraq to a centralized regime and criticizing the use of threats. The KRG’s prime minister, Masrour Barzani, stated that the measures are completely unacceptable.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate drops to 1,690 dinars in Iraq’s parallel market
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar slightly dropped on Thursday in both Baghdad, the Iraqi capital, and Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate declined in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,690 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,694.5 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,695 Iraqi dinars and 1,685 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also declined, fluctuating between 1,694.5 and 1,693.5 Iraqi dinars.

US dollar exchange rates rose noticeably in the Baghdad and Erbil markets on October 7, following the cabinet’s decision to revalue the official rate of the local currency, causing turbulence and instability in the parallel market.

Iraq officially depreciated its national currency, with the baseline dropping from about 1,300 Iraqi dinars to 1,500 dinars per US dollar.

The Iraqi cabinet approved the structural adjustment, which marks a 14.5 percent decline compared to the previous official framework that had been in place since early 2023.

Following the announcement, parallel market rates in Baghdad and Erbil soared, with exchange shops reporting market gains of more than 1,700 Iraqi dinars per US dollar.

World.title: Iraq discusses raising overseas bank card usage caps for travelers
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Parliamentary Finance Committee discussed raising the spending limits on bank cards used by Iraqi citizens traveling abroad during a meeting with Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) officials in late November.

The committee hosted directors from key CBI departments—including investments, banking supervision, non-bank financial institution supervision, issuance, and treasuries—to review monetary policy plans.

Alongside raising overseas card usage caps for travelers, the discussions addressed expanding financial inclusion, increasing the number of exchange companies, ensuring adequate cash liquidity, and boosting state treasury revenues.

In mid-October, the CBI directed financial institutions to implement a monthly transaction limit for bank cards and to establish a maximum daily limit for purchases made at points of sale outside of Iraq.

The CBI underlined that the decision relates to point-of-sale transactions made outside Iraq, notably those that require the actual presence of the card with the merchant.

Holders of bank cards may use them for point-of-sale purchases outside Iraq up to a daily limit equivalent to $3,333 (or five million Iraqi dinars), provided that total monthly transactions do not exceed five million Iraqi dinars.

The measure replaces the previous daily limit of $333.3 (equivalent to 500,000 Iraqi dinars) specifically for this type of transaction.

World.title: Iraqi judiciary sentences 11 people to 15 years in prison for oil smuggling
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Central Criminal Court sentenced on Thursday 11 people to 15 years in prison each for smuggling oil to neighboring countries.

Reports indicate that the defendants were part of an armed group led by fugitive Ahmed Abdul-Wahid Shaya. This group smuggled oil from Basra province using boats and forged documents.

The court has ordered the confiscation of the boats involved, while authorities are actively pursuing the remaining members of the group.

The unanimous verdict credits the defendants’ time served in pre-trial detention between September 19 and November 25, 2026.

The ruling is subject to appeal and mandatory review by the Court of Cassation. Once finalized, harmed parties retain the right to seek financial compensation in civil courts.

The sentences coincide with an intensified federal campaign against fuel theft and illicit exports. Earlier on Thursday, Iraqi authorities began closing all unofficial border crossings with neighboring countries following a directive from Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi.

Earlier in November, al-Zaidi removed several senior officials and security personnel in connection with smuggling investigations at the state-run North Oil Company and pipeline-tapping networks in Babil province.

World.title: 10 French nationals sentenced to prison for joining ISIS
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Karkh Criminal Court sentenced on Thursday 10 French nationals to prison for joining the terrorist group ISIS.

Eight received life imprisonment, which equates to a 20-year term under Iraqi law, and two received 15-year prison sentences.

The 10 men are part of 47 French nationals transferred to Iraq from northeast Syria in 2025, whose trials in Baghdad began in September 2026 under Iraq’s anti-terrorism law.

Thursday’s rulings bring the number of convicted French citizens in this group to 26, as 16 had previously been convicted in earlier hearings. Another 10 defendants had their verdicts postponed to a later date.

Representatives from the French Embassy in Iraq and defense lawyers attended the hearings.

Iraq prosecutes ISIS members under its anti-terrorism statutes regardless of whether their alleged activities took place in Iraq or neighboring Syria.

France has repatriated hundreds of family members of jihadists while largely declining to bring back adult men accused of involvement.

Rights groups have criticized the pace and due process of Iraq’s terrorism trials, while Iraqi authorities continue processing thousands of detainees transferred from Syria.

World.title: Iraq in discussions with Apple to activate Apple Pay
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi authorities are holding official talks with Apple to introduce Apple Pay in Iraq as part of a broader push to expand digital payment services.

Head of the Communications and Media Commission (CMC) Baligh Abu-Kallal said in early November that Iraq is negotiating with Apple over launching Apple Pay, privacy policies, and gaming sector cooperation.

In August, Iraq accredited Apple as a verified digital platform, covering services such as the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Podcasts, Apple Arcade, and Apple Ads under local regulations.

Abu-Kallal stated that launching Apple Pay depends on completing technical, legal, and financial procedures, local news outlet Shafaq News reported.

Iraqi banks have also signaled interest in digital wallet expansion amid wider banking modernization and digital payment reforms.

Earlier in July, an Iraqi government source mentioned that the committee in charge of activating Apple Pay services met with Apple’s regional managers to make the service accessible in Iraq.

The initiative is part of the Iraqi government’s efforts to enhance the electronic payment infrastructure and boost the adoption of modern technology, thereby fostering financial inclusion and advancing digital transformation.

Iraq aims to make Apple Pay available to users, in accordance with the government’s strategy to expand the online payment sector and support the transition to a digital economy.

World.title: Iraq expands digital services for Iraqi Airways
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Transport has expanded digital services for Iraqi Airways to facilitate passenger travel and reduce airport congestion.

Travelers can complete check-in procedures and issue their electronic boarding passes online before arriving at the airport.

Passengers can also choose their preferred seats in advance during booking or check-in.

Users can now electronically change their flight schedules and destinations without visiting a sales office.

The airline enhanced its electronic reservation and online payment systems for both domestic and international flights.

A new pricing structure lets passengers select different fare classes with varying baggage allowances and modification terms.

Passengers can use these services through the Iraqi Airways official website or via the mobile app.

The step is part of the company’s strategy to grow its digital capabilities, improve passenger experience, and stay up with the latest standards in the aviation industry.

The service generally opens for check-in between 48 and 24 hours before the scheduled flight departure and closes up to two hours prior to takeoff.

World.title: Iraq’s judiciary rules that Baghdad can deploy forces along all borders
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Federal Supreme Court ruled on Wednesday that the federal government in Baghdad can deploy troops to secure all international borders, including those in Iraqi Kurdistan.

The decision backs Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s push to assert central control over border crossings and oil fields across the country.

The court affirmed federal jurisdiction over international borders, customs oversight, and the auditing of oil and gas fields, while allowing shared management with regional authorities and provinces.

Ali al-Zaidi ordered federal takeovers of Kurdish-run border crossings and disputed oil fields following an oil smuggling investigation. The Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) described the moves as constitutional violations and military threats, calling instead for dialogue.

The crackdown, which also targets militias with ties to Iran, is seen by analysts as part of Zaidi’s larger effort to consolidate power. As a result, the Supreme Judicial Council has called on all parties to uphold the 2005 constitution.

A day earlier, al-Zaidi ordered federal authorities to take control of all border crossings in Iraqi Kurdistan and directed the Oil Ministry to manage oilfields under Kurdish security control in Diyala, Kirkuk, Salah al-Din, and Nineveh provinces.

The KRG was instructed to approve crude oil and petroleum product exports only through the federal Oil Ministry.

The directives followed an investigation into smuggling at the state-run North Oil Company and a wider campaign against illicit oil networks—including alleged smuggling in Jurf al-Sakhar linked to the Iran-backed Kataib Hezbollah group, which denied the accusation.

World.title: Jagan Mohan Reddy's YSRCP to back NDA's Delimitation Bill push in Parliament but with a rider
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Jagan Mohan Reddy-led YSRCP will support the NDA government's push for the Delimitation Bill in Parliament, provided it ensures regional balance, party sources told news agency ANI on Friday.

The support from the YSRCP will strengthen the NDA's numbers as the Centre prepares to bring the legislation back to Parliament during a special sitting.

Party sources told ANI that the YSRCP would support the Bill if it is introduced with provisions "ensuring regional balance."

The development assumes significance as the government seeks to secure the two-thirds majority required to pass the legislation, which failed to clear the floor test during the Budget Session.



Apart from the YSRCP, Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP) has also adopted a softer stance on the proposed legislation. Party leader

recently indicated that there might be "something good" about the Bill, adding that the party would not "blindly" oppose it simply because it was in the opposition.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The Union government's latest move to reconvene Parliament has added to the political focus on the proposed legislation. Ending the suspense, the government on Thursday moved to convene a short session of Parliament from November 30, during which it is expected to bring back the delimitation Bills to implement the women's reservation law from 2029.





The proposed exercise is expected to increase the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha to 850 from 550, with the government seeking to ensure that the expansion addresses concerns over regional representation.

Parliamentary affairs minister

announced on Thursday that the government had requested Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla to reconvene the Lower House on November 30 and Rajya Sabha chairman C P Radhakrishnan to call a sitting of the Upper House on December 2 to transact "essential government business".

World.title: Watch: Putin hails PM Modi's 'Make in India' vision, praises 16-year-old Indian AI entrepreneur
World.content:
Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday praised the work of 16-year-old Indian entrepreneur Raul John Aju, linking his efforts in artificial intelligence (AI) to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's '

' initiative during the AI Journey 2026 conference.

Putin and Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev interacted with young innovators at the conference, where Aju, the founder and chief technology officer (CTO) of AI Realm Technologies, was among those introduced to the Russian president.

During the interaction, Putin acknowledged Aju's work and highlighted how young innovators developing their own technological solutions contribute to the objectives of the 'Make in India' initiative.



"Ultimately your work helps realize PM Modi's "Make in India" call right? Because it helps young people find their own solutions and implement these solutions," Putin told Aju.

Putin's remarks come days after the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) criticised India's manufacturing and export policies, including the 'Make in India' initiative, in a report examining structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors.





Putin's praise comes days after US trade body targets 'Make in India'

In its Section 301 investigation report into India's acts, policies and practices relating to structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors, the USTR alleged that India had adopted several measures that contributed to excess manufacturing capacity and production while failing to effectively address the resulting global concerns.

"India engages in a range of acts, policies, and practices that create, maintain, or contribute to the structural excess capacity and production evident in the indicia described above. Key among these are the umbrella efforts of Make in India, PLI, Atmanirbhar Bharat (Self-Reliant India), and IBEF, with a particular emphasis on efforts related to or under these efforts in the steel, solar, health, and ICT sectors," the USTR said.

The report specifically identified the government's flagship 'Make in India' programme, Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative and India Brand Equity Foundation (IBEF) among the measures it said contributed to structural excess capacity.

Who is Raul John Aju, the 'AI Kid of India'?

Popularly known online as 'Raul the Rockstar' and often described as the 'AI Kid of India', Aju is a teenager from Kerala who has pursued artificial intelligence despite coming from a Commerce background rather than a conventional engineering or computer science pathway.

According to information shared on his LinkedIn profile, his interest in technology began when he was around nine years old. What started as independent learning and experimentation gradually developed into AI projects, educational initiatives and a growing online community.

Aju studied Plus Two Commerce at North Edappally GHSS while simultaneously working on artificial intelligence projects. His LinkedIn profile identifies him as the founder and CTO of AIRealm Technologies, where he develops AI products and practical technology solutions.

Projects associated with him include ThinkCraft, RESQ AI and MeBot, among other AI-based tools. He is also associated with ThinkCraft Academy, an AI learning platform that introduces students and professionals to emerging technologies.
